sentences.text: Bí a bá ránni níṣẹ́ ẹrú, à fi jẹ́ tọmọ.
sentences.en: If one is sent on an errand like a slave, one carries it out like a freeborn.

sentences.text: Bí a bá rí èké, à ṣebí èèyàn rere ni; à sọ̀rọ̀ ságbọ̀n a jò.
sentences.en: When one sees a devious person one mistakes him for a good person; one talks into a basket and it leaks.

sentences.text: Bí a bá rí òwúrọ̀, alẹ́ ńkọ́?
sentences.en: Although one has seen the morning, what about night time?

sentences.text: Bí a bá sọ̀rọ̀ tán, ẹrín là ń rín; bí a bá yó tán orun ní ń kunni.
sentences.en: When one is done discussing a matter one laughs, when one is satiated sleep claims one.

sentences.text: Bí a bá ṣe ohun ńlá, à fi èpè gba ara ẹni là.
sentences.en: If one has committed a great offense, one frees oneself by swearing (innocence).

sentences.text: Bí a bá ta ará ilé ẹni lọ́pọ̀, a kì í rí i rà lọ́wọ̀n-ọ́n mọ́.
sentences.en: If one sells a member of one's household cheap, one will not be able to buy him back at a great value.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá gbọ́n ju àparò oko ẹni lọ, a kì í pa á.
sentences.en: If one is not more clever than the partridge on one's farm, one cannot kill it.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá rádànán, à fòòbẹ̀ ṣẹbọ.
sentences.en: If one cannot find a bat, one sacrifices a housebat.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá torí iṣu jẹ epo, à torí epo jẹṣu.
sentences.en: If one does not eat oil because of yams, one will eat yams because of oil.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bímọ rí, a kò ha rọ́mọ lẹ́yìn adìẹ?
sentences.en: If one has never had a child, has one not seen chicks flocking after chickens?

sentences.text: Bí a kò ránni sọ́jà, ọjà kì í ránni sílé.
sentences.en: If one does not send a message to the market, the market does not send a message to one at home.

sentences.text: Bí a kò ṣe ọdẹ rí, a kò lè mọ ẹsẹ̀ẹ kò-lọ-ibẹ̀un.
sentences.en: If one has never hunted, one would not know the tracks of “it-did-not-go-that-way.”

sentences.text: Bí alẹ́ bá lẹ́, à fi ọmọ ayò fún ayò.
sentences.en: When night comes, one gives the ayò seeds to ayò.

sentences.text: Bí alẹ́ bá lẹ́, bọnnọ-bọ́nnọ́ a rẹ̀wẹ̀sì.
sentences.en: When night falls, bọnnọ-bọ́nnọ́ goes limp.

sentences.text: Bí alẹ́ kò lẹ́, òòbẹ̀ kì í fò.
sentences.en: If night does not fall, the house bat does not fly.

sentences.text: Bí apá ò ká àràbà, apá lè ká egbò ìdíi rẹ̀.
sentences.en: If the arms cannot encompass the silk-cotton tree, they may encompass its root.

sentences.text: Bí àrùn búburú bá wọ̀lú, oògùn búburú la fi ń wò ó.
sentences.en: If a terrible epidemic descends on a town, it is confronted with a terrible medicine.

sentences.text: Bí eégún ó bàá wọlẹ̀, orò ni ń ṣe.
sentences.en: If a masquerader wishes to disappear into the ground, it cries “Orò!”

sentences.text: Bí eré bí eré, àlàbọrùn-ún dẹ̀wù.
sentences.en: Like play, like play, the makeshift cape became a dress.

sentences.text: Bí ẹlẹ́rẹ̀kẹ́ régérégé bá ro ẹjọ́ọ tirẹ̀ tán, kó rántí pé ẹlẹ́rẹ̀kẹ́ mẹ́kí á rí rò.
sentences.en: After the person with smooth cheeks has stated his or her case, he or she should remember that the person with blemished cheeks will have something to say.

sentences.text: Bí igí bá wó lu igi, tòkè là ń kọ́ gbé.
sentences.en: If trees fall atop one another, one removes the topmost one first.

sentences.text: Bí ikún bá jẹ, bí ikún bá mu, ikún a wo oòrùn alẹ́.
sentences.en: When the squirrel has eaten, when the squirrel has drunk, the squirrel looks at the setting sun.

sentences.text: Bí ilẹ̀ẹ́ bá laná, ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ á fò gun igi.
sentences.en: If the earth catches fire, the toad will hop on a tree.

sentences.text: Bí ilú bá dá sí méjì, tọba ọ̀rún là ń ṣe.
sentences.en: If the town is split into two, one does the will of the heavenly king.

sentences.text: Bí iṣẹ́ kò pẹ́ ẹni, a kì í pẹ́ iṣẹ́.
sentences.en: If a task does not delay one, one does not drag it out.

sentences.text: Bí kò bá tíì rẹ ìjà, a kì í là á.
sentences.en: If a fight is not yet spent, one does not intervene to end it.

sentences.text: Bí kò bá tíì rẹ ìjà, a kì í là á.
sentences.en: If a fight is not yet spent, one does not intervene to end it.

sentences.text: Bí kò bá tíì rẹ ìjà, a kì í là á.
sentences.en: If a fight is not yet spent, one does not intervene to end it.

sentences.text: Bí nǹkan bá tán nílẹ̀, ọmọ ẹbọ a bọ́ síjó, àwọn tó wà níbẹ̀ a múra àti lọ.
sentences.en: At the conclusion of a ceremony the acolyte commences to dance, and the onlookers prepare to make their exit.

sentences.text: Bí o bá já n ó so ọ́, kókó yó wà láàárín-in rẹ̀.
sentences.en: “If you break I will retie you”; there will be a knot in it.

sentences.text: Bí o kò gbọ́ Ègùn, o kò gbọ́ wọ̀yọ̀-wọ̀yọ̀?
sentences.en: If you do not understand Ègùn, do you not recognize signs that someone is speaking?

sentences.text: Bí obìnrin ò bá gbé ilé tó méjì, kì í mọ èyí tó sàn.
sentences.en: If a woman has not lived in at least two homes, she never knows which is better.

sentences.text: Bí ojú bá rí ọ̀rọ̀, a wò ó fín.
sentences.en: When the eyes come upon a matter, they must look hard and well.

sentences.text: Bí ojú ọmọdé ò tó ìtàn, a bá àwígbọ́.
sentences.en: If a youth's eyes do not witness a story, they should be good for hearsay.

sentences.text: Bí olósùn-ún bá lọ osùn, araa rẹ̀ ní ń fi dánwò.
sentences.en: When the camwood powder seller grinds the powder, she tests it on her own body.

sentences.text: Bí òrìṣá bá mú ẹlẹ́yìn, kí abuké máa múra sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: If the gods take a person with a protruding back, the humpback should make ready.

sentences.text: Bí òwe bí òwe nIfá ń sọ̀rọ̀.
sentences.en: Like proverbs, like proverbs are the pronouncements of Ifá.

sentences.text: Bí ọ̀bùn ò mọ èrè, a mọ ojú owó.
sentences.en: If the filthy person does not know profit, he should know his capital.

sentences.text: Bí ọkùnrín réjò, tóbìrín pa á, à ní kéjò má ṣáà lọ.
sentences.en: If a man sees a snake, and a woman kills it, what matters is that the snake does not escape.

sentences.text: Bí Ọlọ́run-ún bá ti fọ̀tá ẹni hanni, kò lè pani mọ́.
sentences.en: Once God has revealed one's enemy to one, he can no longer kill one.

sentences.text: Bí ọlọgbọ́n bá ń fi wèrè se iṣu, ọ̀mọ̀ràn a máa fi gègé yàn án.
sentences.en: If a wise person is cooking yams in an insane way, a knowing person picks them with stakes.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọ́ bá jágbọ́n-ọn kíké, ìyáa rẹ̀ a jágbọ́n-ọn rírẹ̀ ẹ́.
sentences.en: If a child learns the trick of crying, the mother learns the trick of consoling him or her.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọ́ bá jágbọ́n-ọn kíkú, ìyá ẹ̀ a jágbọ́n-ọn sísín.
sentences.en: If a child learns the trick of dying, his mother should learn the trick of burying.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọ́ bá yó, a fikùn han baba.
sentences.en: When a child is full, he shows his stomach to his father.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọdé bá dúpẹ́ ore àná, a rí tòní gbà.
sentences.en: If a child expresses gratitude for yesterday's favor, he will receive today's.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọdé bá ń bẹ́ igi, àgbàlagbà a máa wo ibi tí yóò wó sí.
sentences.en: If a youth is felling a tree, an elder will be considering where it will fall.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọdé bá mọ ayò, ẹyọ la ó fi pa á.
sentences.en: If a child is an adept ayò player, one defeats him with single seeds.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọdé bá ṣubú a wo iwájú; bí àgbá bá ṣubú a wo ẹ̀yìn.
sentences.en: When a youth falls he looks ahead; when an elder falls he looks behind.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọdé kọ iyán àná, ìtàn la ó pa fún un.
sentences.en: If a child refuses yesterday's pounded yams, it is stories one treats the child to.

sentences.text: Bí ọ̀rán bá pẹ́ nílẹ̀, gbígbọ́n ní ń gbọ́n.
sentences.en: If a problem remains long enough, it becomes clever.

sentences.text: Bí ọwọ́ ò bá ṣeé ṣán, à ká a lérí.
sentences.en: If the arms cannot be swung, one carries them on one's head.

sentences.text: Bí túlàsí bá di méjì, ọ̀kan là ń mú.
sentences.en: When emergencies number two, one concentrates on one.

sentences.text: “Bùn mi níṣu kan” kì í ṣáájú “Ẹkú oko òo.”
sentences.en: “Give me one yam” does not precede “Greetings to you on the farm.”

sentences.text: Dà-á-sílẹ̀-ká-tun-pín, ogún ijọ́un, a ò pín in re.
sentences.en: The recent throw-it-all-on-the-floor-that-we-may-redistribute-it inheritance was not well distributed the first time around.

sentences.text: Dídì ní ń mú abẹ mú.
sentences.en: It is wrapping that makes a knife sharp.

sentences.text: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ nimú ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ẹ́ fi ń wọgbà.
sentences.en: It is bit by bit that the nose of the pig enters the fence.

sentences.text: DÍfá-dÍfá ò fIfá ṣeré.
sentences.en: The diviner does not take Ifá lightly.

sentences.text: Dùgbẹ̀-dùgbẹ̀ kì í fi ẹyin rẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: The egg-bearing spider never leaves its eggs behind.

sentences.text: Dúró o kíkà; bí o ò dúró kíkà, ìkà a ba tìrẹ jẹ́.
sentences.en: Stop and say hello to the wicked; if you do not say hello to the wicked, the wicked will find problems for you.

sentences.text: Ebi ń pa mí ọlọ́ṣẹ ń kiri; ìgbà tí n ò wẹnú n ó ṣe wẹ̀de?
sentences.en: I am hungry and the soap seller hawks her wares; when I have not washed my inside, how can I wash my outside?

sentences.text: Ebi ò pàJèṣà ó lóun ò jẹ̀kọ Ọ̀yọ́; ebí pa ọmọ Obòkun ó jẹ ori.
sentences.en: The Ijeṣa person is not hungry and he rejects corn-loaf prepared by an Ọ̀yọ́ person; when hunger gripped the son of Obokun (an apellation for Ijeṣa people) he ate ori(the Ọ̀yọ́ name for corn-loaf.)

sentences.text: Ebi ò pÀmọ̀le ó ní òun ò jẹ àáyá; ebí pa Súlè ó jọ̀bọ.
sentences.en: The muslim is not hungry and he vows he will not eat a red Colobus monkey; hunger gripped Suleiman and he ate a monkey.

sentences.text: Eégún Ẹ̀gbá, Ẹ̀gbá ní ń fọ̀.
sentences.en: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.

sentences.text: Ejòó rí ihò tó há ó kó wọ̀ ọ́; ìyáa rẹ̀ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ àti fà á yọ?
sentences.en: A snake sees a tight hole and crawls into it; has its mother hands to pull it out?

sentences.text: Elékuru kì í kiri lóko.
sentences.en: The seller of steamed ground beans does not hawk her wares on a farm.

sentences.text: Èló là ń ra adìẹ òkókó, tí à ń gba ọmọọ rẹ̀ sìn?
sentences.en: How much does a hen cost that one would contract to raise chicks for the owner?

sentences.text: Èmi-ò-níí-fẹ́-obìnrin-tẹ́nìkan-ńfẹ́, olúwarẹ̀ ò níí fẹ́ obìnrin ni.
sentences.en: I-will-court-no-woman-being-courted-by-another-man will court no woman at all.

sentences.text: Èmi-ò-níí-ṣu-imí-le-imí, olúwarẹ̀ ó rìn jìnnà ààtàn.
sentences.en: I-will-not-defecate-on-existing-excrement will walk a good distance into the bush.

sentences.text: Èpè la fi ń wo èpè sàn.
sentences.en: Curses are the antidote for curses.

sentences.text: Epo ló ṣeé jẹṣu; àkàsọ̀ ló ṣeé gun àká; obìnrín dùn-ún bá sùn ju ọkùnrin lọ.
sentences.en: It is palm oil that goes best with yams; it is a ladder that is best for climbing granaries; a woman is more pleasant to make love to than a man.

sentences.text: Epo lojú ọbẹ̀.
sentences.en: Palm-oil is the countenance of stew.

sentences.text: Eré là ń fọmọ ayò ṣe.
sentences.en: All one does with ayò seeds is play.

sentences.text: Èrò kì í mọ ibùsọ̀ kọ́rùn ó wọ̀ ọ́.
sentences.en: A wayfarer does not know the location of the rest stop and yet have his neck crushed from the weight of a heavy load.

sentences.text: Ète lẹ̀gbọ́n; ìmọ̀ràn làbúrò; bí-a-ó-ti-ṣe lẹ̀kẹta wọn.
sentences.en: Intention is the eldest, contemplation is the next, and plan of action is the third.

sentences.text: Ètò lòfin kìn-ín-ní lóde ọ̀run.
sentences.en: Order is the first law in heaven.

sentences.text: Ewúrẹ́ ò ṣeé fiṣu ṣọ́.
sentences.en: A goat is not a wise choice as the guard over yams.

sentences.text: Èyí tó yẹ ará iwájú, èrò ẹ̀yìn fiyè sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: To what turned out favorably for those going ahead, you coming behind, pay close attention.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀bẹ̀ là ń bẹ òṣìkà pé kó tún ìlúu rẹ̀ ṣe.
sentences.en: One can only remonstrate with a wicked person to urge him or her to improve his or her town.

sentences.text: Ẹbọ díẹ̀, oògùn díẹ̀, ní ń gba aláìkú là.
sentences.en: A little sacrifice, a little medicine, is what keeps the one who does not die alive.

sentences.text: Ẹbọ ẹnìkan là ń fi ẹnìkan rú.
sentences.en: It is a sacrifice on behalf of only one person that demands only one person as offering.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀fẹ̀ẹ́ dẹ̀fẹ̀ iyán; a paláwẹ́ ẹ̀kọ baálé ilé ní ẹ̀ ń pèun bí?
sentences.en: The teasing involves pounded yams; the corn-loaf is unwrapped, and the father of the household asks, “Did someone call me?”

sentences.text: Ẹ̀fẹ̀ẹ́ dẹ̀fẹ̀ iyán; ò báà gbémi lulẹ̀ n ó bá ọ jẹun.
sentences.en: The teasing involves pounded yam; even if you throw me on the ground I will eat with you.

sentences.text: Ẹgbẹ́ ẹni kì í wọ́n láyé ká wá a lọ sọ́run.
sentences.en: One does not upon failing to find suitable company in this world go looking in heaven.

sentences.text: Ẹjọ́ a-fẹ́ni-lóbìnrin là ń wí; a kì í wíjọ́ a-fẹ́ni-lọ́mọ.
sentences.en: One may complain about a person who courts one's wife, but one does not complain about a person who courts one's daughter.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀ẹ̀kan lejò ń yánni.
sentences.en: One gets bitten by a snake only once.

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́nuú tóó rí sá.
sentences.en: An overly loquacious person is someone to flee from.

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ẹ́ ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́n-ọn hùn, ọjọ́ náà ni ọ̀rọ̀ ò ti nìun lára mọ́.
sentences.en: The pig says since the day it learned to reply to every statement with a grunt it has not got into any trouble.

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́jọ́ ṣa èyí tó wù ú wí.
sentences.en: The person with complaints selects the most pressing ones to press.

sentences.text: Ẹni a óò gbé òkúu rẹ̀ sin, a kì í sọ pé ó ń rùn pani.
sentences.en: One does not complain that a corpse one will have to bury stinks.

sentences.text: Ẹni a pé kó wáá wo kọ̀bì: ó ní kí nìyí kọ́bi-kọ̀bi?
sentences.en: The person invited to take a look at the palace stateroom: he exclaims, “What a maze of apartments!”

sentences.text: Ẹni à ń wò kì í wòran.
sentences.en: The person people have gathered to watch should not himself or herself be a spectator.

sentences.text: Ẹni àìgbọ́n pa ló pọ̀; ẹni ọgbọ́n pa ò tó nǹkan.
sentences.en: People killed by folly are innumerable; people killed by wisdom are few.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá ríkun nímú ọlọ́jà ní ń fọn ọ́n.
sentences.en: Whoever sees mucus in the nose of the king is the one who cleans it.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá tó ẹnií gbà là ń ké pè.
sentences.en: One appeals only to those capable of helping one.

sentences.text: Ẹní du araa rẹ̀ lóyè Apènà: kó tó jẹ ẹran ọ̀fẹ́, ó dọ̀run.
sentences.en: Whoever deprives himself of the title of Apena will wait until he dies before tasting free meat.

sentences.text: Ẹní gbọ́n juni lọ ní ń tẹni nÍfá.
sentences.en: It is someone wiser than one who consults the oracle for one.

sentences.text: Ẹní léku méjì á pòfo.
sentences.en: Whoever chases after two rats will catch neither.

sentences.text: Ẹní máa ké ìbòsí á pa baba rẹ̀ jẹ.
sentences.en: Whoever wishes to raise an alarm will have to murder his father.

sentences.text: Ẹní rúbọ òrìṣà gbọ́dọ̀ rú ti èèyàn kí ẹbọọ́ tó gbà.
sentences.en: Whoever offers a sacrifice to a deity must also offer a sacrifice to humans in order for the sacrifice to be efficacious.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a bá fi oríi rẹ̀ fọ́ àgbọn ò níí jẹ níbẹ̀.
sentences.en: The person on whose head a coconut is broken will not share in eating it.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a bá ń bá nájà là ń wò, a kì í wo ariwo ọjà.
sentences.en: One pays attention to the person with whom one is bargaining, not to the commotion of the market place.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a wífún kó gbọ́; ẹni tí kò gbọ́, taraa rẹ̀ ni yó dà.
sentences.en: Let the person one advises heed one; the heedless person places himself at risk.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ẹ̀gún gún lẹ́sẹ̀ ní ń ṣe lákáǹláká tẹ̀lé alábẹ́rẹ́.
sentences.en: It is the person with a thorn in his foot who limps to the person with a needle.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí kò gbọ́n lààwẹ̀ ń gbò.
sentences.en: Only the unwise hungers while fasting.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí kò mọ iṣẹ́ẹ́ jẹ́ ní ń pààrà lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
sentences.en: It is a person who does not know how to carry out instructions that is forced to repeat his or her efforts.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí kò mọ ọba ní ń fọba ṣeré.
sentences.en: Only a person who does not know the king trifles with the king.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó lè jà ni yóò kúnlẹ̀ kalẹ́.
sentences.en: It is the incorrigible fighter who has to remain on his or her knees until nightfall.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí yó bọ Ògún, yó ra ọjàa tirẹ̀ lọ́tọ̀.
sentences.en: The person who will worship Ògun will keep his or her market purchases separate from those of others.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí yó fò yó bẹ̀rẹ̀.
sentences.en: The person who will leap must first crouch.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí yó mu ẹ̀kọ fòrò, yó bàá ọmọ ẹlẹ́kọ ṣeré.
sentences.en: Whoever wishes to eat steaming corn pap will play with the child of the seller.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí yó mu ẹ̀kọ ọ̀fẹ́ yó bàá ọmọ ẹlẹ́kọ ṣeré.
sentences.en: The person who wishes to eat free corn pap will play with the seller's child.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí yó yááni lówó, tí kò níí sinni, ohùn ẹnuu rẹ̀ la ti ń mọ̀.
sentences.en: The person who will lend one money and will not keep pestering one for repayment: one can tell from the tone of his or her voice.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá da omi síwájú á tẹ ilẹ̀ tútù.
sentences.en: Whoever throws water ahead will step on cool earth.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá fi ojù àná wòkú, ẹbọra a bọ́ ọ láṣọ.
sentences.en: Whoever looks at the dead with yesterday's eyes will be stripped naked by the spirits.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá máa jẹ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ a jẹ èyí tó lẹ́yin.
sentences.en: If one must eat a toad one should eat one with eggs.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá máa lu òṣùgbó a lu ńlá; kékeré ẹgbẹ̀fà, ńlá ẹgbẹ̀fà.
sentences.en: Whoever will smite a secret-cult priest had better smite an important one; for a lowly one twelve hundred cowries in fines, and for an important one twelve hundred cowries.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá máa mú ọ̀bọ a ṣe bí ọ̀bọ.
sentences.en: Whoever wishes to catch a monkey must act like a monkey.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá mọ ìdí ọ̀ràn tẹ́lẹ̀ ní ń bu àbùjá èké.
sentences.en: It is a person who has prior knowledge of the facts of a matter that can foil a devious person's attempts to skirt them.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá ní igbàá lò, bí igbàá bá já, kó dúró so ó.
sentences.en: If one must use a tree-climbing rope and it breaks, one must pause to repair it.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá pẹ́ lórí imí, eṣinṣin kéṣinṣin yóò bá a níbẹ̀.
sentences.en: Whoever prolongs his or her defecating will be visited by a host of flies.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá rántí Efuji, kó má fi ore ṣe ẹṣin.
sentences.en: Whoever remembers Efuji should show no kindness to any horse.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá rántí ọjọ́ ní ń ṣe ọmọ òkú pẹ̀lẹ́; ta ní jẹ́ ṣe ọmọ eégún lóore?
sentences.en: Those who gratefully remember past favors extend compassion to the survivors of the deceased; who would rather show compassion to the child of a masquerader?

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá sọ pé ẹsẹ̀ eégún ń hàn ní ń wá abẹ́rẹ́ lọ.
sentences.en: Whoever announces that the legs of the masquerader are showing is the one who goes in search of a needle.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó bá yá ìwọ̀fà ẹgbàá, tòun tirẹ̀ ní ń lọ ata kúnná.
sentences.en: Whoever hires a pawn for only sixpence will join the pawn in grinding pepper.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó dùbúlẹ̀ ṣe oògùn ìjàkadì tán.
sentences.en: The person who remains prone has perfected the charm for wrestling.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó fi irun dúdú ṣeré, yó fi funfun sin ẹniẹlẹ́ni.
sentences.en: Whoever plays around with his or her black hair will serve others with his or her white hair.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó fi owóo rẹ̀ ra ẹṣin, kò níí jẹ́ kó ṣe àrìnjẹ́.
sentences.en: Whoever paid his or her own money for a horse will not let it be sacrificed for a good-luck charm.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó gbajúmọ̀ tí kò mọ èèyàn-án kí, òun òbúrẹ́wà ẹgbẹ́ra.
sentences.en: The dandy who does not know how to extend greetings to people is no different from a boor.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó máa tẹ́ òkú ọ̀pọ̀lọ́, yóò ní ilé ògbóni tirẹ̀ lọ́tọ̀.
sentences.en: Whoever wishes to lay a dead toad in state will have to build his own cult shrine separately.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó máa yáni lẹ́wù, ti ọrùn-un rẹ̀ là ń wò.
sentences.en: If a person offers to lend one a dress, one should consider what he or she has on.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó mi kùkùté, araa rẹ̀ ní ń mì.
sentences.en: The person who shakes a tree stump shakes himself.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó mọ ẹtu ní ń kì í ní “òbèjé, ẹlẹ́sẹ̀ ọwọ̀.”
sentences.en: It is someone who knows the duiker intimately who can recite its praise, “spindle-legged duiker.”

sentences.text: Ẹni tó ń ṣápẹ́ fún wèrè jó, òun àti wèrè ọ̀kan-ùn.
sentences.en: The person who claps for a mad person to dance to is no different from the mad person.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó pa kẹ́tẹ́kẹ́tẹ́ yó ru káyá ẹrù.
sentences.en: The person who kills the donkey will carry a heavy burden.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó ránṣẹ́ sí oròó bẹ̀wẹ̀ fún àìsùn.
sentences.en: Whoever sends for Orò is contracting for sleeplessness.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó re Ìbàdàn tí kò dé ilé Olúyọ̀lé, oko igi ló lọ.
sentences.en: Whoever goes to Ibadan and does not visit Oluyọle's house merely went wood gathering.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó rúbọ tí kò gba èèwọ̀, bí ẹni tó fi owó ẹbọ ṣòfò ni.
sentences.en: The person who makes a sacrifice but does not follow the prescribed taboos is just like someone who throws away the money for the sacrifice.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó sọ ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ lékùrọ́, oúnjẹ ló fún un.
sentences.en: The person who throws palm-nuts at a pig gives food to it.

sentences.text: Ẹni tó torí òtútù fi ọmọrí odó yáná ò gbọdọ̀ retí a-ti-jẹyán.
sentences.en: Whoever because of cold weather uses the pestle as kindling to warm him/herself must not expect to eat pounded yams.

sentences.text: Ẹnu àìmẹ́nu, ètè àìmétè, ní ń mú ọ̀ràn bá ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́.
sentences.en: A mouth that will not stay shut, lips that will not stay closed, are what bring trouble to the cheeks.

sentences.text: Ẹnu ehoro ò gba ìjánu.
sentences.en: A rabbit's mouth does not accept a leash.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ ni ilé ẹ̀rín.
sentences.en: The cheeks are the home of laughter.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀rù bíbà ní ń múni pe àjẹ́ ní ará ire.
sentences.en: It is fear that makes one call witches the good people.

sentences.text: Ẹrùu hòo kì í wọni lọ́rùn.
sentences.en: “I agree” is not a load that causes one's neck to shrink.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀sín alátọ̀sí ò sí lọ́wọ́ òkóbó.
sentences.en: The ridiculing of the person with gonorrhea does not belong with the eunuch.

sentences.text: Ẹyẹ igbó kì í mọ fífò ọ̀dàn.
sentences.en: The bird of the forest does not know how to fly in the grassland.

sentences.text: Ẹyẹ ń wá àtifò, wọ́ ń sọ òkò sí i.
sentences.en: A bird is preparing for flight, and people throw stones at it.

sentences.text: Fi ìjà fún Ọlọ́run jà, fọwọ́ lérán.
sentences.en: Leave the fighting to God, sit back and watch.

sentences.text: Fimí-pamọ́-kí-n-pa-ọ́ làrùn-ún jẹ́.
sentences.en: Hide-me-and-I-will-kill-you is the name a disease answers to.

sentences.text: “Gba ọmọ fún mi kí n rèdí”; bí ìdí ò bá ṣeé rè ká gbọ́mọ fọ́lọ́mọ.
sentences.en: “Hold my child for me so I may wiggle my buttocks”; if one cannot wiggle one's buttocks one should return the child to its mother.

sentences.text: Ibi tí a bá ń gbé la ti ń gbàwìn; à-rà-àì-san ni ò sunwọ̀n.
sentences.en: One's home is a legitimate place to buy things on credit; what is bad is avoiding payment.

sentences.text: Ibi tí a gbé epo sí a kì í sọ òkò síbẹ̀.
sentences.en: One does not throw rocks at the place where one has one's palm-oil stored.

sentences.text: Ibi tí a ti gùn, ibẹ̀ la ti ń rọ̀.
sentences.en: Where one began one's climb, there one effects one's descent.

sentences.text: Ibi tí à ń gbé là ń ṣe; bí a bá dé ìlú adẹ́tẹ̀ à di ìkúùkù.
sentences.en: One should live according to the customs and fashions of the place one finds oneself in; if one lands in the city of lepers, one should make a fist, i.e., conceal one's fingers.

sentences.text: Ibi tí o máa sùn lo tẹ́ ọmọ sí.
sentences.en: It is precisely where you will eventually have to sleep that you have laid down your child to sleep.

sentences.text: Ibi tí òjòó ti ń pa igún bọ̀ jìnnà; ta ní rán igún níṣẹ́?
sentences.en: The vulture has endured the drenching rain from a great distance, but who sent the vulture on an errand?

sentences.text: Ibi tí òjòó bá ọjọ́ ní ń pa á sí.
sentences.en: Wherever the rain catches up with the day, there it drenches it.

sentences.text: Ibi tí oníyọ̀nmọ̀ntìí ṣubú sí, ibẹ̀ ló ti tà á tán.
sentences.en: Wherever the yọ̀nmọ̀ntì (food made from benniseed) seller falls, there she has sold all her wares.

sentences.text: Ibi tí oyín gbé ń hó, tí àdó ń hó, ìfun ò dákẹ́ lásán.
sentences.en: As the bees hum and the small calabash containing charms hums, the intestine does not keep silent.

sentences.text: Ìdí òwò ni òwòó gbé tà.
sentences.en: It is at its home base that a company or trade prospers.

sentences.text: Ìgbà ara là ń búra.
sentences.en: One swears when it is time to swear.

sentences.text: Ìgbà tí a bá dóko làárọ̀ ẹni.
sentences.en: The time of one's arrival on the farm is one's dawn.

sentences.text: Ìgbà tí a bá rẹni lòwúrọ̀ ẹni.
sentences.en: Whenever one first sees a person, that is that person's morning.

sentences.text: Igbá tó gbédè là ń pè lóṣùwọ̀n.
sentences.en: It is a calabash that understands one's language that one describes as a measure.

sentences.text: Ìgbín ìbá má mọ̀ ọ́n jẹ̀ ìbá ti kú síjù.
sentences.en: Had the snail been careless in its foraging it would have died in the bush.

sentences.text: Ìgbín ìbá má mọ̀ ọ́n jẹ̀ kò tó okòó.
sentences.en: Had the snail been careless in its foraging it would not “have grown large enough to” be worth twenty cowries.

sentences.text: Ìgbín kì í pilẹ̀ aró, àfè ìmòjò kì í pilẹ̀ àràn.
sentences.en: The snail never embarks on a dyeing trade, and the spotted grass-mouse never digs for àràn.

sentences.text: Igbó lẹranko ń gbé.
sentences.en: The forest is the home for animals to live in.

sentences.text: Ìgbọ̀nwọ́ ti kékeré yọké.
sentences.en: The elbow develops a hump right from its youth.

sentences.text: Ijó ní ń bọ́ṣọ, ìjà ní ń bọ́ ẹ̀wù.
sentences.en: It is dance that strips one of one's cloth; it is a fight that takes off one's shirt.

sentences.text: Ikúdú pa ẹṣin à ń yọ̀; ó ń bọ̀ wá pa ọmọ èèyàn.
sentences.en: An abandoned well kills a horse and we rejoice; it will in time kill a human being.

sentences.text: Ilé ajá là ń wá ìwo lọ?
sentences.en: Is a dog's house the place to go in search of horns?

sentences.text: Ilé olóuńjẹ là ń dẹ̀bìtì àyà sí.
sentences.en: It is in the home of a person who has food that one sets one's chest like a trap.

sentences.text: Ilẹ̀ nìjòkò ń jókòó de ìdí.
sentences.en: It is on the ground that the stool sits to await the buttocks.

sentences.text: Ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ àmúyọ, a kì í sin kádìí tán.
sentences.en: One does not string decorative beads all around one's waist.

sentences.text: Ìloro là ń wọ̀ ká tó wọlé.
sentences.en: One enters the porch first before one enters the house.

sentences.text: Iná èsìsì kì í jóni lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
sentences.en: The fire of the stinging tragia plant does not burn a person twice.

sentences.text: Iná kúkú ni yó ba ọbẹ̀ ará oko jẹ́.
sentences.en: It is too much fire that will ruin the stew of a bushman.

sentences.text: Iná tó ń lérí omi á kù sọnù.
sentences.en: The fire that challenges water will die off.

sentences.text: Ìpàṣán tí a fi na ìyálé ń bẹ láàjà fún ìyàwó.
sentences.en: The whip used on the senior wife is resting on the rafters waiting for the new wife.

sentences.text: Ìròrẹ́ ò leè jà ó múlé ti agbọ́n.
sentences.en: Ìròrẹ́ cannot fight, so it makes its home close to the wasp's.

sentences.text: Isó inú ẹ̀kú, à-mú-mọ́ra.
sentences.en: The fart within a masquerader's shroud “is” something to be endured.

sentences.text: Ìṣeǹṣe ewúrẹ́, kágùntàn fiyè síi.
sentences.en: The fate that has befallen the goat, the sheep should bear in mind.

sentences.text: Iṣú ta iṣu ò ta, ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ń wúṣu lébè.
sentences.en: Whether the yams are large or not, it is one by one that one extracts them from the heap.

sentences.text: Ìtórò tó so lóko tí kò fẹ̀yìntì, afẹ́fẹ́ oko ní ń tú u.
sentences.en: The lemon plant that grows in the bush and does not support itself against something will be uprooted by the forest breeze.

sentences.text: Ìwòo ọlọgbọ́n ò jọ ti aṣiwèrè.
sentences.en: The way a wise person looks at things is different from the way an imbecile does.

sentences.text: Ìyàwó mi ò sunwọ̀; nítorí ọmọ ni mo ṣe fẹ́ ẹ; ẹni mélòó la ó wìí fún tán?
sentences.en: “My wife is not good looking, but I married her for the sake of children”; to how many people will one give that explanation?

sentences.text: Ìyàwó sọ ọ̀rọ̀ kan tán: ó ní ìyálé òun a-bẹnu-funfun-bí-ègbodò.
sentences.en: The junior wife has said what will be her last; she said the senior wife's mouth is as white as the new yam.

sentences.text: Ìyàwó ṣe ọ̀ràn kan tán; ọkọ ẹ̀ ẹ́ ṣe ọ̀ràn-an n kò-jẹ-mọ́.
sentences.en: The wife has done the unpardonable; her husband has adopted an I-will-not-eat-any-longer attitude.

sentences.text: “Já ilé ẹ̀ kí ń bá ẹ kọ́ ọ”; ìtẹ́ èèkàn kan ní ń fúnni.
sentences.en: “Unroof your house and I will help you re-roof it” usually gives one only one bundle of thatching grass.

sentences.text: Jùrù-fẹ̀fẹ̀ jùrù-fẹ̀fẹ̀, ewúrẹ́ wọ ilé àpọn jùrù-fẹ̀fẹ̀; kí làpọ́n rí jẹ tí yó kù sílẹ̀ féwúrẹ́?
sentences.en: Busily wagging tail, busily wagging tail, a goat enters a bachelor's house busily wagging its tail; what does a bachelor have to eat whose left-over the goat can have?

sentences.text: Kàkà kí ọmọdé pàgbà láyò, àgbà a fi ọgbọ́n àgbà gbé e.
sentences.en: Instead of permitting defeat by a child in a game, an elder should resort to elderly wiles.

sentences.text: Kì í jẹ́ kí etí ẹni di kì í jẹ kí inú ẹni dùn.
sentences.en: Whatever keeps one from being deaf to certain things keeps one from being happy.

sentences.text: Kí ni à ń wọ̀ nínúu ṣòkòtò mẹ́ta ọ̀ọ́dúnrún?
sentences.en: What is there to wear in a pair of trousers bought at three for three hundred cowries, or three a penny?

sentences.text: Kí ni fìlà yó ṣe lórí ògógó? Ata ni yó ṣi.
sentences.en: What would a cap be doing atop the ògógó mushroom? Pepper will remove it.

sentences.text: Kíkọ́ ni mímọ̀, òwe ìjàpá.
sentences.en: Learning is knowing, Àjàpà's proverb.

sentences.text: Kéré-kéré leku ń jawọ; díẹ̀-díẹ̀ leèrà ń bọ́ ìyẹ́.
sentences.en: Bit by bit the rat consumes the leather; gently gently the ant sloughs its skin.

sentences.text: Kò sí alámàlà tí ń sọ pé tòun ò yi; aládàlú nìkan ló sòótọ́.
sentences.en: There is no yam-flower meal seller who will advertise her ware as fluffy; the àdàlú seller alone speaks the truth.

sentences.text: Kò sí aláásáà tí ń ta ìgbokú; gbogbo wọn ní ń ta oyin.
sentences.en: There is no snuff seller who will advertise her ware as awful; they all say they are selling honey.

sentences.text: Kò sí ẹni tí kò mọ ọgbọ́n-ọn ká fẹran sẹ́nu ká wá a tì.
sentences.en: There is nobody who does not know the trick of putting meat in the mouth and making it disappear.

sentences.text: Kókó ló kọ́kọ́ dé orí, tàbí orí ló kọ́kọ́ dé kókó?
sentences.en: Was it the lump that first got to the head, or the head that first got to the lump?

sentences.text: Kóǹkólóyo: èyí tó ní tèmi.
sentences.en: A rather small thing: this is enough for me.

sentences.text: Kóró-kóró là ń dá Ifá adití.
sentences.en: Very loud is the way one consults Ifá for a deaf person.

sentences.text: Kùbẹ̀rẹ̀, ká roko ìpére. Ó ní èyí tí òún lọ òun òì bọ̀.
sentences.en: “Kubẹrẹ, let us go to the bush where small snails are picked.” He said the last such trip he went on, he has not returned from it.

sentences.text: Lójú òpè, bíi kọ́lọgbọ́n dàbí ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: As far as the dunce is concerned, the wise person should rather be shiftless.

sentences.text: “Máa jẹ́ ǹ ṣó” lọ̀yà fi ń ju ẹmọ́ lọ.
sentences.en: “Go on feeding” is what makes the cane rat fatter than the Tullberg's rat.

sentences.text: “Màá kó ẹrú, màá kó ẹrù” là ń bá lọ sógun; ọ̀nà lẹnìkẹta ń báni.
sentences.en: “I will capture slaves and I will capture loot” is what one has in mind on departure for a war; the third one comes upon one only along the way.

sentences.text: Màjèṣín dóbò àkọ́kọ́, ó sáré yọ okó síta, ó ní Olúwaá ṣeun.
sentences.en: The tender youth has sex for the first time ever, pulls out his penis prematurely, and says “God be praised!”

sentences.text: Mójú-kúrò nilé ayé gbà; gbogbo ọ̀rọ̀ kọ́ ló ṣéé bínú sí.
sentences.en: Judicious forbearance is the wise approach to the world; not every matter deserves to be angry at.

sentences.text: Ní ìlú tí a ò ti fẹ́ ẹyẹlé, adìẹ yóò ṣọ̀wọ́n níbẹ̀.
sentences.en: In a town that does not welcome pigeons, chickens will be very scarce there.

sentences.text: Ní inú Ifá ni Fá-túmọ̀-ọ́ wà.
sentences.en: It is within Ifá that one finds Fátúmọ̀.

sentences.text: “Níbo ló gbé wà?” nìyájú ẹkùn.
sentences.en: “Where is it?” is a great insult to the leopard.

sentences.text: Nígbà tí ọwọ́ ò tí ì gbọ́n lojú ń ṣepin.
sentences.en: It is when the hands have not learned wisdom that the eyes ooze matter.

sentences.text: Nítorí adití lòjò fi ń ṣú; nítorí afọ́jú ló ṣe ń kù.
sentences.en: It is for the benefit of deaf people that rain clouds gather; it is for the benefit of the blind that thunder rumbles.

sentences.text: Nítorí èèyàn la ṣe ń ní ọwọ́ ọ̀tún; òsì là bá lò.
sentences.en: It is on account of people that one has a right hand; one could do with only a left hand otherwise.

sentences.text: Nítoríi ká lè ríbi gbé e la ṣe ń ṣe ọyàn sódó.
sentences.en: It is so that one would have a means of lifting it that one carves breasts [handles] on the mortar.

sentences.text: Ó di kan-nu-rin kan-nu-rin, agogo Ògúntólú.
sentences.en: All one hears is noise without pattern, like that of Oguntolu's bell.

sentences.text: O fẹ́ joyè o ní o ò níí jà.
sentences.en: You aspire to taking a chieftaincy title and you say you will not get into a fight.

sentences.text: O fi awọ ẹkùn ṣẹbọ àìkú; ẹkùn ìbá má kùú ìwọ ìbá rawọ ẹ̀ ṣoògùn?
sentences.en: You use a leopard's skin as an ingredient for medicine to hold off death; had the leopard not died would you have had access to its hide for the medicine?

sentences.text: O kò lu òmìrán lóru, ò ń lù ú lọ́sàn-án.
sentences.en: You did not hit the giant at night time, but you hit him in daylight.

sentences.text: O kò wọ bàtà nínù ẹ̀gún ò ń sáré; o lágbára màlúù?
sentences.en: You have no shoes on on the thorny path and yet you are running; do you have a cow's “hoof” power?

sentences.text: O kò ì mú ẹrú, o ní Àdó ni ò ó tà á fún.
sentences.en: You have not captured a slave, but you are already saying you will sell him/her only to an Àdò person.

sentences.text: O ló o fẹ́ jọba o ní o ò nìí ṣÒgbóni, o ò níí pẹ́ lóyè.
sentences.en: You propose to become a king but you refuse to join the Ògbóni society; you will not last long on the throne.

sentences.text: Ò ń bẹ oníṣègùn, o ò bẹ asínwín; bí oníṣègùn-ún ṣe tí asínwín ò gbà ń kọ́?
sentences.en: You are pleading with the medicine man but not with the demented person; what if the medicine man produces the medicine and the demented person refuses it?

sentences.text: Ó ń ti ilé bọ̀ kò ra ẹ̀gbẹ; ó dé oko tán ó ní ẹ̀gbẹ ni oníkú ẹ̀kọ.
sentences.en: Leaving the home he did not purchase dried meat; after arriving on the farm he says dried meat is the indispensable thing to eat corn loaf with.

sentences.text: O rí etí adẹ́tẹ̀ o fi san okòó; kò nípọn tó ni, tàbí kò rẹ̀ dẹ̀dẹ̀ tọ́?
sentences.en: You see a leper's ears and you value it at twenty cowries; does it lack sufficient thickness or is it not red enough?

sentences.text: O rí ẹsẹ̀ẹ wèrè o ò bù ú ṣoògùn; níbo lo ti máa rí tọlọgbọ́n?
sentences.en: You see the footprint of an imbecile and you do not take soil from it to make a charm; where will you find the footprint of a wise person?

sentences.text: O sá fún ikú, o bọ́ sí àkọ̀ idà.
sentences.en: You run from death and seek refuge in a scabbard.

sentences.text: “Ó ṣe mí rí”; ògbó adìẹẹ́ rí àwòdì sá.
sentences.en: “I have experienced it before”; a grown chicken flees at the sight of a kite.

sentences.text: Ó ti ojú orun wá ó ń fọ ẹnà; ó ní “ẹ jẹ́ ká máa ji ní mẹ́mu-mẹ́mu.”
sentences.en: He woke up from sleep and spoke in scrambled language; he said, “Let us wake it in moos.”

sentences.text: O wà láyé, mo wà láàyè, ò ń bi mí bí ọ̀rún ṣe rí.
sentences.en: You are on earth “alive” and I am on earth, and yet you ask me what heaven is like.

sentences.text: Ó yẹ kí eégún mọ ẹni tó mú àgbò so.
sentences.en: It is proper that the masquerader know who tethered the ram.

sentences.text: Obìnrin ò gbé ibi tó máa rọ̀ ọ́ lọ́rùn.
sentences.en: A woman never remains where her well being rests.

sentences.text: Òbò ò ṣé ṣe àlejò.
sentences.en: The vagina is not a thing for showing hospitality.

sentences.text: Odídẹrẹ́ dawo, ìkó ìdí ẹ̀ẹ́ dọ̀gbẹ̀rì.
sentences.en: The parrot becomes fully initiated into the secrets, his tail feather becomes a non-initiate.

sentences.text: Òdú kì í ṣe àìmọ̀ olóko.
sentences.en: The òdú vegetable is not something the farmer does not know.

sentences.text: Ogún kì í pọ̀ ká pín fún aládùúgbò.
sentences.en: The inheritance is never so abundant that one shares it with neighbors.

sentences.text: Ogún ń bókòó? Òwe aṣiwèrè.
sentences.en: Twenty or a score? An imbecile's puzzle.

sentences.text: Ohun tí a bá pàdé ò jọ ohun tí a rí tẹ́lẹ̀.
sentences.en: That which one comes upon is nothing to compare to what one has always had.

sentences.text: Ohun tí a ò rí rí lèèwọ̀ ojú.
sentences.en: It is something one has never seen before that is taboo for the eyes.

sentences.text: Ohun tí a ṣe nílé àna ẹni, “Ojú ń tì mí” kúrò níbẹ̀.
sentences.en: What one does in the home of one's parents-in-law leaves no room for “I am bashful.”

sentences.text: Ohun tí kò jẹ́ káṣọ pé méjì ni ò jẹ́ kó dú.
sentences.en: The same thing that keeps one from having more than one item of clothing also keeps that one from blackening from dirt.

sentences.text: Ohun tí kò jẹ́ kí oko pọ̀ ni ò jẹ́ kó mọ́.
sentences.en: Whatever limits the size of a farm is the same thing that makes it overgrown with weeds.

sentences.text: Ohun tó fọ́ni lójú ló ń júwe ọ̀nà fúnni.
sentences.en: Whatever deprives one of one's sight is the same thing that shows one the way.

sentences.text: Ohun tó jọ oun la fi ń wé ohun; èpo ẹ̀pà ló jọ ìtẹ́ ẹ̀lírí.
sentences.en: It is what resembles a thing that one compares it with; peanut shells are most like the nest of the rodent ẹ̀lírí.

sentences.text: Ohun tó ní òun óò bẹ́ni lórí, bó bá ṣíni ní fìlà, ká dúpẹ́.
sentences.en: If a thing that vows to decapitate one only knocks off one's hat, one shounld be thankful.

sentences.text: Ohun tó ní òun óò ṣeni lẹ́rú, tó wá ṣeni níwọ̀fà, ká gbà á.
sentences.en: If whatever promised to make one a slave only makes one a pawn, one should accept one's fate.

sentences.text: Òjòwú ò lẹ́ran láyà.
sentences.en: The jealous woman lacks flesh on her chest.

sentences.text: Ojú àwo làwó fi ń gba ọbẹ̀.
sentences.en: It is on its face that a plate accepts soup.

sentences.text: Ojú kan làdá ń ní.
sentences.en: A cutlass has only one edge.

sentences.text: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká fi pọ́nlẹ̀.
sentences.en: One should not because of one's suffering try honing one's eyes on the ground.

sentences.text: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká mu ìṣápá; òùngbẹ kì í gbẹni ká mu ẹ̀jẹ̀.
sentences.en: One is never so desperate that one drinks red sorrel juice; one is never so thirsty that one drinks blood.

sentences.text: Ojú kì í ti àgbà lóru; jagun a lóṣòó góńgó.
sentences.en: An elderly person does not become embarrassed under cover of darkness; the stalwart squats nonchalantly.

sentences.text: Ojú kì í ti eégún kó má mọ̀nà ìgbàlẹ̀.
sentences.en: A masquerader is never so shamed that he cannot find his way to the secret grove.

sentences.text: Ojú tó rọ̀ nirorẹ́ ń sọ.
sentences.en: Pimples attack only faces that are delicate.

sentences.text: “Òkè ìhín ò jẹ́ ká rí tọ̀ún” ò ṣéé pa lówe nílé àna ẹni.
sentences.en: “The nearer hill kept one from seeing the farther one” is not a proverb one uses in one's parents-in-law's home.

sentences.text: Okó ilé kì í jọ obìnrin lójú, àfi bó bá dó tìta.
sentences.en: “The nearer hill kept one from seeing the farther one” is not a proverb one uses in one's parents-in-law's home.

sentences.text: Oko kì í jẹ́ ti baba àti tọmọ kó má nìí àlà.
sentences.en: Farms do not, by virtue of belonging to a father and his son, lack boundaries.

sentences.text: Oko mímọ́ ṣeé ro; ọ̀nà mímọ́ dùn-ún tọ̀; gbogbo ìyàwó dùn-ún gbàbálé; aṣọ ìgbàá ṣeé yọ.
sentences.en: A clean farm is a pleasure to weed; a clean-swept path is a pleasure to trod; all new wives are a pleasure to deflower; the new fashionable cloth of the season is a pleasure to wear.

sentences.text: Okotoroboó tùyẹ́ sílẹ̀ ọmọ titún ń gbe jó; ó ní ó rọ òun lọ́rùn lòún tu ú?
sentences.en: Okotorobo, a bird, casts away a feather, and a young chick picks it up to dance with it; the one who shed the feathers asks, would I have discarded it if it was not a nuisance.

sentences.text: Okotoroboó yé ẹyin sílẹ̀, àdàbà ń garùn wo ẹyin ẹlẹ́yin.
sentences.en: Okotorobo the bird lays an egg, and the turtle dove stretches its neck to inspect the egg that does not belong to it.

sentences.text: Òkú ẹran kì í ti ajá lójú.
sentences.en: A dog is never to squeamish to eat a carcase.

sentences.text: Olè tó gbé fèrè ọba ò róhun gbé.
sentences.en: The thief who stole the king's bugle could find nothing to steal.

sentences.text: Olé tó jí kàkàkí, níbo ni yó ti fọn ọ́n?
sentences.en: A thief who stole a bugle, where will he blow it?

sentences.text: Olóògùn ní ńṣe bí a-láigbọ́-mọ̀ràn; bí ogun ó bàá wọ̀lú ọlọgbọ́n là ńfọ̀rọ̀ lọ̀.
sentences.en: The medicine man behaves like a person impervious to wise counsel; if war threatens a town the person to consult for counsel is the sage.

sentences.text: Olóhun-ún dolè; “Gbà bù jẹ́” dolóhun.
sentences.en: The owner becomes a thief; “Take this and eat” becomes the owner.

sentences.text: Olóhun kì í rí ohun ẹ̀ kó pè é lórò.
sentences.en: The owner will not see what he owns and call it a fearful; abomination.

sentences.text: Olórìṣà tó da kiriyó: ọjọ́ tó gbọ́ dùrù orí ijó lẹsẹ̀ẹ́ kán sí.
sentences.en: The idol worshipper who became a Christian; the day he first heard the organ play he lost his legs dancing.

sentences.text: Olòṣì ọmọ ní ń fọwọ́ òṣì júwe ilée babaa ẹ̀.
sentences.en: It is a worthless child that points the way to his father's house with his left-hand fingers.

sentences.text: Olóúnjẹẹ́ tóó bá kú.
sentences.en: Someone who has food is worth dying with.

sentences.text: Olówe laláṣẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀.
sentences.en: A person who knows proverbs has the last word in a dispute.

sentences.text: Olówó pèlù o ò jó; ọjọ́ wo lo máa rówó pe tìẹ?
sentences.en: A rich person engages a dance band and you do not dance; when will you have the money to hire your own band?

sentences.text: Òmùgọ̀ èèyàn ní ń bóbìnrin mulẹ̀: ọjọ́ tóbìnrín bá mawo lawó bàjẹ́.
sentences.en: A rich person engages a dance band and you do not dance; when will you have the money to hire your own band?

sentences.text: Òmùgọ̀ ní ń gbé ígunnu; ọlọgbọ́n ní ń gbowó.
sentences.en: It is the fool that wears the Nupe masquerade; it is the wise person that collects the monetary gifts.

sentences.text: Onígi ní ń figi ẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀.
sentences.en: It is the firewood seller who sets a low price for his wares.

sentences.text: Onígbá ní ń pe igbá ẹ̀ ní àíkàrágbá káyé tó fi kólẹ̀.
sentences.en: It is the owner of the calabash who first called it a broken piece of gourd before the world used it for scooping dirt.

sentences.text: Onígbèsè tí ń pa àpatà ẹyẹ́lé.
sentences.en: Habitual debtor who butchers a pigeon for sale.

sentences.text: Onígẹ̀gẹ́ fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀; adámú fi sàárà san ẹgbẹ̀ta.
sentences.en: The goitered person sets a low price on beads; the person with a blocked nose repays six thousand cowries with alms.

sentences.text: Oníṣègùn tó sọ pé díẹ̀ ò tó òun, òfo ni yó fọwọ́ mú.
sentences.en: The medicine man who is dissatisfied with a modest payment will wind up with nothing.

sentences.text: Ooré pẹ́, aṣiwèrèé gbàgbé.
sentences.en: The favor is long past; the imbecile forgets.

sentences.text: Orí ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́ popo láwo; bí a wí fọ́mọ ẹni a gbọ́ràn.
sentences.en: The squirrel's head sits in a plate like a lump; if one counsels one's child it should listen.

sentences.text: Orí tí yó jẹ igún kì í gbọ́; bí wọ́n fun ládìẹ kò níí gbà.
sentences.en: The head that is destined to eat a vulture cannot be saved; if a chicken is offered to it it will refuse.

sentences.text: Orí tó kọ ẹrù, owó ní ńnáni.
sentences.en: A head that refuses “to carry” loads will cost its owner some money.

sentences.text: Orin tí ò ṣoroó dá kì í ṣòroó gbè; bí ó bá ní “héééé,” à ní “háááá.”
sentences.en: A song that is not difficult to lead is not difficult to follow; if the leader sings “haaaay,” one responds “haaaah.”

sentences.text: Orín yí, ìlùú yí padà.
sentences.en: The song changes, and the drumming changes to suit.

sentences.text: Òrìṣà tó ní tÒgún kì í ṣe ọ̀nà ò ní rí nńkan jẹ lásìkò tó fẹ́.
sentences.en: The god that says matters pertaining to Ògún are irrelevant will not find anything to eat when he/she wishes.

sentences.text: Oòrùn kì í jẹ iṣu àgbà kó má mọbẹ̀.
sentences.en: An elder does not lose his yams to the sun without knowing where the event happened.

sentences.text: Oòrùn kì í là kínú bí olóko.
sentences.en: The sun does not shine and cause displeasure in the farmer.

sentences.text: Òṣùpá lé a ní kò gún; ẹni tọ́wọ́ ẹ̀ ẹ́ bá to kó tún un ṣe.
sentences.en: The moon appears and people say it is not straight; whoever can reach it let him go and right it.

sentences.text: Òtòṣì ò gbọ́ tìṣẹ́ ẹ̀ ó ní ogún kó àparò; ọdẹ́ rorò.
sentences.en: The destitute person does not look to repairing his fortune; he says the partidge has been captured in a war, for the hunter is merciless.

sentences.text: Owó kì í lóye kọ́mọ kú sẹ́rú.
sentences.en: If the amount of money is known, a child cannot die in slavery.

sentences.text: Owó kì í yéye kọ́mọ ó kú.
sentences.en: If money is available in abundance, a child does not die.

sentences.text: Owó la fi ń fíná owó; bí ẹgbẹ̀rún bá so lókè, igbió la fi ń ká a.
sentences.en: Money is what one uses to kindle the fire for money; if a thousand cowries grow from the branches above, one uses two hundred cowries to pluck them.

sentences.text: Owó la fi ń lògbà; ọgbọ́n la fi ń gbélé ayé.
sentences.en: It is with money that we secure pleasures; it is with wisdom that one secures a good life.

sentences.text: Owó ní ń pa ọjà ọ̀mọ̀ràn.
sentences.en: It is money that brings a knowing person's trading to a conclusion.

sentences.text: Owó tọ́mọdé bá kọ́kọ́ ní, àkàrà ní ń fií rà.
sentences.en: The first money a youth comes into he spends on bean fritters.

sentences.text: Òwú kì í là kínú bí olóko.
sentences.en: The cotton seed does not open and thus anger the farmer.

sentences.text: Owú pani ju kùmọ̀.
sentences.en: Jealousy kills more surely than a cudgel.

sentences.text: Òyìnbó Òkè Eléérú, ó ṣubú sóde Alọ́ba; kùmọ̀ ni yó gbe dìde.
sentences.en: The white man from Òkè Elérú; he collapses in front of Alọba's compound; cudgels will help him up.

sentences.text: Ọ̀bẹ ń wólé ara ẹ̀ ó ní òún ń ba àkọ̀ jẹ́.
sentences.en: The knife is destroying its own home, it says it is ruining the sheath.

sentences.text: Ọbẹ̀ tí baálé kì í jẹ, ìyáálé ilé kì í sè é.
sentences.en: The sort of stew the man of the house will not eat, the woman of the house should not cook.

sentences.text: Ọ̀dẹ̀ ọmọ ń fi ìdò ṣeré.
sentences.en: An idiot child that plays with ìdò flowers.

sentences.text: Ọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀ ò gba òró, àfi abẹ́ ọdán.
sentences.en: The porch does not accommodate standing people; only the shade of the (ọdán) banyan tree does.

sentences.text: Ọ̀fàfà fohùn ṣakin.
sentences.en: The tree-bear wins renown with its voice.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n a-dákọ-kéré ò tó ti a-yọwó-má-rà.
sentences.en: The cunning of the person who skimps on the measure of her corn meal is not as great as that of the would-be purchaser who refuses to buy.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n dùn-ún gbọ́n; ìmọ́ dùn-ún mọ̀.
sentences.en: Wisdom is a good thing to have; knowledge is a good thing to have.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n ju agbára.
sentences.en: Wisdom is greater than strength.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n kì í tán.
sentences.en: Wisdom is never used up.

sentences.text: Ọgbọn la fi ń gbé ayé.
sentences.en: One needs wisdom to live in this world.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n lajá fi ń pa ìkokò bọ Ifá.
sentences.en: It is cunning that the dog employs in order to sacrifice a wolf to Ifá.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n ní ń ṣẹgun; ìmọ̀ràn ní ń ṣẹ́ ẹ̀tẹ̀.
sentences.en: Cunning wins battles; knowledge defeats plots.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n ọlọgbọ́n la fi ń ṣọgbọ́n, ìmọ̀ràn ẹnìkan ò tọ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
sentences.en: One learns wisdom from other people's wisdom one person's knowledge does not amount to anything.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n tí ahún gbọ́n, ẹ̀yìn ni yó máa tọ ti ìgbín.
sentences.en: The cunning that the tortoise has will always rank behind that of the snail.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n tí ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ fi pa ẹfọ̀n ló fi ń jẹ ẹ́.
sentences.en: The same cunning with which the toad killed the buffalo will show it how to eat the prey.

sentences.text: Ọgbọọgbọ́n làgbàlagbàá fi ń sá fún ẹran ńlá.
sentences.en: It is with cunning that a grown man runs away from a bull.

sentences.text: Ọjọ́ eré là ń jiyàn ohun.
sentences.en: It is on a playful occasion that one argues about matters.

sentences.text: Ọjọ́ tíìlùú bá ń lu onílù, iṣẹ́ mìíràn-án yá.
sentences.en: The day the drum begins to beat the drummer is the day he should seek another employment.

sentences.text: Ọjọ́ tí olówó ń ṣẹbọ ni à-wà-jẹ-wà-mu ìwọ̀fà.
sentences.en: The day the person who did the hiring makes a sacrifice is the day the hired hand eats and drinks.

sentences.text: Ọkọ́ ọlọ́kọ́ la fi ń gbọ́n èkìtì.
sentences.en: It is other people's hoe that one uses to clear a mound of rubbish.

sentences.text: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ń yọ ẹsẹ̀ lábàtà.
sentences.en: One at a time is how one extricates one's feet from a mire.

sentences.text: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ń yọ ẹsẹ̀ lẹ́kù.
sentences.en: One at a time is how one removes one's legs from a masquerade costume.

sentences.text: Ọkùnrin jẹ́jẹ́ a-bìwà-kunkun.
sentences.en: An easy-going man's gentle mien hides a strong disposition.

sentences.text: Ọlọ ò lọ ló dé Ìbarà? Ìbarà a máa ṣe ilé ọlọ?
sentences.en: If the grindstone did not move, how did it get to Ìbarà? Is Ìbarà the home of grindstones?

sentences.text: Ọlọ́gbọ́n jẹni bí ẹmùrẹ́n; aṣiwèré jẹni bí ìgbọ̀ngbọ̀n.
sentences.en: The wise person bites one like a mosquito; the mad person bites one like a gadfly.

sentences.text: Ọlọgbọ́n ló lè mọ àdììtú èdè.
sentences.en: Only a wise person can decipher the meaning of speech.

sentences.text: Ọlọgbọ́n ni yó jogún ògo; aṣiwèrè ni yó ru ìtìjú wálé.
sentences.en: The wise child will inherit glory; the idiot child will bring shame home with him.

sentences.text: Ọlọgbọ́n ọmọ ní ń mú inúu bàbá ẹ̀ dùn; aṣiwèrè ọmọ ní ń ba inú ìyá ẹ̀ jẹ́.
sentences.en: A wise child gladdens the heart of his father; an imbecile of a child saddens the heart of his mother.

sentences.text: Ọlọ́jà kì í wí pé kọ́jà ó tú.
sentences.en: The owner of the market never wishes the market to be disrupted.

sentences.text: Ọlọ́tí kì í mọ ọmọ ẹ̀ lólè
sentences.en: The wine seller never realizes that his child is a thief.

sentences.text: Ọlọ́tọ̀ọ́ ní tòun ọ̀tọ̀; ìyá ẹ̀ẹ́ kú nílé, o gbé e lọ sin sóko.
sentences.en: Ọlọ́tọ̀ says his ways are different; his mother dies at home and he takes her to the farm for burial.

sentences.text: Ọmọ atiro tó ra bàtà fún bàbá ẹ̀, ọ̀rọ̀ ló fẹ́ gbọ́.
sentences.en: The child of a cripple who bought shoes for his father is asking for a stern lecture.

sentences.text: Ọmọ ẹní dàra, bíi ká fi ṣaya kọ́.
sentences.en: One's child may be beautiful, but one cannot make her one's wife.

sentences.text: Ọmọ ẹni kì í gbọnsẹ̀ ká fi eèsún nù ú nídìí.
sentences.en: One does not, after one's child defecates, wipe the child's anus with the abrasive elephant grass.

sentences.text: Ọmọ iná là ń rán síná.
sentences.en: It is the child of fire that one sends on an errand to fire.

sentences.text: “Ọmọọ̀ mi ò yó” la mọ̀; “ọmọọ̀ mí yó, ṣùgbọ́n kò rí sáárá fẹ́,” a ò mọ ìyẹn.
sentences.en: “My child did not have enough to eat,” we understand; “My child had enough to eat but had no snuff to snort,” that we do not understand.

sentences.text: Ọmọ tí ò ní baba kì í jìjà ẹ̀bi.
sentences.en: A fatherless child should not engage in an unjust fight.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé kì í mọ àkókò tí kúrò-kúròó fi ń kúrò.
sentences.en: A small child never knows when kúròkúrò takes its leave.

sentences.text: Ọmọde kì í mọ ìtàn, kó mọ à-gbọ́-wí, kó mọ ọjọ́ tí a ṣe ẹ̀dá òun.
sentences.en: A child does not know so much history and know so much hearsay that it knows the day of its creation.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé kì í mọ orií jẹ kó má rá a lẹ́nu.
sentences.en: A child is never so careful about eating corn meal that it does not smear the meal on its mouth.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé kì í ní ina níle kí tòde má jòó o.
sentences.en: A child does not have fire at home and therefore escape being burned by the fire abroad.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé mọ sáárá, ṣùgbọ́n kò mọ àlọ̀yí.
sentences.en: A child knows snuff, but does not know how to grind and turn the tobacco.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé ò mẹ̀fọ́, ó ń pè é légbògi.
sentences.en: A child does not recognize a vegetable and calls it medicine.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé ò mọ oògùn, ó ń pè é lẹ́fọ̀o?; kò mọ̀ pé ikú tó pa baba òun ni.
sentences.en: A child does not know medicine and he therefore calls it vegetables; it does not recognize it as what killed its father.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé ò moògùn ó ń pè é lẹ́gùn-ún.
sentences.en: A child does not know medicine and says it is a thorn.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé yìí, máa wò mí lójú, ẹni (tí) a bá lọ sóde là ń wò lójú.
sentences.en: Child, keep your eyes on me; one keeps one's eyes on the person who takes one visiting.

sentences.text: Ọ̀mọ̀ràn ní ń mọ oyún ìgbín.
sentences.en: Only a sage knows the pregnancy of a snail.

sentences.text: Ọ̀pá gbóńgbó ní n ṣíwájú agbọ́ọni.
sentences.en: It is a small walking-stick that goes before the person who walks a path overhung with foliage that is wet with morning dew.

sentences.text: Ọpẹ́ ló yẹ ẹrú.
sentences.en: Gratitude is what befits the slave.

sentences.text: Ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀ èèyàn, bí a ò bá gbé e lulẹ̀, kò níí lè fọhùn ire.
sentences.en: A person who is like the divining string: unless you throw him down he will not talk sense.

sentences.text: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní kéjò máa kálọ; ìjà òún di ojú ọ̀nà.
sentences.en: The toad tells the snake to follow it, for it does not fight except by the roadside.

sentences.text: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní òún lè sín ìlẹ̀kẹ̀; ta ní jẹ́ fi ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sídìí ọmọọ ẹ̀?
sentences.en: The toad boasts that it knows how to string beads; who, though, would put a toad's beads around his child's waist?

sentences.text: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀ ń yan káńdú-kàǹdù-káńdú lóju ẹlẹ́gùúsí; ẹlẹ́gùúsí ò gbọdọ̀ yí i lata.
sentences.en: The toad struts nonchalantly before the person cooking ẹ̀gúsí stew; the person cooking the ẹ̀gúsí stew will never add it to the ingredients.

sentences.text: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò mọ̀nà odò, ó dà á sí àwàdà.
sentences.en: The toad does not know the way to the stream and turns matters into a jest.

sentences.text: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ òjò ní ń lé eégún wọlé kẹri-kẹri.
sentences.en: It is a deluge that chases the eégún masquerader indoors indefinitely.

sentences.text: Ọ̀ràn kan la fi ń ṣòfin ọ̀kan.
sentences.en: One problem serves as the basis for a law that will apply to another case.

sentences.text: Ọ̀ràn ọlọ́ràn la fi ń kọ́gbọ́n.
sentences.en: From other people's problems one learns wisdom.

sentences.text: Ọ̀ràn tí ò sunwọ̀n, konko ǹ ṣojú.
sentences.en: A matter that is unpalatable hardens the eyes.

sentences.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ kì í gbórín ká fi ọ̀bẹ bù ú, ẹnu la fi ń wí i.
sentences.en: A problem is not so formidable that one attacks it with a knife; one tackles it with the mouth.

sentences.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ la fi ń jẹ omitooro ọ̀rọ̀.
sentences.en: Words are the things with which to savor the delicious broth of words.

sentences.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ọ́ ni òun ò nílé; ibi tí wọ́n bá rí ni wọ́n ti ń sọ òun.
sentences.en: Discourse says it has no home; people engage in it wherever they please.

sentences.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ rere ní ń yọ obì lápò; ọ̀rọ̀ búburú ní ń yọ ọfà lápó.
sentences.en: Good talk brings the kola-nut out of the pouch; provocative talk draws the arrow out of th quiver.

sentences.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ọlọgbọ́n bá sọ, ẹnu aṣiwèrè la ti ń gbọ́ ọ.
sentences.en: Whatever a wiseman says will be heard repeated by the nitwit.

sentences.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ tó dojú rú di ti ọlọ́rọ̀, ayé á dẹ̀yìn.
sentences.en: A problem that is too complicated to resolve becomes the sole responsibility of the person concerned; the world leaves him/her to his/her devices.

sentences.text: Ọsán gbé ojú ọrun le kókó; bó bá wọ odò, a di ọ̀-rọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀.
sentences.en: The bow-string is taut while it remains on the bow; dipped into the river it becomes very soft indeed.

sentences.text: Ọ̀sán ọ̀run ò pọ́n; ẹni tó bá yá kó máa bá tiẹ̀ lọ.
sentences.en: It is not yet noon time in heaven; whoever is anxious to get there may go ahead by himself/herself.

sentences.text: Ọwọ́ aṣiwèrè ni a gbé ń bá apá yíya.
sentences.en: It is in the hands of an imbecile that one finds a severed arm.

sentences.text: Ọ̀wọ̀ọ kókó la fi ń wọ igi; ọ̀wọ̀ òrìṣà la fi ń wọ àfín.
sentences.en: The regard one has for the knob is the one with which one clothes the tree; the regard one has for the gods is the same that one invests the albino with.

sentences.text: Ràdà-ràdà-á mọ ibi tí ó ńrè.
sentences.en: The meandering person knows where he is headed.

sentences.text: Rírí tí a rí igún la fi ń ta igún lọ́fà.
sentences.en: It is because one sees the vulture that one shoots arrows at it.

sentences.text: “Sìn mí ká relé àna,” ó wẹ̀wù ẹtù.
sentences.en: “Go with me to my in-laws' home,” and he wore a garment made from rich hand-woven material.

sentences.text: Sọ̀rọ̀ kí ọlọ́rọ̀ gbọ́, àbùkù ní ń fi kanni.
sentences.en: Spreading rumors into the ears of the subject of the rumor brings disgrace to one.

sentences.text: Ṣàǹgó kì í jà kó mú ilé aró.
sentences.en: Ṣango does not fight and destroy the enclosure for dyeing.

sentences.text: “Ṣe mí níṣu” ní ń ṣíwájú “ẹ kúuṣẹ́” bí?
sentences.en: Does “Give me some yam” go before “Hello there, you working man.”?

sentences.text: Ṣẹ̀kẹ̀rẹ̀ ò ṣéé fọ̀pá na.
sentences.en: The beaded musical gourd is not something to play with a stick.

sentences.text: Ṣẹ́kẹ́ṣẹkẹ̀ dára, ṣùgbọ́n alágbẹ̀dẹ ò rọ ọ́ fún ọmọ ẹ̀.
sentences.en: Handcuffs are pretty, but the blacksmith does not fashion them for his own child.

sentences.text: Sútà ò nílé; ìkóríta lÈṣù ń gbé.
sentences.en: Perfidy has no home; the home of Èṣù is the crossroads.

sentences.text: Ta lèèyàn nínú ẹrú Ààrẹ? A ní Ìdaganna la wá wá, ẹ ní Ìdakolo?
sentences.en: Which of the Ààrẹ́'s slaves is a person of any account? We said we came looking for Ìdaganna, and you ask, “Ìdakolo?”

sentences.text: Ta ní jẹ́ jẹ ọṣẹ kó fògìrì fọṣọ?
sentences.en: Who would eat soap and wash clothes with fermented beans?

sentences.text: Ta ní mọ̀dí òjò, bí kò ṣe Ṣàngó?
sentences.en: Who can know the secret of the rain if not Ṣàngo?

sentences.text: Tábà tí ò dùn, ẹnu ò tà á.
sentences.en: Snuff that is not pleasant, the mouth cannot not sell.

sentences.text: “Tèmi ò ṣòro,” tí kì í jẹ kọ́mọ alágbẹ̀dẹ ní idà.
sentences.en: “Mine is not urgent.” which prevents the son of the blacksmith from owning a sword.

sentences.text: Tẹni ní ń jọnilójú; eèràá bímọọ ẹ̀ ó sọ ọ́ ní òyírìgbí.
sentences.en: One's own thing is what impresses one; the ant has a child and names it The-one-who-rolls-mightily-around.

sentences.text: Tẹni-n-tẹni; bí àpọ́n bá sun iṣu a bù fọ́mọọ ẹ̀.
sentences.en: One's own is one's own; when a man without a wife roasts yams he cuts a piece for his child.

sentences.text: Tẹ̀tẹ́ ní ń ṣíwájú eré sísa.
sentences.en: A child's learning to walk comes before running.

sentences.text: Tiè̩é̩ sàn, tèmí sàn, lolókùnrùn méjì fi ń dìmú.
sentences.en: “Your condition is better; My condition is better,” is what gets two invalids into a fight.

sentences.text: Tinú ọ̀lẹ lọ̀lẹ ń jẹ; aṣiwèrè èèyàn ni ò mọ èrú tí yó gbà.
sentences.en: The lazy person eats the products of his native wisdom; only a fool does not know what devious way will be fruitful.

sentences.text: Wàrà-wàrà là ń yọ oró iná.
sentences.en: When one is on fire one's reaction is extremely agile.

sentences.text: Wèrèé dùn-ún wò, kò ṣéé bí lọ́mọ.
sentences.en: An imbecile makes an entertaining spectacle, but one would not want one as one's child.

sentences.text: Wèrèé yàtọ̀ sí wéré; wéré kì í ṣe wèrè; ìjá yàtọ̀ sí eré.
sentences.en: Madness differs from the singing of Islamic songs; the singing of Islamic songs is not madness; fighting is different from playing.

sentences.text: Wéré-wéré lọmọdé ń bọ oko èèsì.
sentences.en: A child's journey home from a nettle bush is fast indeed.

sentences.text: Wò mí lójú, wò mí lẹ́ẹ̀kẹ́; ẹni a bá lọ sóde là ń wò lójú.
sentences.en: Keep your eyes on my face, and keep your eyes on my cheeks; one keeps one's eyes on the person with whom one goes visiting.

sentences.text: “Wo ọmọọ̀ mi dè mí”: ó ń lo kíjìpá mẹ́ta gbó; mélòó ni ọlọ́mọọ́ máa lò gbó?
sentences.en: “Look after the child for me”: she wears three durable hand-loom wrappers to tatters; how many would the mother of the child herself wear out?

sentences.text: Wolé-wolé kì í wolé agbọ́n láì tẹ́.
sentences.en: The sanitary inspector does not inspect a wasp's home without coming to grief.

sentences.text: Wọ́n ní, “Afọ́jú, o ò tanná alẹ́.” Ó ní àtọ̀sán àtòru, èwo lòún rí níbẹ?
sentences.en: People said, “Blind man, you did not light a lamp.” He asked, night or day, which one would his eyes register?

sentences.text: A bu omi lámù a rí eégún; kí ni ẹni tó lọ sódò lọ pọnmi yó rìí?
sentences.en: We scoop water from the water pot and see a masquerader; what will the person who goes to draw water at the river find?

sentences.text: A fún ọ níṣu lỌ́yọ̀ọ́ ò ń dúpẹ́; o rígi sè é ná?
sentences.en: You are given yams at Ọyọ and you rejoice; have you secured wood to cook them?

sentences.text: A kì í bá ẹlẹ́nu jìjà òru.
sentences.en: One does not fight at night with a braggart.

sentences.text: A kì í bú ọba onígẹ̀gẹ̀ lójú àwọn èèyàn-án ẹ̀.
sentences.en: One does not insult a king with a goitre in the presence of his people.

sentences.text: A kì í du orí olórí kí àwòdì gbé tẹni lọ.
sentences.en: One does not fight to save another person's head only to have a kite carry one's own away.

sentences.text: A kì í fi ìkánjú lá ọbẹ̀ gbígbóná.
sentences.en: One does not eat scalding stew in a hurry.

sentences.text: A kì í gbélé gba ọfá láìlọ ogun.
sentences.en: One does not sit at home, not go to war, and yet be shot with an arrow.

sentences.text: A kì í kánjú tu olú-ọrán; igba ẹ̀ ò tóó sebẹ̀.
sentences.en: One does not gather olú-ọrán mushrooms in haste; two hundred of them are not enough to make a stew.

sentences.text: A kì í rídìí òkun; a kì í rídìí ọsà; ọmọ-oní-gele-gele kì í jẹ́ kí wọ́n rídìí òun.
sentences.en: One never sees the bottom of the ocean; no one ever sees the bottom of the lagoon; a well-bred woman will never expose her buttocks to anyone.

sentences.text: A kì í rójú ẹni purọ́ mọ́ni.
sentences.en: One does not look into the eyes of a person and still tell a lie against that person.

sentences.text: A kì í sọ̀rọ̀ orí bíbẹ́ lójú ọmọdé; lọ́rùnlọ́rùn ni yó máa wo olúwaa ẹ̀.
sentences.en: One does not speak of a beheading in the presence of a child; otherwise his gaze will be fixated on the neck of the person concerned.

sentences.text: À ń gba òròmọ adìẹ lọ́wọ́ ikú, ó ní wọn ò jẹ́ kí òun jẹ̀ láàtàn.
sentences.en: One struggles to save the chick from certain death, and it complains that one is preventing it from foraging at the dump.

sentences.text: À ń ṣa kẹ́kẹ́, aájò ẹwà ni; à ń bàbàjà, aájò ẹwà ni.
sentences.en: Marking one's face with kẹ́kẹ́ is a quest for beauty; marking one's face with àbàjà is a quest for beauty.

sentences.text: A sìnkú tán, alugba ò lọ; ó fẹ́ ṣúpó ni?
sentences.en: The funeral is over, but the calabash beater does not take his leave; does he want to inherit a wife?

sentences.text: Abẹ́rẹ́ bọ́ sómi táló; Ọ̀dọ̀fín ní òun-ún gbọ́ “jàbú!”
sentences.en: The needle makes an almost inaudible sound when it drops into the water; Ọdọfin said he heard a loud splash.

sentences.text: Abiyamọ, kàgbo wàrà; ọjọ́ ń lọ.
sentences.en: Nursing mother, make the herbal decoction in good time; the day is waning.

sentences.text: Àbùlẹ̀ ní ń mú aṣọ tọ́; ẹni tí kò tọ́jú àbùlẹ̀ yó ṣe araa ẹ̀ lófò aṣọ.
sentences.en: Patching extends the life of clothes; whoever does not save materials for patching deprives himself or herself of clothing.

sentences.text: Àdàbà ń pògèdè, ó rò pé ẹyẹlé ò gbọ́; ẹyẹlé gbọ́, títiiri ló tiiri.
sentences.en: The dove recites incantations, thinking that the pigeon cannot hear; the pigeon hears; it is only pretending to sleep.

sentences.text: Àdó gba ara ẹ̀ tẹ́lẹ̀, ká tó fi oògùn sí?
sentences.en: Could the small gourd save itself, before we put charms into it?

sentences.text: Àdóìṣí loògùn ọrọ̀.
sentences.en: Choosing-a-base-and-maintaining-it is the medicine for wealth.

sentences.text: Afẹ́fẹ́ tó wọlé tó kó aṣọ iyàrá, ìkìlọ̀ ni fún ẹni tó wọ tiẹ̀ sọrùn.
sentences.en: The wind that enters into the house and carries off the clothes in the bedroom is a warning to those who wear theirs around their necks.

sentences.text: Àfojúdi ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ní ń jẹ́ “Ẹrú-kò-ní.”
sentences.en: It is an impertinent bead that is named “The-slave-does-not-own-its like.”

sentences.text: Àgékù ejò, tí ń ṣoró bí agbọ́n.
sentences.en: Partially severed snake, that stings like a wasp.

sentences.text: Àgúnbàjẹ́ ni tolódó.
sentences.en: Pounding-until-it-is-ruined is the habit of the owner of the mortar.

sentences.text: Àgùntàn bọ̀lọ̀jọ̀ ò gbàgbé eléèrí bọ̀rọ̀.
sentences.en: The big, fat sheep does not soon forget the provider of corn bran.

sentences.text: Àgùntàn ń wò sùn-ùn; ọgbọ́n inú pé egbèje.
sentences.en: The sheep stares blankly, but its cunning stratagems number a thousand four hundred.

sentences.text: Àgùntàn ò jí ní kùtùkùyù ṣe ẹnu bọbọ.
sentences.en: A sheep does not wake in the morning and droop its mouth.

sentences.text: Àgbà òṣìkà ń gbin ìyà sílẹ̀ de ọmọọ rẹ̀.
sentences.en: A wicked elder sows suffering for his children.

sentences.text: Àgbẹ̀ ò dáṣọ lóṣù, àfọdún.
sentences.en: A farmer does not make new clothes monthly, only annually.

sentences.text: Àgbẹ̀ tó bá pẹ́ nílé ò níí kọ oko ọ̀sán.
sentences.en: A farmer who tarries in the house will not object to hoeing the farm in the afternoon.

sentences.text: À-gbẹ́rù-àì-wẹ̀yìn lọ̀pálábá fi gbàgbé ìyá ẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: Picking-up-one's-load-without-checking-one's-rear caused the piece of broken bottle to forget its mother on the ground.

sentences.text: Agbójúlógún fi araa rẹ̀ fóṣì ta.
sentences.en: He-who-places-his-hopes-on-inheritance delivers himself to destitution.

sentences.text: Àgbọ́ká etí ọlọ́ràn á di.
sentences.en: The ear that will insist on hearing everything will go deaf.

sentences.text: Àgbọ́kànlé ò pani lébi.
sentences.en: A thing in which one reposes one's trust does not make one hunger.

sentences.text: Àìfẹ̀sọ̀ké ìbòsí ni kò ṣéé gbè.
sentences.en: It is an alarm that is raised without moderation that finds no helpers.

sentences.text: Àìgbọ́ràn, baba àfojúdi.
sentences.en: Disobedience, father of disregard.

sentences.text: Àìlèfọhùn ní ń ṣáájú orí burúkú.
sentences.en: Inability to speak out precedes misfortunes.

sentences.text: Àìrọ́rọ̀sọ ìyàwó tó wí pé èkúté-ilé yó jẹ idẹ; bẹ́ẹ̀ni Mọ́jidẹ nìyálée rẹ̀ ń jẹ́.
sentences.en: The junior wife could find nothing to say, and said that the mice in the house will eat brass; the senior wife if the household happens to be named Mọjidẹ(Ọmọ-ọ́-jẹ-idẹ) (meaning “Child eats brass.”)

sentences.text: Àìtètèmólè, olèé mólóko.
sentences.en: Because of the delay in apprehending the thief, the thief apprehends the owner of the farm.

sentences.text: Ajá ilé ò mọdẹẹ́ ṣe.
sentences.en: A domesticated dog does not know how to hunt.

sentences.text: Ajá kì í dán-nu “Kò séwu” lókò ẹkùn.
sentences.en: A dog does not boast “No danger” in a leopard's bush.

sentences.text: Ajá tí yó sọnù kì í gbọ́ fèrè ọdẹ.
sentences.en: A dog destined to be lost does not hear the hunter's whistle.

sentences.text: Ajá tó rí mọ́tò tó dúró fi araa ẹ̀ bọ Ògún.
sentences.en: A dog that sees a motor vehicle and stands in its was makes itself a sacrifice to Ogun.

sentences.text: Àjànàkú tí a gbẹ́ ọ̀fìn sílẹ̀ dè, erin-ín mojú; erin ò bá ibẹ̀ lọ.
sentences.en: One digs a pit in the path of the elephant, but the elephant can read signs; the elephant does not go that way.

sentences.text: Àjẹ́ ń ké, òkùnrùn ò paradà; ó lówó ẹbọ nílé.
sentences.en: A witch proclaims her presence and an invalid does not make away; he must have money for sacrifices at home.

sentences.text: Ajẹnifẹ́ni, èkúté ilé.
sentences.en: One-that-bites-and-blows-on-the-wound, the house-mouse.

sentences.text: Aaka ò gbé ọ̀dàn; igbó ní ń gbé.
sentences.en: The hedgehog does not live in the grassland, only in the forest.

sentences.text: Àkàlàmàgbòó ṣoore ó yọ gẹ̀gẹ̀ lọ́rùn.
sentences.en: The ground hornbill did a favor and developed a goitre.

sentences.text: Akánjú jayé, ọ̀run wọn ò pẹ́.
sentences.en: People who live impatiently: their going to heaven is not far off.

sentences.text: Àáké tí ń gégií kọsẹ̀, gbẹ́nàgbẹ́nàá bu ètù sórí.
sentences.en: The axe that cuts wood stumbles, and the carver anoints his head with medicinal powder.

sentences.text: Àkèekèé ò ṣéé dì níbò.
sentences.en: A scorpion is not a thing to close one's palms on.

sentences.text: Àkèekèé rìn tapótapó.
sentences.en: The scorpion travels accompanied by venom.

sentences.text: Àkèekèé ta Kindo lẹpọ̀n, ará ilée Labata ń rojú; kí ló kàn án níbẹ̀?
sentences.en: A scorpion stung Kindo in the testicle, and a person from Labata's household frowns in dismay; what business is it of his?

sentences.text: Akóbáni lèkúté-ilé; ejò kì í jàgbàdo.
sentences.en: The mouse is a bringer of disaster to the innocent; snakes do not eat corn.

sentences.text: Àkọ̀ tó bá bá ọ̀bẹ dìtẹ̀ á gbọgbẹ́ láti inú.
sentences.en: A sheath that engages in a dispute with a knife will suffer an internal wound.

sentences.text: Alágbàró ò yege; aláṣọ á gbà á bó dọ̀la.
sentences.en: She who borrows a wrapper-skirt to wear is not home free; the owner of the cloth will take it back come tomorrow.

sentences.text: Aláǹgbá tó fojú di erè, ikùn ejò ni yó bàá araa ẹ̀.
sentences.en: A lizard that views a python with disregard will find itself in the belly of the snake.

sentences.text: Alápàáǹdẹ̀dẹ̀ ń jayé lébé-lébé.
sentences.en: The sparrow enjoys life carefully.

sentences.en: Something-seen-but-unmentionable, something-seen-but-unspeakable is the death of a guardian of the mysteries.

sentences.en: A cripple does not block the road with his legs.

sentences.en: A cripple who has no legs to stand on has wisdom inside him.

sentences.en: He-who-flees-on-seeing-the-king is no coward.

sentences.text: Arúgbó ṣoge rí; àkísà-á lògbà rí.
sentences.en: The old person was once a dandy; the rag was once in fashion.

sentences.text: Asárétete ní ń kọjá ilé; arìngbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni yóò rí oyè jẹ.
sentences.en: The fast runner will run past his home; the leisurely stroller is the one who will win the title.

sentences.en: The kite plays with the pigeon and the pigeon rejoices; the pigeon is courting death.

sentences.en: Roughhousing keeps the young of the cane rat from learning wisdom.

sentences.en: What one puts aside is what one returns to find; whoever dumps water ahead of him/her will step on wet earth.

sentences.en: Only the newly weaned cat suffers; eventually it will learn to kill mice.

sentences.en: Difficult-to-wear like the garment of immoderation.

sentences.en: Pepper is small; its fight is much bigger.

sentences.en: Person-who-stones-and-breaks-partridge's-eggs; the eyes find what the eyes seek.

sentences.en: A-creature-that-learns-wisdom-in-reverse-order, dog-with-severed-ears; after its ears have been severed it hides the razor.

sentences.text: Àtẹ́lẹwọ́ ẹni kì í tanni.
sentences.en: One's palm does not deceive one.

sentences.text: 1e Atọrọ-ohun-gbogbo-lọ́wọ́-Ọlọ́run kì í kánjú.
sentences.en: The-seeker-of-all-things-from-God does not yield to impatience.

sentences.text: Àwòfín ní ń mú ọ̀rẹ́ bàjẹ́; fírí là ń wo ẹni tí ń woni.
sentences.en: Persistent-staring ruins a friendship; one looks only glancingly at those looking at one.

sentences.text: Àáyá kan-án bẹ̀ ọ́ wò; igba wọ́n ti rí ọ.
sentences.en: If a single Colubus monkey sees you, be sure that two hundred of them have seen you.

sentences.en: The-impatient-reporter, wife of the hunter, she says that her husband killed the first and killed the sixth.

sentences.text: Àyé gba ògùnmọ̀ ó ránṣẹ́ sí òdú; àyé gba Tápà ó kọ́lé ìgunnu.
sentences.en: The cultivated vegetable is contented, so it sends for its wild variety; the Nupe (Fulani) person is so comfortable that he builds a tall house.

sentences.text: Ayé ò ṣéé fipá jẹ.
sentences.en: Life is nothing to enjoy heedlessly.

sentences.text: “Bá mi mádìẹ” kì í fi orúnkún bó.
sentences.en: “Help me catch a chicken” does not scrape his knees.

sentences.text: Baálé ilé kú, wọ́n fi olókùnrùn rọ́lé; ẹkún ń gorí ẹkún.
sentences.en: The man of the house died and they put an invalid in his place; weeping climbs upon weeping.

sentences.text: “Baálé pè mí n kò wá”, ọ̀hànhàn ní ń pa wọ́n.
sentences.en: “The patriarch of the compound called me but I did not respond” dies of anxiety.

sentences.text: Bánú sọ, má bàá èèyàn sọ; èèyàn ò sí; ayé ti dèké.
sentences.en: Counsel with your inside, do not counsel with people; “good” people are no longer to be found; the world has turned false.

sentences.text: Bí a bá bu ìrẹ̀ jẹ, ká bu ìrẹ̀ sápò.
sentences.en: If one takes a bite of a cricket, one should put a little in one's pocket.

sentences.text: Bí a bá bu ọba tí a sẹ́, ọba a fini sílẹ.
sentences.en: If one insults a king and denies doing so, the king leaves one in peace.

sentences.text: Bí a bá bú ọba, à sẹ́; bí a bá bú ọ̀ṣọ̀run, à sẹ́.
sentences.en: If one insults the king, one denies doing so; if one insults the chief minister, one denies doing so.

sentences.text: Bí a bá dákẹ́, tara ẹni a báni dákẹ́.
sentences.en: If one keeps silent, what is in one's body keeps silent with one.

sentences.text: Bí a bá fa àgbò féégún, à fi okùn-un rẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: If one drags a sheep to present to a masquerader, one lets go of its leash.

sentences.text: Bí a bá fẹ́ràn ọ̀rẹ́ ẹni láfẹ̀ẹ́jù, bó bá forígbún, ìjà ní ń dà.
sentences.en: If one loves one's friend beyond reason, when that friend bumps his/her head a fight results.

sentences.text: Bí a bá fi dídùn họ ifò̩n, a ó họra dé eegun.
sentences.en: If one scratches an itch as long as the sensation is pleasant, one will scratch down to the bone.

sentences.text: Bí a bá fi ojú igi gbígbẹ wo tútù, tútùú lè wó pani.
sentences.en: If one approaches a dried-up tree as one would a green one, it is liable to crash on one and crush one to death.

sentences.text: Bí a bá fi ọdún mẹ́ta pilẹ̀ṣẹ̀ẹ wèrè, ọjọ́ wo la ó bunijẹ?
sentences.en: If one takes three years to prepare for one's madness, when will one start biting people?

sentences.text: Bí a bá fi ọdún mẹ́ta ṣánpá, ọdún mélòó la ó fi fò?
sentences.en: If one spends three years flapping one's arms, how many years will one take to fly?

sentences.text: Bí a bá fi ọwọ́ kan fọmọ fọ́kọ, ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá kì í ṣeé gbà á mọ́.
sentences.en: If one gives a girl away in marriage with one hand, ten hands will not suffice to take her back.

sentences.text: Bí a bá lé ẹni, tí a kò bá ẹni, ìwọ̀n là ń bá ẹnií ṣọ̀tá mọ.
sentences.en: If one chases a person and does not catch up with the person, one should moderate one's hatred of the person.

sentences.text: Bí a bá ní ká bẹ́ igi, a ó bẹ̀ẹ́ èèyàn.
sentences.en: If one attempts to cut a tree, one will cut people.

sentences.text: Bí a bá ní ká jẹ èkuru kó tán, a kì í gbọn ọwọ́ọ rẹ̀ sáwo.
sentences.en: If one wishes to clean one's plate of dry bean grits, one does not keep scraping the remnants from one's fingers onto the plate.

sentences.text: Bí a bá ń retí òfò, ká fi ohun tọrẹ.
sentences.en: If one expects a loss, one should make a gift of what one has.

sentences.text: Bí a bá sọ̀kò sí àárín ọjà, ará ilé ẹni ní ń bà.
sentences.en: If one throws a stone into the market place, it hits someone from one's household.

sentences.text: Bí a bá sọ̀rọ̀ fún olófòófó, ajádìí agbọ̀n la sọ ọ́ sí.
sentences.en: Whatever one says to a talebearer one says to a basket that has lost its bottom.

sentences.text: Bí a bá ṣí ìdí ẹni sókè, ọmọ aráyé á rọ omi gbígbóná sí i.
sentences.en: If one exposes one's anus to view, people will fill it with hot water.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá láyàa rìndọ̀rìndọ̀, a kì í jẹ aáyán.
sentences.en: If one's stomach is not immune to nausea, one does not eat roaches.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá lè kú, ìpẹ̀ là ń gbà.
sentences.en: If one is unable (or unwilling) to die, one accepts consolation.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá lè mú ọkọ, a kì í na obìnrin-in rẹ.
sentences.en: If one is no match for the husband, one does not hit the wife.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá lówó aládìn-ín, à jẹun lójúmọmọ, à gbálẹ̀ sùn wàrà.

sentences.en: If a matter is dark, one peeps at it under cover.

sentences.en: “Today belongs to me; tomorrow belongs to me” is the attitude that pushes a youth into debt.
