sentences.en: The cursing is far in excess of what is lost; a needle goes missing and the owners invoke Ṣàngó.

sentences.text: Erée kí lajá ń bá ẹkùn ṣe?
sentences.en: What sort of sport is it that the dog is engaged in with the leopard?

sentences.text: Èrò kì í; jẹ́wọ́ọ “Mo tà tán.”
sentences.en: The trader never confesses, “I sold all my wares.”

sentences.text: Eṣinṣin ò mọkú; jíjẹ ni tirẹ̀.
sentences.en: The fly does not heed death; all its cares to do is eat.

sentences.text: Èṣù ò ṣejò; ẹni tó tẹ ejò mọ́lẹ̀ lẹ̀bá ń bá.
sentences.en: There is no disaster stalking the snake; it is whoever steps on a snake that is in trouble.

sentences.text: Etí mẹta ò yẹ orí; èèyàn mẹ́ta ò dúró ní méjì-méjì.
sentences.en: Three ears are unbecoming for the head; three people cannot stand in twos.

sentences.text: Ewú logbó; irùngbọ̀n làgbà; máamú làfojúdi.
sentences.en: Grey hair shows age; a beard shows maturity; a moustache shows impudence.

sentences.text: Ewúrẹ́ jẹ ó relé; àgùntán jẹ ó relé; à-jẹ-ì-wálé ló ba ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ jẹ́.
sentences.en: The goat forages and returns home; the sheep forages and returns home; the pig's flaw is its habit of not returning home after foraging.

sentences.text: Ewúrẹ́ kì í wọlé tọ ìkokò.
sentences.en: A goat does not venture into the lair of a wolf.

sentences.text: Èèyan má-jẹ̀ẹ́-kí-èèyàn-kú ń bẹ níbòmíràn; bó-le-kú-ó-kú ń bẹ nílée wa.
sentences.en: Save-the-person-from-death type of people abounds elsewhere; let-the-person-die-if-he/she-wishes type abounds in our house.

sentences.text: Èyí ayé ń ṣe n kà ṣàì ṣe; bádìẹẹ́ máa wọ ọ̀ọ̀dẹ̀ a bẹ̀rẹ̀.
sentences.en: Whatever the rest of the world does I will not forswear; when a chicken wants to enter the porch it stoops.

sentences.text: Èyí ò tófò, èyí ò tófò; fìlà ìmàleé kù pẹ́tẹ́kí.
sentences.en: “This is no great loss; this is no great loss;” the muslim's cap dwindles to almost nothing.

sentences.text: Ẹ pa Ayéjẹ́nkú, ẹ pa Ìyálóde Aníwúrà; ìgbà tí ẹ pa Ìyápọ̀ ẹ gbàgbé ogun.
sentences.en: You killed Ayejenku and killed Iyalode Aniwura; but when you killed Iyapọ you forgot about wars.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀bi alábahun kì í gbèé dẹ̀bi ànaa rẹ̀.
sentences.en: The Tortoise's guilt is not long in becoming that of his parent-in-law's.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀bìtì ò peèrà tó ṣe pẹ̀lẹ́pẹ̀lẹ́; ẹnu ẹni ní ń pani.
sentences.en: A trap does not kill an ant that is cautious; it's one's mouth that turns out to be one's death.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀bìtì tí ò kún ẹmọ́ lójú, òun ní ń yí i lẹ́pọ̀n sẹ́yìn.
sentences.en: It is a trap that the giant rat disdains that wrenches its testicles backwards.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀gbá mọ̀dí Ọbà; ẹni tó gbéniṣánlẹ̀ẹ́ lè pani.
sentences.en: The Ẹgba know the secrets of Ọba town; whoever throws a person has the ability to kill the person.

sentences.text: Ẹgbẹ́ ẹja lẹja ń wẹ̀ tọ̀; ẹgbẹ́ ẹyẹ lẹyẹ ń wọ́ lé.
sentences.en: Fish swim in a school of their own kind; birds fly in a flock of their own kind.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀yìn àjànàkú là ń yọ ogbó; ta ní jẹ́ yọ agada lójú erin?
sentences.en: It is after the demise of the elephant that one brandishes a cudgel; who dares draw a scimitar in the face of an elephant?

sentences.text: Ẹ̀hìn ní ńdun ol-ókùú-àdá sí.
sentences.en: It is the back of the man with a blunt cutlass that suffers.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀ẹ̀kan ṣoṣo lọmọ ń sín tí à ń ní “à-sín-gbó, à-sín-tọ́.”
sentences.en: It is when a child sneezes only once that one wishes the child “sneeze and grow old, sneeze and live long.”

sentences.text: Ẹ̀kọ tí kò bá léwé làgbà ń gbà.
sentences.en: It is corn-loaf that has no leaf wrapping that the elder takes.

sentences.text: Ẹkùn kì í yan kí ajá yan.
sentences.en: A leopard does not strut and be answered by strutting from a dog.

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ tó kú légbodò ló ní ká fòun jẹyán.
sentences.en: It is a pig that dies at the time of the harvesting of new yams that asks to be eaten with pounded yam.

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́jọ́ kú sílé, aláròyé kú síta gbangba.
sentences.en: The person involved in an affair dies at home; the spokesperson dies out in the open.

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́kún sunkún ó bá tirẹ̀ lọ; aláròpa ìbá sunkún kò dákẹ́.
sentences.en: The person with a cause to cry cries and departs; if it were a person whose mind never leaves a problem he or she would never have stopped crying.

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́rù ní ńgbé ẹrù ká tó ba ké ọfẹ.
sentences.en: The owner of the load must first lift it before one lends one's encouragement.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀lúlùú, ìwọ ló fòjò pa araà rẹ.
sentences.en: Larkheeled Cuckoo, it was you that got yourself drenched in the rain.

sentences.text: Ẹni àjò ò pé kó múra ilé.
sentences.en: The person for whom the journey has not been profitable should prepare to return home.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá rọra pa eèrà á rí ìfun inúu rẹ̀.
sentences.en: Whoever takes great care in killing an ant will see its innards.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá fẹ́ abuké ni yó ru ọmọọ rẹ̀ dàgbà.
sentences.en: Whoever marries a humpbacked woman will carry her child on his back until the child is weaned.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá fẹ́ arúgbó gbẹ̀yìn ni yó sìnkúu rẹ̀.
sentences.en: The last spouse of an old person will bury him or her.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá mọ ayéé jẹ kì í gun àgbọn.
sentences.en: Whoever knows what makes for a good life never climbs coconut palms.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá mọ ayéé jẹ kì í jà.
sentences.en: Whoever knows how to enjoy life does not enter into a fight.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá mọ iṣin-ín jẹ a mọ ikú ojúu rẹ̀ẹ́ yọ.
sentences.en: Whoever knows how to eat Akee Apple must know how to remove its deadly raphe.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá na Ọ̀yẹ̀kú á ríjà Ogbè.
sentences.en: Whoever whips Ọ̀yẹ̀kú will have Ogbè to answer to.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá sọ púpọ̀ á ṣìsọ.
sentences.en: Whoever talks a lot will misspeak.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá pé kí àkàlà má jòkú, ojúu rẹ̀ lẹyẹ ń kọ́kọ́ yọ jẹ.
sentences.en: Whoever says the ground-hornbill should not eat carrion, he or she will be the first to lose his or her eyes to the bird.

sentences.text: Ẹní bẹnií tẹ́ni.
sentences.en: Whoever pleads with one makes one lose face.

sentences.text: Ẹní dáríjiní ṣẹ̀tẹ́ ẹjọ́.
sentences.en: Whoever forgives one defuses the dispute.

sentences.text: Ẹní gúnyán kalẹ̀ yóò júbà ọbẹ̀.
sentences.en: A person who has made pounded yams must pay homage to the stew.

sentences.text: Ẹní gbé adíẹ òtòṣì-í gbé ti aláròyé.
sentences.en: Whoever steals a poor person's chicken steals from an incessant complainer.

sentences.text: Ẹní kánjú jayé á kánjú lọ sọ́run.
sentences.en: Whoever is in a hurry to enjoy life will go to heaven in a hurry.

sentences.text: Ẹni méjì kì í bínú egbinrin.
sentences.en: Two people do not hold a grudge and refuse reconciliation.

sentences.text: Ẹni òyìnbó fẹ́ràn ní ń tì mọ́lé.
sentences.en: It is the person the white man likes that the white man incarcerates.

sentences.text: Ẹní ṣe ọ̀ràn Ìjẹ̀bú: etí ẹ̀ á gbọ́ ìbọn.
sentences.en: Whoever provokes an Ijẹbu person, his or her ears will hear gunshot.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a bá ń mú ìyàwó bọ̀ wá fún kì í garùn.
sentences.en: The person to whom a bride is being brought does not strain his neck (to see her from a distance.)

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a bá ti rí kì í tún ba mọ́lẹ̀ mọ́.
sentences.en: A person who has been seen has no further need of hiding.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a fẹ́ẹ́ sunjẹ kì í fepo para lọ jókòó sídìí iná.
sentences.en: A person being eyed for barbecuing does not baste himself with oil and sit by the fire.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a lù lógbòó mẹ́fà, tí a ní kó fiyèdénú: ìgbà tí kò fiyèdénú ń kọ́?
sentences.en: A person is hit with a cudgel six times and then urged to learn forbearance; what other option does he or she have?

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a ò lè mú, a kì í gọ dè é.
sentences.en: One does not lie in ambush for an adversary one is no match for.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a ò lè mú, Ọlọ́run là ń fi lé lọ́wọ́.
sentences.en: An adversary over whom one cannot prevail, one leaves to God's judgement.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ń sáré kiri nínúu pápá ń wá ọ̀nà àti jìn sí kòtò.
sentences.en: The person who runs about in the bush courts the danger of falling into a ditch.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bá wọ odò ni àyà ń kò, àyà ò fo odò.
sentences.en: It is the person who enters a river who is terrified, not the river.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó jìn sí kòtòó kọ́ ará ìyókù lọ́gbọ́n.
sentences.en: The person who falls into a ditch teaches others a lesson.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó tọ odò tí kò dẹ̀yìn yò bàá Olúwẹri pàdé.
sentences.en: Whoever follows the river without turning back will come face to face with Oluwẹri.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bá mu ọtí ogójì á sọ̀rọ̀ okòó.
sentences.en: Whoever drinks forty cowries worth of wine will talk twenty cowries worth of talk.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó yá ẹgbàafà tí kò san án, ó bẹ́gi dí ọ̀nà egbèje.
sentences.en: The person who borrows twelve hundred cowries and does not pay them back blocks the path of fourteen hundred cowries.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó ba ogún-un baba rẹ̀ jẹ́, ó ja òkú ọ̀run lólè, yó sì di ẹni ìfibú.
sentences.en: Whoever ruins his or her father's bequest robs the dead, and becomes a person of reproach.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bá obìnrin kó lọ sílée rẹ̀ yó sùn nínú ẹ̀rù.
sentences.en: A man who goes with a woman to her house will sleep in fear.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ò fẹ́ẹ́ wọ àkísà kì í bá ajá ṣe erée géle.
sentences.en: A person who does not wish to wear rags should not engage in rough play with a dog.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ò tónií nà ò gbọdọ̀ ṣe kọ́-ń-dú síni.
sentences.en: A person who is not strong enough to beat one up should not adopt a threatening pose towards one.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí Oròó máa mú ń ba wọn ṣe àìsùn orò.
sentences.en: The person who will be the sacrificial victim of orò is joining in the revelry on the eve of the sacrifice.

sentences.text: Ẹnìkan kì í fi ọ̀bẹ tó nù jẹṣu.
sentences.en: No one eats yams with a lost knife.

sentences.text: Ẹnu iná ní ń pa iná; ẹnu èrò ní ń pa èrò.
sentences.en: The mouth of the louse is its death; the mouth of the nit is its death.

sentences.text: Ẹnu ni àparòó fi ń pe ọ̀rá; a ní “Kìkì ọ̀rá, kìkì ọ̀rá!”
sentences.en: With its own mouth the partridge invites its own ruin; it cries, “Nothing but fat, nothing but fat!”

sentences.text: Ẹnu tí ìgbín fi bú òrìṣà ní ń fií lọlẹ̀ lọ bá a.
sentences.en: The same mouth with which the snail insults the god is the one on which it crawls to the god.

sentences.text: Ẹnuù mi kọ́ ni wọ́n ti máa gbọ́ pé ìyá ọbaá lájẹ̀ẹ́.
sentences.en: It is not from my mouth that people will learn that the king's mother is a witch.

sentences.text: Ẹrẹ̀ òkèọ̀dàn ni yó kìlọ̀ fún a-láròó-gbálẹ̀ aṣọ.
sentences.en: The mud on the plains will teach a lesson to the person whose loincloth has a train sweeping the ground.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀rù kọ́ ní ń ba ọ̀pẹ tó ní ká dá òun sí, nítorí ẹmu ọ̀la ni.
sentences.en: It is not out of fear that the palm-tree pleads to be allowed to stand; it is on account of tomorrow's palm-wine.

sentences.text: Ẹṣin iwájú ni ti ẹ̀yìn ń wò sáré.
sentences.en: The leading horse is the one by which the followers set their pace.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀sọ̀ ẹ̀sọ̀ la fi ń lá ọbẹ̀ tó gbóná.
sentences.en: Slowly, slowly is the way to eat soup that is scalding hot.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀tẹ́ ní ń gbẹ̀yìn aláṣejù.
sentences.en: Disgrace is the reward of excess.

sentences.text: Ẹyẹ kí lo máa pa tí ò ń fi àkùkọ ṣe oògùn àtè?
sentences.en: What sort of bird do you hope to kill that you use a cock in the birdlime charm?

sentences.text: Ẹyin lọ̀rọ̀; bó bá balẹ̀ fífọ́ ní ń fọ́.
sentences.en: Words are eggs; when they drop on the floor they shatter into pieces.

sentences.text: Ẹyin adìẹ ò gbọdọ̀ forí sọ àpáta.
sentences.en: A chicken egg should not strike its head against a rock.

sentences.text: Fáàárí àṣejù, oko olówó ní ń mú ọmọ lọ.
sentences.en: Intemperate dandyism lands a youth in a creditor's farm as a pawn.

sentences.text: Fẹ̀yìntì kí o rí ìṣe èké; farapamọ́ kí; o gbọ́ bí aṣenií ti ń sọ.
sentences.en: Sit back and you will see how a devious person operates; conceal yourself and you will hear how those who seek others' destruction speak.

sentences.text: Fi ẹ̀jẹ̀ sínú, tu itọ́ funfun jáde.
sentences.en: Keep your red blood inside and spit out clear saliva.

sentences.text: Fi ohun wé ohun, fi ọ̀ràn wé ọ̀ràn; fi ọ̀ràn jì ká yìn ọ́.
sentences.en: Liken one thing to another, liken one matter to another; forgive and forget and earn people's praise.

sentences.text: Fi ọ̀ràn sínú pète ẹ̀rín; fi ebi sínú sunkún ayo.
sentences.en: Keep your troubles inside and laugh heartily; keep your hunger hidden and pretend to weep from satiation.

sentences.text: Fò síhìnín fò sọ́hùnún làkèré fi ń ṣẹ́ nítan.
sentences.en: Jump this way, jump that way is the way a frog breaks its thigh.

sentences.text: Ganganran ò ṣéé kì mọ́lẹ̀; a-gúnni-lọ́wọ́-bíi-ṣoṣoro.
sentences.en: A sharp object is not something to grab for; “it is” a-thing-that-pierces-one's-hand-like-a-sharp-instrument.

sentences.text: Gìdì-gìdì ò mọ́là; ká ṣiṣẹ́ bí ẹrú ò da nǹkan.
sentences.en: Scurrying around does not ensure prosperity; working like a slave results in nothing.

sentences.text: Gùdùgudu ò túra sílẹ̀ lẹ́ẹ̀kan.
sentences.en: Poisonous yam has never lost its skin.

sentences.text: Gùdùguduú kan légbò kán-ín-kán-ín.
sentences.en: Poisonous yam's roots are sour indeed.

sentences.text: “Gbà sókè” ni “Gbà sọ́kọ̀”; ohun tá a bá sọ síwájú là ḿbá.
sentences.en: “Put this above (ashore)” equals “Put this in the boat”; it is what one throws ahead that one finds in one's path.

sentences.text: Gbéjò-gbéjò ò gbé ọká.
sentences.en: No snake dancer dances with a cobra.

sentences.text: Gbẹ́ran-gbẹ́ran ò gbé ẹkùn.
sentences.en: No animal pilferer ever pilfers a leopard.

sentences.text: Gbígbòòrò là ń ṣe ọ̀nà igi.
sentences.en: The path along which a log will be rolled must be made wide enough.

sentences.text: Gbogbo ajá ní ń jẹ imí: èyí tó bá jẹ tiẹ̀ mẹ́nu laráyé ń pè ní dìgbòlugi.
sentences.en: All dogs eat excrement, but only those that smear their mouths with it are described as rabid.

sentences.text: Gbogbo ìjà nìjà; bóo gbémi lulẹ̀ mà mọ́ ẹ lójú lákọ lákọ.
sentences.en: Every way of fighting is a legitimate way of fighting. If you are strong enough to throw me, I will fight back by looking at you with absolute disdain.

sentences.text: Gbogbo obìnrin ló ń gbéṣẹ́, èyí tó bá ṣe tiẹ̀ láṣejù laráyé ń pè láṣẹ́wó.
sentences.en: All women are unfaithful; only those who know no moderation are put down as whores.

sentences.text: Gbólóhùn kan Agán tó awoó ṣe.
sentences.en: Just one utterance by the masquerader Agán is sufficient to effect a great deal of wonders.

sentences.text: Gbólóhùn kan-án ba ọ̀rọ̀ jẹ́; gbólóhùn kan-án tún ọ̀rọ̀ ṣe.
sentences.en: One solitary statement muddies an entire affair; one solitary statement clears all the confusion.

sentences.text: Gbólóhùn kan la bi elépo; elépo ń ṣe ìrànrán.
sentences.en: One asks only one question of the palm-oil seller, but she rambles endlessly on.

sentences.text: Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ òṣì bí ọmọ ọlọ́rọ̀ là ń rí.
sentences.en: At the beginning of one's penury one seems like the child of most prosperous parents.

sentences.text: Ibi ìṣáná la ti ńkíyè sóògùn.
sentences.en: It is from the time one makes one's boasts that one should begin to mind one's charms (or juju).

sentences.text: Ibi rere làkàsọ̀ńgbé sọlẹ̀.
sentences.en: The ladder always rests on a propitious spot.

sentences.text: Ibi tí a gbọ́n mọ là ń ṣòwò-o màlúù mọ.
sentences.en: One should limit the depth of one's involvement in cattle trading to the extent of one's astuteness.

sentences.text: Ibi tí a ti ń wo olókùnrùn lati ń wo ara ẹni.
sentences.en: Just as one cares for the sick, one should also care for oneself.

sentences.text: Ibi tí à ńlọ là ńwò, a kì í wo ibi tí a ti ṣubú.
sentences.en: One should keep one's eyes on where one is going, not where one stumbled.

sentences.text: Ibi tí akátá ba sí, adìẹ ò gbọdọ̀ débẹ̀.
sentences.en: Wherever the jackal lurks, the chicken must give the place a wide berth.

sentences.text: Ibi tí ó mọ là ń pè lọ́mọ.
sentences.en: Where it stops, there one designates “child.”

sentences.text: Ìbínú baba òṣì.
sentences.en: Anger “is the” father of hopelessness.

sentences.text: Ìbínú lọbá fi ń yọ idà; ìtìjù ló fi ń bẹ́ ẹ.
sentences.en: It is in anger that the king draws his sword; it is shame that makes him go through with the beheading.

sentences.text: Ìbínú ò mọ̀ pé olúwa òun ò lẹ́sẹ̀ ńlẹ̀
sentences.en: Anger does not know that its owner has no legs to stand on.

sentences.text: Ìbìsẹ́yín àgbò kì í ṣojo.
sentences.en: A ram's stepping backwards is not indicative of cowardice.

sentences.text: Ìbọn-ọ́n ní apátí kò lápátí, taní jẹ́ jẹ́ ka kọjú ìbọn kọ òun?
sentences.en: Whether a gun has a trigger or not, who would calmly permit the gun to be pointed at him/her?

sentences.text: Ìfẹ́ àfẹ́jù lewúrẹ́ fi ń bá ọkoọ ẹ̀ hu irùngbọ̀n.
sentences.en: It is excessive love that induces the goat to grow a beard in sympathy with her mate.

sentences.text: Ìfi ohun wé ohun, ìfi ọ̀ràn wé ọ̀ràn, kò jẹ́ kí ọ̀ràn ó tán.
sentences.en: Citing comparable things and recalling similar occurrences “in the past” makes ending a quarrel impossible.

sentences.text: Ìfunra loògùn àgbà.
sentences.en: Wariness is the elders' most efficacious juju.

sentences.text: Igi tó bá bá Ṣàngó lérí, gbígbẹ ní ń gbẹ.
sentences.en: Whatever tree engages in a contest of threats with Ṣàngó will suffer the fate of drying up.

sentences.text: Igúnnugún gbọ́n sínú.
sentences.en: The vulture conceals a lot of wisdom in itself.

sentences.text: Ìgbà ara ń bẹ lára là ń bù ú tà.
sentences.en: It is when there is a surfeit of flesh on the body that one cuts some of it for sale.

sentences.text: Igbá dojúdé ò jọ ti òṣónú, tinú igbá nigbá ń ṣe.
sentences.en: That a calabash faces downwards is no antisocial sign; the calabash is only acting according to its nature.

sentences.text: Ìgbà tí a bá ní kí Ègùn má jà ní ń yọ̀bẹ.
sentences.en: It is only when one pleads with the Ègùn person (from Porto Novo or Àjàṣẹ́ in present-day Benin Republic)that he draws his knife.

sentences.text: Ohun tí a ò pé yó dẹrù ní ń diṣẹ́.
sentences.en: It is always something one does not expect to become a load that eventually becomes a huge task.

sentences.text: Ohun tí a rí la fi ń bọ párá ẹni; bí igi tíná ń bẹ lẹ́nuu ẹ̀ kọ́.
sentences.en: It is whatever one can find that one uses to fill gaps in one's roof; that does not apply to a faggot spewing flames.

sentences.text: Ohun tí ajá rí tó fi ń gbó ò tó èyí tí àgùntàn-án fi ń ṣèran wò.
sentences.en: That which a dog sees and barks at is nothing compared to what the sheep contemplates in silence.

sentences.text: Ohun tó bá wu ọmọọ́ jẹ kì í run ọmọ nínú.
sentences.en: Whatever a child crave will not give him/her stomach ache.

sentences.text: Òjijì là ń rọ́mọ lọ́wọ́ alákẹdun.
sentences.en: It is all of a sudden that one sees a baby in the arms of the colobus monkey.

sentences.text: Òjò kan kì í báni lábà ká jìjàdù ọ̀rọ̀ọ́ sọ; bí ẹgbọ́n bá sọ tán, àbúrò á sọ.
sentences.en: When people are trapped in a hut by a downpour there is no sense in fighting to get a word in the discussion; after the older person has spoken, the younger person will speak.

sentences.text: Ojú abẹ ò ṣéé pọ́nlá.
sentences.en: The edge of a razor is not a thing to lick.

sentences.text: Ojú ológbò lèkúté ò gbọdọ̀ yan.
sentences.en: It is in the presence of the cat that the mouse must not saunter.

sentences.text: Ojú tí kì í wo iná, tí kì í wo òòrùn; ojú tí ń báni dalẹ́ kọ́.
sentences.en: Eyes that cannot stand lamplight, and that cannot stand sunlight, are not eyes that will last one until the twilight of one's life.

sentences.en: The eyes that will last one until night time will not start oozing matter at the dawn.

sentences.en: Water is the first thing one's foot encounters before it encounters the sand.

sentences.en: The favor was excessive; it was repaid with wickedness.

sentences.en: It is the person in a hurry who studies the complexion of the day.

sentences.text: Àṣá ò gbádìẹ níkọ̀kọ̀; gbangba làṣá ń gbádìẹ.
sentences.en: The kite does not snatch chicks in secret, it snatches them openly.

sentences.text: Àṣá ò lè balẹ̀ kó gbéwúrẹ́.
sentences.en: The kite cannot swoop down and carry off a goat.

sentences.text: Àṣá wo ahun títí; àwòdí wo ahun títí; idì baba àṣá, kí ló lè fi ahun ṣe?
sentences.en: The kite looks long at the tortoise; the eagle looks long at the tortoise; what can the hawk, father of the kite, do to the tortoise?

sentences.text: Àṣá wo ìgbín kọ̀rọ̀; ìkaraun-un rẹ̀ ò jẹ́ kó gbé e.
sentences.en: The kite looks slyly at the snail, but its shell stops the bird from snatching it.

sentences.text: Àṣá wọ̀bọ kò rọ́wọ́ gbé e.
sentences.en: The kite watches the monkey but has no hands to carry it off.

sentences.text: Àṣírí ìkokò, ajá kọ́ ni yó tùú u.
sentences.en: The secrets of the hyena's being will not be revealed through the actions of the dog.

sentences.text: Àtẹ́lẹwọ́ ẹni kì í tanni.
sentences.en: One's palm does not deceive one.

sentences.text: Àyè kì í há adìẹ kó má dèé ìdí àbaa rẹ̀.
sentences.en: The space is never so tight that a chicken will not be able to reach its incubating nest.

sentences.text: Bí a bá ń pa èpo oṣè, ṣe ní ń máaá sanra sí i.
sentences.en: The more one peels the bark of the baobab, the fatter it becomes.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá jìyà tó kún agbọ̀n; a ò lè jẹ oore tó kún ahá.
sentences.en: If one does not experience enough suffering to fill a basket, one cannot enjoy enough good to fill a cup.

sentences.text: Bí a kò bá ṣe bí ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ lọ́nà Ìkòròdú, a ò lè ṣe bí Adégbọrọ̀ lọ́jà ọba.
sentences.en: If one does not act like a pig on the way to Ikòròdú one cannot act like Adégbọrọ̀at the king's market.

sentences.text: Bí ebí bá ń pa ọ̀lẹ, à jẹ́ kó kú.
sentences.en: If a lazy person is suffering from hunger, he/she should be left to die.

sentences.text: Bí ẹkẹ́ẹ tálákà ò tó lówùúrọ̀, á tó lálẹ́.
sentences.en: If a poor person's forked stake is not long enough in the morning, it will be long enough at night.

sentences.text: Bí ẹnìkan ò kíni “Kú-ù-jokòó,” kíkí Ọlọ́run-ún ju ti igba èèyàn lọ.
sentences.en: If a person does not extend greetings to one, God's greetings are worth more than two hundred peoples'.

sentences.text: Bí ẹrú yó bàá jẹ ìfun, ibi ẹ̀dọ̀ níí tí ń bẹ̀rẹ̀.
sentences.en: A slave that would eat intestines must begin with the liver.

sentences.text: Bí ẹ̀yá bá dẹkùn, ẹran ní ńpajẹ.
sentences.en: When the cub becomes a grown leopard, it kills animals for food.

sentences.text: Bí ìbí bá tẹ̀, bí ìbí bá wọ́, oníkálukú a máa ṣe baba nílé araa rẹ̀.
sentences.en: If the pedigree is bent, if the pedigree is crooked, each person will play the father in his own home.

sentences.text: Bí ilẹ̀ẹ́ bá mọ́, ojú orun lọ̀lẹ ń wà.
sentences.en: When day breaks the lazy person will still be asleep.

sentences.text: Bí iná kò bá tán láṣọ, ẹ̀jẹ̀ kì í tán léèékánná.
sentences.en: If lice are not completely gone from one's clothings, one's nails will not be free of blood.

sentences.text: Bí iwájú ò bá ṣeé lọ sí, ẹ̀yìn a ṣeé padà sí.
sentences.en: If one cannot go forward, one will be able to retreat.

sentences.text: Bí màlúù tó màlúù, ọ̀pá kan ni Fúlàní fi ń dà wọ́n.
sentences.en: However numerous the cattle might be, it is with only one staff that the Fulbe man herds them.

sentences.text: Bí ó pẹ́ títí, akólòlò á pe baba.
sentences.en: However long it may take, the stammarer will eventually say, “Father.”

sentences.text: Bí ó pẹ́ títí, àlejò á di onílé.
sentences.en: In time, a sojourner becomes a native.

sentences.text: Bí ó ti wuni là ń ṣe ìmàle ẹni; bó wu Lèmó̩mù a fẹlẹ́dẹ̀ jẹ sààrì.
sentences.en: One practices one's Islam as one pleases; if the Imam wishes he may break his fast with pork.

sentences.text: Bí Ògún ẹní bá dánilójú, à fi gbárí.
sentences.en: If one is sure of one's Ògún cult object, one taps ones head with it.

sentences.text: Bí ojú kò pọ́nni bí osùn, a kì í he ohun pupa bí idẹ.
sentences.en: If one's eyes do not become as red as camwood stain, one does not come by something as red as brass.

sentences.text: Bí ojú owó ẹni ò yóni, ènì ò lè yóni.
sentences.en: If what one bought for one's money does not fill one, the little extra thrown into the bargain will not.

sentences.text: Bí ojúmọ́ mọ́ lékèélékèé a yalé ẹlẹ́fun, agbe a yalé aláró, àlùkò a yalé olósùn.
sentences.en: When day dawns the cattle egret makes for the home of the dealer in chalk, the blue touraco heads for the home of the indigo dealer, the purple àlúkò bird seeks out the dealer in camwood resin.

sentences.text: Bí ọwọ́ kò sin ilẹ̀, tí kò sin ẹnu, ayo ní ń jẹ́.
sentences.en: If the hand does not cease going down and going to the mouth, satiation results.

sentences.text: Bí Ṣàǹgó bá ńpa àràbà, tó ń pa ìrókò, bíi tigi ńlá kọ́.
sentences.en: Even though Ṣango kills the silk-cotton tree and kills the ìrókò tree, no such fate can befall the huge tree.

sentences.text: Dàńdógó kì í ṣe ẹ̀wù ọmọdé.
sentences.en: Dàńdógò is not a garment for the young.

sentences.text: Dídán là ń dán ọ̀ràn wò; bí olówó ẹní kú, à lọ ṣúpó.
sentences.en: One should give everything a try; if one's owner dies one goes to claim his wife.

sentences.text: Dídán lẹyẹlé ń dán kú.
sentences.en: A perpetually shining appearance is what chracterizes the pigeon even until death.

sentences.text: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ leku ń jawọ.
sentences.en: It is bit by bit that rats eat leather.

sentences.text: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ lẹyẹ ń mu ọsàn.
sentences.en: It is bit by bit that a bird eats an orange.

sentences.text: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ ní ń tánṣẹ́.
sentences.en: Gradual efforts complete a task.

sentences.text: Dùndún fọ̀ràn gbogbo ṣàpamọ́ra.
sentences.en: The talking drum endures all matters without complaint.

sentences.text: Ebè kan ṣoṣo àkùrọ́ kúrò ní “Mo fẹ́rẹ̀ẹ́ ṣíwọ́.”
sentences.en: A single heap on the farm does not warrant “I am just about done.”

sentences.text: Ebi ni yó kọ̀ọ́ wèrè lọ́gbọ́n.
sentences.en: It is hunger that will force sense into the imbecile.

sentences.text: Ebí ń pa ejò, ahún ń yan.
sentences.en: The snake is hungry, and the tortoise saunters by.

sentences.text: Ebi ò jẹ́ ká pa ọwọ́ mọ́; ebí ṣenú papala.
sentences.en: Hunger keeps one from folding one's hands; hunger causes the mouth “or cheeks” to shrink.

sentences.text: Èébú kì í so.
sentences.en: Insults do not attach to one's body like pods.

sentences.text: Èdì kì í mú ọjọ́ kó má là.
sentences.en: No charm can act upon the day and keep it from dawning.

sentences.text: Eégún tí ń jẹ orí ẹṣin, orí àgbò ò lè kò ó láyà.
sentences.en: The masquerader who is accustomed to eating horse heads will not be daunted by ram heads.

sentences.text: Èkó ilá gba ara ẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ ọ̀bẹ.
sentences.en: Okro that has gone fibrous has delivered itself from the knife.

sentences.text: Èminrin ń jẹni, kò tó ìyà.
sentences.en: Being bothered by sandflies is no misfortune.

sentences.text: Èpè ìbínú ò pa odì.
sentences.en: An angry curse does not kill an enemy.

sentences.text: Èpè ìlasa kì í ja àgbọ̀nrín.
sentences.en: The curses of okro leaves do not affect the deer.

sentences.text: Èpò ìbúlẹ̀ kì í pa irẹ́.
sentences.en: Creeping weeds cannot kill the silk rubber tree.

sentences.text: Eṣú jẹ oko tán eṣù lọ; eṣú lọ Wata, ilée rẹ̀.
sentences.en: The locusts are done feeding, the locusts have departed; the locusts have gone to Wata, their home.

sentences.text: Èèwọ̀ ni tọwọ̀; a kì í figi ọwọ̀ dáná.
sentences.en: As far as the broom is concerned it is taboo: one does not make kindling of broomsticks.

sentences.text: Ewu iná kì í pa àwòdì.
sentences.en: The African black kite is never killed in a brushfire emergency.

sentences.text: Ewúrẹ́ ń ṣọdún, àgùtán gbàlù sẹ́yìn, òbúkọọ́ ní ká sin òun lọ sílé àna òun.
sentences.en: The goat is celebrating an event, the sheep is in a procession with drums, and the he-goat asks to be accompanied to its in-law's home.

sentences.text: Ewúrẹ́ ò lè rí ewé ọdán òkè fi ṣe nǹkan.
sentences.en: A goat can in no wise take the fig tree's leaves aloft for any purpose.

sentences.text: Ewúro ò fi tojo korò.
sentences.en: The bitter-leaf did not become bitter as a result of cowardice.

sentences.text: Èèyàn ìbáà kúrú, ìbáà búrẹ́wà, gbèsè ò sí, ìtìjú ò sí.
sentences.en: Whether a person be short or ugly, if there is no debt, there can be no disgrace.

sentences.text: Ẹbọ jíjẹ kì í pa igún.
sentences.en: The consumption of sacrificial offerings will not kill the vulture.

sentences.text: Ẹgbẹ̀rún eèrà ò lè gbé ṣúgà; wọ́n ó kàn tò yí i ká lásán ni.
sentences.en: A thousand ants cannot lift “a cube of” sugar; they can only mill around it in vain.

sentences.text: Ẹgbẹ̀rún ẹja ò lè dẹ́rù pa odò.
sentences.en: A thousand fishes will not overload a river.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀yìn ológbò kì í balẹ̀.
sentences.en: A cat's back never touches the ground.

sentences.text: Ẹjọ́ ẹlẹ́jọ́, lọ́yà ń rò ó, áḿbọ̀ǹtorí ẹjọ́ araa rẹ̀.
sentences.en: The lawyer argues other people's cases, much more his own.

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́mùn-ún ò mú eégún.
sentences.en: An apprehender does not apprehend a masquerader.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀lúlùú ní kàkà kí òun má dun ọbẹ̀, òun á rúnwọ rúnsẹ̀ sí i.
sentences.en: The larkheeled Cuckoo vows that rather than not being delicious in the stew, it will crush its arms and legs in pursuit of that end.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀lukú tí kò ní èlè lẹgbẹ́ẹ rẹ̀ ń ṣá pa.
sentences.en: It is the Ẹ̀lukú masquerader without a matchete that is hacked to death by its colleagues.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá ń ṣiṣẹ́ kì í ṣọ̀lẹ; bórí bá túnniṣe a kì í tẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
sentences.en: Whoever has a job should not malinger; if Providence smiles on one one can hardly fail.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá ń jẹ òbúkọ tó gbójú, yó jẹ àgùtàn tó yọ̀wo.
sentences.en: Whoever is used to eating full-grown he-goats will eat lambs that have sprouted horns.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá yẹ ọ̀nà Ìjẹ̀bú tì ni yó yẹ̀ ẹ́ tán.
sentences.en: The same person who weeds the road to Ìjẹ̀bú without carrying off the weeds will eventually remove them.

sentences.text: Ẹní gbani láya ò ní kírú ẹni má rà.
sentences.en: The person who takes one's wife cannot stop one's locust bean seeds from fermenting.

sentences.text: Ẹní máa jẹun kunkun a tìlẹ̀kùn kunkun.
sentences.en: Whoever wishes to eat heartily must lock his door firmly.

sentences.text: Ẹní máa rí àtisùn akàn á pẹ́ létí isà.
sentences.en: Whoever wishes to see a crab go to sleep will stay long by its hole.

sentences.text: Ẹní máa jẹ oyin inú àpáta kìí wo ẹnu àáké.
sentences.en: Whoever will eat the honey in a rock does not worry about the edge of the axe.

sentences.text: Ẹní máa rí àtisùn-un pẹ́pẹ́yẹ á jẹ gbèsè àdín.
sentences.en: Whoever wishes to see ducks go to sleep will go into debt paying for (fuel) oil.

sentences.text: Ẹní yára lÒgún ń gbè.
sentences.en: Ògún is on the side of the swift.

sentences.text: Ẹni èèyàn ò kí kó yọ̀; ẹni Ọlọ́run ò kí kó ṣọ́ra.
sentences.en: Whoever is shunned by people should rejoice; whoever is shunned by God should look out.

sentences.text: Ẹni ọ̀lẹ́ paá re ọ̀run òṣì; ẹni iṣẹ́ paá re ọ̀run ẹ̀yẹ.
sentences.en: Whoever dies from poverty dies a miserable death; whoever dies from work dies a noble death.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó gbálẹ̀ ni ilẹ̀ ń mọ́ fún.
sentences.en: It is for the person who sweeps the floor that the floor is clean.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bá ní ìtara ló ní àtètèbá.
sentences.en: It is the industrious person that wins the spoils.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó forí sọlẹ̀ẹ́ gbìyànjú ikú.
sentences.en: Whoever dives head first to the ground has made a creditable attempt at suicide.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí à ḿbọ́ ò mọ̀ pé ìyàn-án mú.
sentences.en: A person fed by others is never aware that there is famine.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó fò sókèé bẹ́ ijó lórí.
sentences.en: Whoever leaps up decapitates dance.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí iṣẹ́ ń paá yá ju ẹni tí ìṣẹ́ ń pa.
sentences.en: A person dying from overwork is better than a person dying of destitution.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bá pẹ́ lẹ́yìn ni à ń yọ́ omi ọbẹ̀ dè.
sentences.en: Those who arrive late are the ones who find the watery residue of the stew awaiting them.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ń gbẹ́lẹ̀ ní ń sìnkú; ẹni tí ń sunkún ariwo ló ń pa.
sentences.en: The person digging a grave is the one performing his or her funerary duties; the person crying is merely making a noise.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bá wo ojú ìyàwó ní ń mọ̀ pé ìyàwó ń sunkún.
sentences.en: Only a person who looks at the bride's face knows that the bride is crying.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ọ̀ṣọ́ bá wù kó ṣòwò; ẹni ajé yalée rẹ̀ ló gbọ́n.
sentences.en: Whoever likes fineries should engage in a trade; it is the person blessed by riches that is wise.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bá ńjẹ lábẹ́ẹ Jẹ́gẹ́dẹ́ ní ńpè é nígi àràbà.
sentences.en: Only those whose livelihood depends on Jẹgẹdẹ call him a silk cotton tree.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí kíkíi rẹ̀ ò yóni, àìkíi rẹ̀ ò lè pani lébi.
sentences.en: A person whose greetings do not fill one's stomach cannot cause one to starve by withholding the greetings.

sentences.text: Ẹnu òfìfo kì í dún yànmù-yànmù.
sentences.en: Empty mouths do not make chewing noises.

sentences.text: Ẹnú dùn-ún ròfọ́; agada ọwọ́ dùn-ún ṣánko.
sentences.en: The mouth cooks vegetable stew most expertly; the hand emulating a machete cuts a field most effortlessly.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀rù kì í ba igbó, bẹ́ẹ̀ni kì í ba odò; ẹ̀rù kì í ba ọlọ lójú ata.
sentences.en: The forest knows no fear, and neither does the river know fear; the grind-stone never shows fear in the face of pepper.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀rù kì í ba orí kó sá wọnú.
sentences.en: The head is never so frightened that it disappears into the shoulder.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀rù ogun kì í ba jagun-jagun.
sentences.en: Fear of battle never afflicts a warrior.

sentences.text: Ẹsẹ̀ kì í wúwo kí ẹlésẹ̀ má lè gbé e.
sentences.en: The feet are never so heavy that the owner cannot lift them.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀sọ̀ ẹ̀sọ̀ ni ìgbín fi ń gbà gun igi.
sentences.en: Slowly slowly is the way a snail climbs a tree.

sentences.text: Ẹṣin kì í dani kí á má tún gùn ún.
sentences.en: One does not refrain from mounting a horse that has thrown one.

sentences.text: Ẹṣin kì í já kó já èkejìi rẹ̀.
sentences.en: A horse does not get loose and stop to free its companion.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀tẹ́ bá ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: Disgrace comes upon the shiftless.

sentences.text: Ẹyẹ ò sọ fún ẹyẹ pé òkò ń bọ̀.
sentences.en: A bird does not tell a bird that a stone is on its way.

sentences.text: Fi gọ̀gọ̀ sílẹ̀ fún ọ̀dáwé; fi ọkọ sílẹ̀ fún onílara.
sentences.en: Leave the hooked stick alone for the leaf plucker; leave the husband alone for the jealous woman.

sentences.text: Fífẹ́ la fẹ́ ẹ̀fọ́ tí à ń pèé ní ọ̀rẹ́ ẹ̀kọ ti ilé ogeé tó ogeé jẹ.
sentences.en: It is only because one loves spinach that one calls it a friend of corn loaf; what the dandy has at home is enough food for him or her.

sentences.text: “Fọ́ ẹ̀kọ ká jọ mu ú,” kò tó ọkọlóbìnrin-ín ṣe ni.
sentences.en: “Prepare the corn pap and let us eat it together” is an indication that the speaker lacks what it takes to be a husband.

sentences.text: Gbẹ́dó-gbẹ́dó kan ò lè fi ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ṣe nǹkan.
sentences.en: No carver of mortars can do a thing to the banana stem.

sentences.text: Ìbẹ̀rù ejò ò jẹ́ ká tẹ ọmọ ejò mọ́lẹ̀.
sentences.en: Fear of the snake keeps one from stepping on the young of the snake.

sentences.text: Ibi gbogbo ní ń rọ àdàbà lọ́rùn.
sentences.en: Every place is hospitable and comfortable for the dove.

sentences.text: Ibi gbogbo nilẹ̀ ọ̀wọ̀.
sentences.en: Every place deserves to be treated with respect and reverence.

sentences.text: Ibi tí a ní kí gbégbé má gbèé, ibẹ̀ ní ń gbé.
sentences.en: The spot one cautions the gbégbé plant not to inhabit, there it will surely inhabit.

sentences.text: Ibi tí a ní kí tẹ̀tẹ̀ má tẹ̀, ibẹ̀ ní ń tẹ̀.
sentences.en: Wherever one orders wild spinach not to step on, there it will surely trample.

sentences.text: Ibo ni imú wà sẹnu? Ibo ni Làǹlátẹ̀ẹ́ wà sí Èrúwà?
sentences.en: How much distance exists between the nose and the mouth? How much distance exists between Làǹlátẹ̀ and Èrúwà?

sentences.text: Idà kì í lọ kídà má bọ̀.
sentences.en: The sword never departs without returning.

sentences.text: Ìdẹra ò kan àgbà.
sentences.en: Ease has nothing to do with age.

sentences.text: Igúnnugún pa guuru mádìẹ; kò leè gbe.
sentences.en: The vulture rushes at the chicken, but it cannot carry it off.

sentences.text: Igba eṣinṣin kì í dènà de ọwọ̀.
sentences.en: Two hundred flies will not lie in ambush for a broom.

sentences.text: Igba ẹranko kì í dènà de ẹkùn.
sentences.en: Two hundred animals will not lie in ambush for a leopard.

sentences.text: Ìgbà yí làárọ̀? Arúgbó ń kọgba.
sentences.en: Is it just morning now? The old man is striving to make two hundred heaps a day.

sentences.text: Ìgbà yí làárọ̀? Arúgbó ń ṣoge.
sentences.en: Is it just morning now? The old person is grooming himself/herself.

sentences.text: Ìgbé a gbé ìyàwó kò ṣéé gbé owó.
sentences.en: The strategy one adopts in acquiring a wife will not do with regard to money.

sentences.text: Igbe kí-ni-ngó-jẹ-sùn ní ḿpọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: The cry “What shall I eat for supper?” is what kills the lazy person.

sentences.text: Ìgbín kì í tẹnu mọ́gi kó má gùn ún.
sentences.en: The snail will not fasten unto a tree and fail to climb it.

sentences.text: Ìgbín kọ mímì ejò.
sentences.en: The snail rejects the fate of being swallowed by a snake.

sentences.text: Ìjà ò mọ ẹ̀gbọ́n, ó sọ àbúrò dakin.
sentences.en: Fighting knows not who is the elder; it makes a hero of the younger.

sentences.text: Ìje òun oore ní ń mú ọmọ ṣiṣẹ́.
sentences.en: Competition and reward are the inducements for a child to work hard.

sentences.text: Ìjèṣà ò nídìi ìṣáná; ilé lọmọ Ọwá ti ń fọnná lọ sóko.
sentences.en: The Ìjèṣà (person) does not need matches; it is from the home that the scion of Ọwa takes burning faggots to the farm.

sentences.text: Ìjẹkújẹ kì í pa ahanrandi.
sentences.en: Careless eating does not kill the worm ahanrandi.

sentences.text: Ikán ò lè rí ṣe lára ìgànná.
sentences.en: The termite can have no adverse effect on a wall.

sentences.text: Ìkòkò tí yó jẹ ata, ìdí ẹ̀ á gbóná.
sentences.en: The pot that wishes to eat pepper (stew) will first endure a scalded bottom.

sentences.text: Ìkọ́ kì í kọ́ ejò lẹ́sẹ̀.
sentences.en: A snare never catches a snake in the leg.

sentences.text: Ikọ̀ tí ò mọ iṣẹ́ẹ́ jẹ́ ní ń jẹ́ ẹ lẹ́ẹ̀mejèe.
sentences.en: It is the messenger who does not know how to deliver a message properly that delivers it seven times over.

sentences.text: Ilá kì í ga ju akórè lọ kó má tẹ̀ ẹ́ ká.
sentences.en: The okro plant is never so much taller than the harvester that he/she cannot bend it to harvest.

sentences.text: Ilé tí a tóó kun, a kì í bo ìtùfùu rẹ̀.
sentences.en: A house one is in a position to burn, one does not conceal the torch to set it ablaze.

sentences.text: Ilé tí a tó lọ sùn lọ́sàn-án, a kì í tó òru lọ sùn ún.
sentences.en: A house one has the right to sleep in during the day, one does not wait for the cover of night to go sleep in it.

sentences.text: Ìlérí adìẹ, asán ni lójú àwòdì.
sentences.en: The chicken's boasts are unavailing before the kite.

sentences.text: Ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ẹ́ gbé orí àtẹ wu ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: Beads remain on the display tray and from there attract the admiration of the feckless person.

sentences.text: Ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò yí olè lójú.
sentences.en: Frogs' eggs do not attract the attention of the thief.

sentences.text: Ìlọrin ò lóòṣà; ẹnu lòòṣà Ìlọrin.
sentences.en: The Ilorin person has no god;; his/her mouth is his/her god.

sentences.text: Iná kì í jó kí ògiri sá.
sentences.en: Fire does not rage and cause a wall to flee.

sentences.text: Iná kì í jó kó wọlé akàn.
sentences.en: A fire does not rage and enter the home of the crab.

sentences.text: Ìpa à ń poṣè ara ló fi ńsan.
sentences.en: Our attempt to kill the oṣè tree only makes it fatter.

sentences.text: Ìpẹ̀ta lọṣẹ àpọ́n.
sentences.en: The sap of the violet tree is what the bachelor uses for soap.

sentences.text: Ìpilẹ̀ ọrọ̀ọ́ lẹ́gbin.
sentences.en: The beginning of wealth is chock-full of filth.

sentences.text: Ìpọ́njú àgbẹ̀ ò ju ọdún kan.
sentences.en: A farmer's suffering will not last longer than a year.

sentences.text: Ìpọ́njú lọmọdé fi ń kọ́Fá, ìgbẹ̀yìn-in rẹ̀ a dẹni.
sentences.en: A child's learning of Ifá is full of privations, but the outcome is a life of ease.

sentences.text: Ire tí ọwọ́ọ̀ mi ò tó, ma fi gọ̀ǹgọ̀ fà á.
sentences.en: The good my hand cannot reach, I will pull down with a hooked stick.

sentences.text: Ìrèké ti ládùn látọ̀run.
sentences.en: The sugar-cane came with its sweetness from heaven.

sentences.text: Ìríkúrìí kì í fọ́ ojú.
sentences.en: Evil sights do not make the eyes go blind.

sentences.text: Irínwó ẹfọ̀n, ẹgbẹ̀rin ìwo, ogún-un Fúlàní, ójìi bàtà; Ògídíolú ò wẹ̀yìn tó fi lé Adalo lùgbẹ́.
sentences.en: Four hundred buffaloes with eight hundred horns, twenty Fulbe men and forty shoes; Ògídíolú did not look back until he had chased Adalo into the bush.

sentences.text: Ìròjú baba ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: Shirking work “is the” father of laziness.

sentences.text: Ìrókò o-nígun-mẹ́rìn-dín-lógún ò tó erin-ín gbémì, áḿbọ̀ǹtorí ìtóò a-lara-boro-boro.
sentences.en: An ìrókò stick with sixteen edges is nothing for an elephant to swallow, much less the melon fruit with a smooth body.

sentences.text: Ìrònú ìkokò ní yó pa ajá.
sentences.en: Worrying about the wolf is what will kill the dog.

sentences.text: Ìrọ́jú ni ohun gbogbo; ojoojúmọ́ ní ń rẹni.
sentences.en: Perseverance is everything; one gets tired daily.

sentences.text: Ìsàlẹ̀ ọrọ̀ọ́ lẹ́gbin.
sentences.en: The dregs of wealth is filthy.

sentences.text: Isán ń bọ́jú, ìtàlá ń wẹsẹ̀.
sentences.en: Nine days wash the face, thirteen days wash the feet.

sentences.text: Iṣẹ́ ajé le, ó tó ọpa.
sentences.en: Gainful employment is tough, as tough as a supple pole.

sentences.text: Ìṣẹ́ kì í ṣe ohun àmúṣeré; ìyà kì í ṣe ohun àmúṣàwàdà.
sentences.en: Destitution is not something to treat with levity; misery is nothing to joke about.

sentences.text: Iṣẹ́ loògùn ìṣẹ́.
sentences.en: Work is the antidote for destitution.

sentences.text: Ìṣẹ́ ń ṣẹ́ ọ ò ń rojú; ta ni yó fùn-ún ọ ni oògùn-un rẹ̀?
sentences.en: Destitution grips you and you sit scowling; who will give you the antidote?

sentences.text: Ìṣẹ́ ò gbẹ́kún, ebí jàre ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: Destitution does not yield to tears; hunger has a claim on the shiftless.

sentences.text: Iṣẹ́ ọ̀gẹrọ̀ lọ̀lẹ́ mọ̀ọ́ ṣe; kò jẹ́ wá iṣẹ́ agbára.
sentences.en: The lazy person knows how to do only things that call for little effort; he/she never seeks out work that demands strength.

sentences.text: Iṣẹ́-ajé-ò-gbé-bòji, ọmọ ẹ̀ Òjíkùtù.
sentences.en: Gainful-work-does-not-keep-to-the-shade; his/her child is named First-up-at-dawn.

sentences.text: Iṣu àtẹnumọ́ kì í jóná; ọ̀kà àtẹnumọ́ kì í mẹrẹ; àwòdì kì í gbé adìẹ à-tẹnu-kunkun-mọ́.
sentences.en: The yam one does not stop speaking about will not get burnt; the corn-meal one speaks constantly about does not become too well-done; a chicken that is the subject of constant caution does not get snatched up by a hawk.

sentences.text: Iṣu ẹni kì í fini pe ọmọdé kó má ta.
sentences.en: One's yam will not because one is only a youth refuse to grow to maturity.

sentences.text: Iṣú wà lọ́wọ́ ẹ; ọ̀bẹ́ wà lọ́wọ́ ẹ.
sentences.en: The yam is in your hand, and the knife is in your hand.

sentences.text: Ìwà ọ̀lẹ ń ba ọ̀lẹ lẹ́rù; ọ̀lẹ́ pàdánù, ó ní aráyé ò fẹ́ràn òun.
sentences.en: The lazy person's character fills him/her with fear; the lazy person loses all and complains that the world hates him/her.

sentences.text: Ìwòyí èṣí ewùràa babaà mí ti ta; ìrègún rere ò sí níbẹ̀.
sentences.en: “By this time last year my father's water-yam had grown huge”; that is nothing good to reminisce about.

sentences.text: Ìyà tó ń jẹ ọ̀lẹ ò kéré; a-lápá-má-ṣiṣẹ́.
sentences.en: The malaise that afflicts the lazy person is not trifling; one-who-has-arms-that-will-not-work.

sentences.text: Ìyànjú là ń gbà; bí a ò gbìyànjú bí ọ̀lẹ là ń rí; ojoojúmọ́ ní ń rẹni.
sentences.en: One simply makes an effort; if one does not make an effort one seems like a shiftless person; one copes with weariness daily.

sentences.text: Ìyáwọ́, ìyásẹ̀ lajá fi ń pa ehoro; wàrà-wàrà lẹkùn ń gùn.
sentences.en: Nimble hands and nimble feet make it possible for a dog to kill a rabbit; the leopard attacks its prey with lightning speed.

sentences.text: Jagajìgì ò mọ ogun; ogun ń pa elégbèje àdó.
sentences.en: Loading the body down with charms has no effect in a war; war kills even the person carrying fourteen hundred juju gourdlets.

sentences.text: Kàkà kí ilẹ̀ kú, ṣíṣá ni yó ṣàá.
sentences.en: Rather than die, the earth will only become bare.

sentences.text: Kì í kan ẹni ká yẹrí.
sentences.en: When a duty comes to one's turn one does not duck it.

sentences.text: Kí á gbé ọkọ́ so sájà ká pète ìmẹ́lẹ́; ojúgun-ún yó tán ó fikùn sẹ́yìn.
sentences.en: Hiding the hoe in the loft and contriving to shirk work; the shin ate its fill and developed a stomach at its back.

sentences.text: Kí á ránni níṣẹ́ ò tó ká mọ̀ ọ́ jẹ́.
sentences.en: To be sent on an errand is nothing compared to knowing how to carry it out.

sentences.text: Kí á tó bí ọmọdé, ẹnìkan là ń bá ṣeré.
sentences.en: Before the child was born, one had someone as a playmate.

sentences.text: Kí eégún tó dé lAlágbaàá ti ń fọ̀lẹ̀lẹ̀ jẹ̀kọ.
sentences.en: Long before the arrival of masqueraders the Alágbaà had been eating corn-meal with steamed bean loaves.

sentences.text: Kì í rẹ òòrẹ̀ kó rẹ sinsin ìdí ẹ̀.
sentences.en: The porcupine may tire, but never the quills at its rear.

sentences.text: Kì í tán nígbá osùn ká má rìí fi pa ọmọ lára.
sentences.en: The calabash of camwood is never so empty that one does not find enough in it to rub on a baby.

sentences.text: Kí ni eégún ń wò tí kò fi òwúrọ̀ jó?
sentences.en: What was the masquerader looking at that he did not take advantage of the morning to dance?

sentences.text: Kí ní ń bẹ nínú isà tí yó ba òkú lẹ́rù?
sentences.en: What is there in the grave to frighten a corpse?

sentences.text: Kí ni ọmọ ẹyẹ ó ṣe fún ìyá ẹ̀ ju pé kó dàgbà kó fò lọ?
sentences.en: What will a nestling do for its mother other than becoming mature and flying away?

sentences.text: Kí òyìnbó tó dé la ti ń wọ aṣọ.
sentences.en: Long before the white man came we were wearing clothes.

sentences.text: Kíkú ajá, n kò ní omitooro ẹ̀ẹ́ lá; àìkú ẹ̀ n kò ní pè é rán níṣẹ́.
sentences.en: When the dog dies I will not lick the stew made with it; alive I will not send it on an errand.

sentences.text: Kìnnìún ò níí ṣàgbákò ẹkùn.
sentences.en: A lion does not face peril from a leopard.

sentences.text: Kò ka ikú: àdàbà sùú-sùú tí ń jẹ̀ láàrin àṣá.
sentences.en: It fears not death: the pigeon that forages among hawks.

sentences.text: Kò sí alápatà tí ń pa igún.
sentences.en: There is no butcher who slaughters the vulture for sale.

sentences.text: Kò sí bí igbó ṣe lè ta kókó tó, erin óò kọjá.
sentences.en: No matter how knotty the bush might be, the elephant will find a way through it.

sentences.text: Kò sí èrè nínúu “Gba owó kà.”
sentences.en: There is no profit in “Take this money and count it “for me”.”

sentences.text: Kò sí ewu lóko, àfi gìrì àparò.
sentences.en: There is no danger on the farm except for the sudden noise of partridges taking to the air.

sentences.text: Kò sí ẹni tí Ọlọ́run ò ṣe fún, àfi ẹni tó bá ní tòun ò tó.
sentences.en: There is no one to whom God has not been generous, only those who will say he has not been generous enough.

sentences.text: Kò sí ibi tí kò gba ọ̀gọ̀; ọ̀lẹ layé ò gbà.
sentences.en: There is no place where a fool is not welcome; the world rejects only shiftless people.

sentences.text: Kò sí ibi tí ọwọ́-ọ̀jà erin ò tó.
sentences.en: There is no place an elephant's trunk cannot reach.

sentences.text: Kò sí ikú tí kò rọ adìẹ lọ́rùn.
sentences.en: There is no manner of death that is inconvenient for the chicken.

sentences.text: Kò sí ohun tí ń ti òkè bọ̀ tí ilẹ̀ ò gbà.
sentences.en: There is nothing dropping from above that the earth cannot withstand.

sentences.text: Kò sí oúnjẹ tí ń mú ara lókun bí èyí tí a jẹ sẹ́nu ẹni lọ.
sentences.en: There is no food that nourishes one's body like that one puts in one's own mouth.

sentences.text: Kọ̀ǹkọ̀ṣọ̀ọ́ ní bí a ti ṣe òun tó yìí, òún ṣì ń ku èlùbọ́.
sentences.en: The sieve says despite all that has been done to it it still manages to sift yam-flour.

sentences.text: Kùtù-kùtù kì í jíni lẹ́ẹ̀mejì; kùtù-kùtù ní ń jẹ́ òwúrọ̀; biri ní ń jẹ́ alẹ́.
sentences.en: Early dawn does not wake one twice; early dawn is the morning; deep darkness is night.

sentences.text: Labẹ́-labẹ́ ò bá tìjà wá odò; kanna-kánná ò bá ti ẹ̀kọ wá oko.
sentences.en: The labẹ́labẹ́  plant did not come to the river looking for a fight; the crow did not come to the farm in search of corn gruel.

sentences.text: Labẹ́-labẹ́ ò bẹ̀rù ìjà.
sentences.en: The labẹ́labẹ́ plant is not afraid of a fight.

sentences.text: Lékèélékèé gbàràdá, ó gba tẹlòmíràn mọ.
sentences.en: The cattle egret borrows wonders to perform, and performs enough for itself and others.

sentences.text: Lójú-lójú là ń wo ẹni tí a óò kéwì fún.
sentences.en: It is directly in the eyes that one looks at the subject of the praise poem one is performing.

sentences.text: Máà gbíyè lógún; ti ọwọ́ ẹni ní ń tóni.
sentences.en: Place not your hopes in inheritance; the product of one's hand labor is what sustains one.

sentences.text: “Má kọjá mi Olùgbàlà” kì í ṣe orin à-kúnlẹ̀-kọ.
sentences.en: “Pass me not by, dear Redeemer” is not a song one sings on one's knees.

sentences.text: Màrìwò ò wí fúnra wọn tẹ́lẹ̀ tí wọ́n fi ń yọ.
sentences.en: Palm fronds do not consult with one another before they sprout.

sentences.text: Màrìwò ò wojú ẹnìkan, àfi Ọlọ́run.
sentences.en: Palm fronds look up to no one except God.

sentences.text: “Mo ṣe é tán” ló níyì; a kì í dúpẹ́ aláṣekù.
sentences.en: “I have completed the job” is what deserves praise; one does not thank people who leave a job only half done.

sentences.text: Ní inú ẹ̀gún, ní inúu gọ̀gọ̀, ọmọ ayò a ṣara bòró.
sentences.en: In the midst of thorns, in the midst of crooked twigs, the ayò seeds remain smooth.

sentences.text: Ní inú òfíì àti ọ̀láà, ọmọ páńdọ̀rọ̀ ń gbó.
sentences.en: Despite being blown hither and tither in the gale, the fruits of the sausage tree survive to maturity.

sentences.text: Ní inú òwú la ti ń bù ṣènì òwú.
sentences.en: It is out of one's stock of cotton that one takes some for makeweight.

sentences.text: Ní teere, ní tèèrè, Ṣàngó ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀ ó jó wọjà.
sentences.en: Erratically, with almost imperceptible forward movement, just so Ṣàngó danced until he was at the market.

sentences.text: Ò báà kúrú, ò báà párí, gbèsè ò sí, ẹ̀sín ò sí; onígbèsè ló lè fini ṣẹ̀sín.
sentences.en: One may be diminutive, and one may be bald, but without debt one has not earned ridicule; only one's creditor has grounds to make fun of one.

sentences.text: Ó di ọjọ́ tí àkàrà ìyá kùtà ká tó mọ ọmọ tó lè jẹ̀kọ.
sentences.en: It is only on the day when the mother's bean fritters do not sell that one knows which child can consume large quantities of corn-meal.

sentences.text: Ó gbọ́ tiyán sògìrì mọ́dìí; o gbọ́ toko sọ àdá nù.
sentences.en: On hearing about pounded yam he girded himself with cooked melon seeds for stew seasoning; on hearing about farm work he threw his cutlass away.

sentences.text: “Ó kù díẹ̀ kí n wí”: ojo ní ń ssọni da.
sentences.en: “I was just on the verge of speaking my mind”: it only makes one into a coward.

sentences.text: Ó ní ibi tí ó ń dé, itọ́-dídámì nínú ààwẹ̀.
sentences.en: It goes some way “in assuaging hunger”, saliva swallowing during a fast.

sentences.text: O ní kí o gbó ogbó Olúàṣo; o lè jìyà bí Olúàṣo?
sentences.en: You pray to live as long as Olúàṣo, but can you endure the trials of Olúàṣo?

sentences.text: Ó pa obì, ó yọ abidún-un rẹ̀.
sentences.en: He split the kolanut pod open and also removed the bad among the seeds.

sentences.text: Obìnrin tí yó fẹ̀ẹ́ alágbára, ọkàn kan ní ń mú.
sentences.en: A woman who would marry a formidable man must have an unwavering mind.

sentences.text: Òbúrẹ́wà ẹni, tòrìṣà ni; àìraṣọlò, tolúwarẹ̀ ni.
sentences.en: A person's ugliness is the god's doing; the person's lack of clothing is his/her own fault.

sentences.text: Odídẹrẹ́ kì í kú sóko ìwájẹ.
sentences.en: The parrot never dies in the grazing field.

sentences.text: Odò kì í kún bo ẹja lójú.
sentences.en: A river does not so swell as to be over the head of the fish.

sentences.text: Odò tí a bá mọ orísun ẹ̀ kì í gbéni lọ.
sentences.en: A river whose source one knows does not carry one away.

sentences.text: Odó tó bá tojú ẹni kún kì í gbéni lọ.
sentences.en: A river that swells in one's presence does not carry one away.

sentences.text: Oògùn kì í gbé inú àdó jẹ́.
sentences.en: A magical charm does not work from within its gourdlet.

sentences.text: Ogun kì í jà kó wọlé Asẹ́yín.
sentences.en: War does not rage and destroy the home of the Asẹ́yìn.

sentences.text: Ogun kì í rí ẹ̀yìn ogun.
sentences.en: An army does not see the rear of an(other) army.

sentences.text: Ogún ọdún tí ebí ti ń pa ọ̀gà, ìrìn-in fàájì ò padà lẹ́sẹ̀ẹ rẹ̀.
sentences.en: In all the twenty years that the cameleon has been in the throes of hunger, its dignified gait has not deserted it.

sentences.text: Ògbógbó àwọ̀n ní ń bi ajáko.
sentences.en: It is a mighty net that can trip the civet-cat.

sentences.text: Ohun kan ladìẹ ń jẹ kágbàdo tó dé.
sentences.en: The chicken had something to eat before there was corn.

sentences.text: Ohun tí a bá gbìn sẹ́yìn la ó padà bá.
sentences.en: Whatever one sows behind one is what one will return to find.

sentences.text: Ohun tí a fún ẹ̀ṣọ́ ṣọ́ ni ẹ̀ṣọ́ ń ṣọ́.
sentences.en: Whatever one hands to a warrior to look after is what he looks after.

sentences.text: Ohun títán lọdún eégún.
sentences.en: The annual egúngún festival is not endless.

sentences.text: Òjìji ò bẹ̀rù ọ̀fìn.
sentences.en: The shadow has no fear of the gully.

sentences.text: Òjìji; ṣe lẹ́gẹ́-lẹ́gẹ́ má wòó.
sentences.en: The shadow lacks substance but it never crashes.

sentences.text: Òjò ìbá rọ̀, kí ladẹ́tẹ̀ ìbá gbìn? Ọwọ́ adẹ́tẹ̀ ò ká ẹyọ àgbàdo mẹ́wàá.
sentences.en: Were it to rain, what would the leper have planted? A leper's palm cannot scoop ten grains of corn.

sentences.text: Òjò pamí, òjò pa èreè mi; òjò ò pa ẹwà araà mi dànù.
sentences.en: The rain may beat me, and the rain may beat my statue; the rain cannot wash away my good looks.

sentences.text: Òjò-ó pọnmi fún ọ̀lẹ, kò ṣẹ́gi fún ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: The rain provides water for the lazy person; but it does not fetch firewood for the lazy person.

sentences.text: Òjòó pa alágùnúndì, àgúndìí domi; ìyàwó ń retí àgúndì, ọkọ́ sùn sóko.
sentences.en: Rain beats the man carrying pounded yams wrapped in leaves, the pounded yams become water-logged; the wife awaits the pounded yams, the husband sleeps on the farm.

sentences.text: Òjó jìyà gbé; alágbáraá bú u, ó gun àjà; a tọ̀ ọ́.
sentences.en: Òjó is victimized without recourse; a bully insults him, he goes to hide in the rafters, and his nemesis follows him there.

sentences.text: Òjòó pa odídẹ àlùkò ń yọ̀, àlùkòó rò pé ìkó bàjẹ́; òjó mú ìkó wọṣọ.
sentences.en: Rain beats the parrot and the touraco rejoices, thinking that the parrot's tail feather is ruined; the rain only makes the tail feather brighter.

sentences.text: Òjòjò ọ̀lẹ ò tán bọ̀rọ̀; ọ̀lẹ́ bà á tì ó dáná orí.
sentences.en: A lazy person's illness is not soon over; the lazy person finds no way out and prepares a fire to warm his head.

sentences.text: Ojú abanijẹ́ pọ́n, kò lè tan fìtílà.
sentences.en: The detractor's eyes glow red, but they cannot light a lamp.

sentences.text: “Ojú ànaà mi ò sunwọ̀n”; kò ju kó gba ọmọ ẹ̀ lọ.
sentences.en: “The look on my parent-in-law's face is baleful”; the worst he/she can do is take his/her daughter back.

sentences.text: Ojú kì í pọ́n iṣin ká má bàá wóró nínú ẹ̀.
sentences.en: The Akee apple is never so blighted that one does not find a seed in it.

sentences.text: Ojú kì í pọ́n iṣin kó má là.
sentences.en: The Akee apple is never so blighted that it does not eventually split open.

sentences.text: Ojú là ń rọ́; ògó ṣòroó ṣe.
sentences.en: One only tries one's best; heroic deeds do not come easy.

sentences.text: Ojú lakàn-án fi ń ṣọ́ orí.
sentences.en: The crab watches after its head with its eyes.

sentences.text: Ojú mẹ́wàá kò jọ ojú ẹni.
sentences.en: Ten eyes are not like one's own.

sentences.text: “Ojú ò fẹ́rakù” tí ń ta ajá ẹ lókòó; ó fowó ṣíyán jẹ.
sentences.en: “We might see each other again” who sells his dog for twenty cowries and spent the money on pounded yams to eat.

sentences.text: Ojú olójú kì í gba ọ̀ràn fúnni wò.
sentences.en: Other people's eyes will not look after matters for one.

sentences.text: Ojú olójú ò jọ ojú ẹni; a-ṣọ́ràn-deni ò wọ́pọ̀.
sentences.en: Other people's eyes are nothing like one's owń minders of other people's business are few.

sentences.text: Ojú rẹ́gbin kò fọ́: a-jọ̀pọ̀-ìyà-má-rù.
sentences.en: The eye looks on a filthy sight and does not go blind: “like” one who sustains a succession of sufferings without wasting away.

sentences.text: Ojú ti kókó, ojú ti eéwo; ojú ti aáràgbá ìdí pẹ̀lú.
sentences.en: The lump that attacks the head is shamed, the boil is shamed, and the hardened tissue on the buttocks is shames also.

sentences.text: Ojú tó ti rí gbẹ̀lẹ̀dẹ́ ti rópin ìran.
sentences.en: The eyes that have seen gbẹ̀lẹ̀dẹ́ have seen the ultimate in sights.

sentences.text: Ojú tó ti rókun ò ní rọ́sà kó bẹ̀rù.
sentences.en: The eyes that have seen the ocean will not tremble at the sight of the lagoon.

sentences.text: Ojúmọ́ kì í mọ́ kí ọwọ́ má yùn-ún ẹnu.
sentences.en: Never a day dawns that the hand does not make a trip to the mouth.

sentences.text: Ojúoró ní ń lékè omi; òṣíbàtà ní ń lékè odò.
sentences.en: The water lettuce always winds up on the surface of the water; the water-lily always wings up on the surface of the stream.

sentences.text: Òkè lẹyẹ ń fọhùn.
sentences.en: It is from aloft that the bird sounds off.

sentences.text: Òkè méjì kì í bínú ẹni; bí a bá gun ọ̀kan, à sì máa rọ ọ̀kan.
sentences.en: One cannot be bedeviled by two hills; if one ascends a hill, one descends a hill.

sentences.text: Òkété fìjà sẹ́yìn; ó dọ́jà tán ó káwọ́ lérí.
sentences.en: The giant bush rat turns its back at the place where he has a quarrel; after getting to the market it clamps its hands on its head.

sentences.text: Òkìkí ajá kì í pa oṣù.
sentences.en: A dog's howling will not kill the moon.

sentences.text: Òkìkí ò poṣù; ariwo ò pagún; ibi ẹ rí ẹ kíbòsíì mi lọ.
sentences.en: Being widely reputed does not kill the moon; being noised about does not kill the vulture; wherever you please, make a noise about me.

sentences.text: Oko etílé ladìẹ́ lè ro.
sentences.en: The chicken is good at cultivating only the soil close by the home.

sentences.text: Òkò kan igi; òkò padà sẹ́yìn kí o rebi o ti wá.
sentences.en: Stone, hit a tree, stone retrace your steps and return to whence you came.

sentences.text: Òkú ò moye à ń ràgọ̀.
sentences.en: The corpse does not know the cost of the shroud.

sentences.text: Òkú ọdún mẹ́ta kúrò ní àlejò sàréè.
sentences.en: A three-year-old corpse of is no longer a newcomer to the grave.

sentences.text: Òkú ọ̀lẹ ò ní pósí.
sentences.en: A lazy person's corpse does not merit a coffin.

sentences.text: Olójú kì í fojú ẹ̀ sílẹ̀ kí tàlùbọ́ kó wọ̀ ọ́.
sentences.en: The owner of the eyes will not neglect them and watch foreign matter lodge in them.

sentences.text: Olówó kì í fi owó ẹ̀ fún abòṣì ná.
sentences.en: The rich person will not give his/her money to a poor person to spend.

sentences.text: Olówó mọ òwò.
sentences.en: The rich person is an expert at trading.

sentences.text: Olúmọ Ẹ̀gbá ò ṣéé gbé.
sentences.en: The Olúmọ of the Ègbá territory is impossible to carry.

sentences.text: Omi adágún ò lè gbé màlúù lọ.
sentences.en: A stagnant pool cannot carry off a cow.

sentences.text: Omi ló dànù, agbè ò fọ́.
sentences.en: It is the water that is spilled; the water gourd is not broken.

sentences.text: Omi ń bẹ látọ́.
sentences.en: There is water in the long-necked calabash.

sentences.text: Omi ṣẹ́lẹ̀rú ò mu akèrègbè.
sentences.en: The water from a new spring will not cover a gourd to the top.

sentences.text: Omí wọ́ yanrìn gbẹrẹrẹ, bẹ́ẹ̀ni omi ò lọ́wọ́, omi ò lẹ́sẹ̀.
sentences.en: Water drags the sand about, and yet water lacks hands and lacks legs.

sentences.text: “Oní ló ń mọ,” ìjà ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: “It will all end some time today”: a lazy person's motto in a fight.

sentences.text: Òní, “Mò ń lọ”; ọ̀la, “Mò ń lọ,” kò jẹ́ kí àlejò gbin awùsá.
sentences.en: Today, “I am leaving”; tomorrow, “I am leaving,” prevents the sorjourner from planting awùsá.

sentences.text: Òní ọ̀wẹ̀, ọ̀la àáró; iṣẹ́ oníṣẹ́ ò jẹ́ ká ráàyè ṣe tẹni.
sentences.en: Today, a communal project; tomorrow group work on a somebody's farm; other people's work prevents one from doing one's own.

sentences.text: Oníbàjẹ́ ò lódó; ẹnu gbogbo lodóo wọn.
sentences.en: Detractors of others have no pestles; their mouths are their pestles.

sentences.text: Oníbànà ní ń tọ́jú òroǹbó; onídẹ ní ń tọ́jú awẹdẹ.
sentences.en: It is he who has copper ornaments who must procure oranges; whoever has brass ornaments must procure the herb awẹdẹ.

sentences.text: Onígbèsè èèyàn-án ti kú; a ò tíì sìnkú ẹ̀ ni.
sentences.en: The habitual debtor is already dead; except that he ha not yet been buried.

sentences.text: OníṢàngó ò mẹni tí òún ń wà lóògì dànù.
sentences.en: The Ṣàngó worshipper knows not whose ground corn he is spilling.

sentences.text: Oníṣe kì í fiṣe ẹ̀ sílẹ̀ re ibi; ó ń re àjò ó mú iṣe ẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ gírígírí.
sentences.en: The owner of a habit will not go on a journey and leave his habit at home; when he goes he takes his habit along with him.

sentences.text: Oníṣòwó wà lóòrùn; náwónáwó wà níbòji.
sentences.en: The person who does the trading is in the sun; the person who spends the money is in the shade.

sentences.text: Oníṣú fiṣu ẹ se ẹ̀bẹ; ojú ti atèèpojẹ.
sentences.en: The owner of the yams makes yam pottage out of the yams; the person who eats the yam scrapings off the peels is shamed.

sentences.text: Orí adẹ́tù ń pète àrán; orí adáràn-án ń pète àtijọba.
sentences.en: The head that wears a cloth cap strives to wear a velvet cap; the one that wears a velvet cap strives to become a king.

sentences.text: Orí iṣẹ́ laago ń kú lé.
sentences.en: It is while at work that a clock dies.

sentences.text: Orí ń lá kì í pá tán.
sentences.en: A huge head does not go completely bald.

sentences.text: Orí olórí kì í báni gbẹ́rù.
sentences.en: Other people's heads will not carry one's load for one.

sentences.text: Òrìṣà tí ń gbọ̀lẹ ò sí; apá ẹni ní ń gbeni.
sentences.en: There is no god that comes to the aid of shiftless people; only one's arms aid one.

sentences.text: Oríta mẹ́ta ò kọnnú ẹbọ.
sentences.en: A crossroads where three roads meet is not afraid of sacrificial offerings.

sentences.text: Òru ni ìnàyìn àgbẹ̀.
sentences.en: Night time is a farmer's time to stretch the back.

sentences.text: Oòrùn ò kan àtàrí, ọwọ́ ò dá.
sentences.en: The sun has not risen directly above the head; working hands cannot cease their toil.

sentences.text: Oòrùn ò pa ọ́, òjò ò pa ọ́, o ní ò ń ṣiṣẹ́ ajé.
sentences.en: The sun does not beat you, the rain does not beat you, and yet you say you are engaged in a gainful pursuit.

sentences.text: Òṣìṣẹ́ lọ̀tá ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: The industrious person is the enemy of the shiftless person.

sentences.text: Òṣìṣẹ́ wà lóòrùn; ẹní máa jẹ́ wà níbòji.
sentences.en: The laborer is in the sun; the person who will reap the fruit is in the shade.

sentences.text: Oṣù mẹ́ta lebi ń pàgbẹ̀.
sentences.en: The farmer's hunger lasts only three months.

sentences.text: Òwò àdà kì í pa àdá; òwò ọkọ́ kì í yọ ọkọ́ lẹ́nu.
sentences.en: A machete's trade does not kill the machet; a hoe's trade does not cause problems for the hoe.

sentences.text: Owó ò mọ ẹ̀gbọ́n, ó sọ àbúrò dàgbà.
sentences.en: Wealth does not know who is the elder; it makes a senior of the younger person.

sentences.text: Owó ò níran; àfi ẹni tí kò bá ṣiṣẹ́.
sentences.en: Money has no lineage; except for the person who will not work.

sentences.text: Òwò tí a bá máa ṣe àṣelà, a kì í rí àpá ẹ̀ lára ẹni.
sentences.en: The trade that one will pursue and that will make one prosper does not leave scars on one.

sentences.text: Òwò tí a ó ṣe là ń tọ́jú; Òjí fabẹ họra.
sentences.en: The trade one will pursue is the one one protects; Òjí scratches his body with a razor.

sentences.text: Owó olówó leégún ń ná.
sentences.en: Other people's money is what the masquerader spends.

sentences.text: Òyìnbó baba ọ̀nájà; ajé baba téní-téní.
sentences.en: The white man is the past master of trading; money is the guarantee of fashionableness.

sentences.text: Òyìnbó ta ọjà ta orúkẹ; Ègún tajà ta èdìdì.
sentences.en: The white man sells merchandise with the name brand still attached; the Ègùn person sells cloth still in its bundle.

sentences.text: Ọba tó fi iyùn bọlẹ̀, ọba tó wú u, àwọn méjèèjì la ó máa sọ orúkọọ wọn.
sentences.en: The king who buries coral beads, the king who digs them up, both of then will have their names remembered by posterity.

sentences.text: Ọbẹ̀ tó dùn, owó ló pa á.
sentences.en: A delicious stew was procured with money.

sentences.text: Ọbẹ̀ẹ́ tutù tán, a dawọ́ bù ú lá.
sentences.en: The stew having cooled, one hollows one's palm to eat it.

sentences.text: Ọ̀dájú ló bí owó; ìtìjú ló bí gbèsè.
sentences.en: It is brazenness that gives birth to wealth; it is excessive reticence that gives birth to poverty.

sentences.text: Ọdọọdún làgbẹ̀ ń níyì.
sentences.en: It is every year that the farmer receives praise.

sentences.text: Ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ dúdú ò ṣéé bùṣán; ọmọ burúkú ò ṣéé lù pa.
sentences.en: An unripe plantain is not something to eat; a useless child is not something to beat to death.

sentences.text: Ọgbọ́n òyìnbó ti ojú òkun là wá; aṣọ kí ni o borí akẹsẹ?
sentences.en: The white man's wisdom shines even across the seas; what cloth, though, is better than akẹsẹ cloth?

sentences.text: Ọjà tí a fowó rà, owó la fi ń pa.
sentences.en: One makes money from goods one purchased with money.

sentences.text: Ọ̀-jẹ-wọ̀mù-wọ̀mù-kú-wọ̀mù-wọ̀mù lorúkọ tí àpà ń jẹ́.
sentences.en: One-who-eats-recklessly-and-dies-recklessly is the name one calls a wasteful person.

sentences.text: Ọjọ́ a bá kọ́ ọ̀lẹ là ń kọ́ inú rírọ́.
sentences.en: The day one learns laziness is the day one should learn how to endure a painfully empty stomach.

sentences.text: Ọjọ́ a bá rí ìbí nìbí ń wọlẹ̀.
sentences.en: The day one sees the after-birth is the day it enters the earth.

sentences.text: Ọjọ́ eré lọ̀ràn ń dun ọ̀lẹ.
sentences.en: It is on the day of relaxation that the lazy person experiences regret.

sentences.text: Ọjọ́ tí a dóko là ń jìjà ilẹ̀.
sentences.en: The day one gets to the farm is the day one fights over boundaries.

sentences.text: Ọjọ́ tí a ń kọ́ṣẹ́ là ń kọ́ ìyára.
sentences.en: The day one learns a trade is the day one learns to be quick at it.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ bà á tì, ó kó sílé Ifá.
sentences.en: The lazy person fails at everything, whereupon he becomes an Ifá acolyte.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ bà á tì, ó kó sílée kéú.
sentences.en: The lazy person fails at everything, whereupon he goes to a Quaranic school.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ, baba àrùn.
sentences.en: Laziness, father of all diseases.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ èèyàn ò rí ayé wá.
sentences.en: A lazy person has found no world to come to.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ fẹ́ àrùn kù, ó bú pùrù sẹ́kún.
sentences.en: The lazy person cannot find a disease to contract, he bursts into tears.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ fi ọ̀ràn gbogbo ṣe “hòo.”
sentences.en: The lazy person replies “yes” to all propositions.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ jogún ìbànújẹ́, ó ní òún jogún ìran òun.
sentences.en: The lazy person inherits unhappiness, he says he has inherited the fate of his lineage.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ jogún ìbáwí.
sentences.en: The lazy person inherits recriminations.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ kákò, ó di òjòjò.
sentences.en: The lazy person curls up, and his condition becomes a serious ailment.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ kún àárẹ̀ lọ́wọ́.
sentences.en: Laziness lends weariness a hand.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ mọ èèwọ̀ ìjà: ó ní bàbá òún ní kóun má jà lọ́nà oko.
sentences.en: The coward knows the preventive for fighting: he says his father has ordered him not to fight on the way to the farm.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ ò yẹẹ́ ní lọ́mọ.
sentences.en: A lazy person is not something one wants as a child.

sentences.text: Ọ̀lẹ́ wáṣẹ́ rírọ̀ ṣe.
sentences.en: The lazy person seeks out an easy task to do.

sentences.text: Ọlọgbọ́n kì í kú sóko ọ̀lẹ; bí ọlọgbọ́n bá kú sóko ọ̀lẹ, ọ̀ràn náà nídìí.
sentences.en: The wise will not die on a farm for the lazy; if a wise person dies on a farm for the lazy, there must be some explanation.

sentences.text: Ọlọ́mú dá ọmú ìyá ẹ̀ gbé.
sentences.en: Each child must lift its mother's breast by itself.

sentences.text: Ọlọ́run yó pèsè; kì í ṣe bí èsè oríta.
sentences.en: The Lord will give alms, but not the type one comes upon at crossroads.

sentences.text: Ọmọ tí yó jẹ̀ẹ́ àṣàmú, kékeré ní ń tií n ṣẹnu ṣámú-ṣámú.
sentences.en: A person that will become exemplary will begin showing precociousness from childhood.

sentences.text: Ọmọ tó káwọ́ sókè ló fẹ́ ká gbé òun.
sentences.en: It is the child that lifts up its arms that induces people to lift it.

sentences.text: Ọmọ tó ṣípá fúnni là ń gbé jó.
sentences.en: It is the child that lifts its arms to one that one picks up to dance with.

sentences.text: Ọmọdé ò mọ ibi tí à ń pọn òun rè.
sentences.en: A child does not know where the person who carries it on her back is headed with it.

sentences.text: Ọ̀mu ní ń gbe ọ̀mu mì.
sentences.en: It is drunkenness that swallows (or drowns) a champion drinker.

sentences.text: Ọ̀nà kì í dí mọ́ aládàá.
sentences.en: The path does not close on a man carrying a machete.

sentences.text: Ọ̀ràn búburú kì í bá ikún nílé.
sentences.en: An evil event never finds the squirrel at home.

sentences.text: Ọrùn kì í wọ òṣùká; ẹlẹ́rù lọrùn ń wọ̀.
sentences.en: The pad placed on the head to soften the friction of the load on the head does not suffer from the weight; the person carrying the load is the one whose neck suffers under the weight.

sentences.text: Ọwọ́ atẹ́gùn ò ká gẹdú.
sentences.en: The wind is no match for timber.

sentences.text: Ọwọ́ ẹni la fi ńtú ìwà ara ẹni ṣe.
sentences.en: One's own hands are what one uses to mend one's fortune.

sentences.text: Ọwọ́ ẹni ni yó yòóni.
sentences.en: One hands are what feed one to satiation.

sentences.text: Ọwọ́ ní ń tún ara ṣe.
sentences.en: The hands are the agents for grooming the body.

sentences.text: Ọwọ́ tó dilẹ̀ là ń fi lérán.
sentences.en: It is on an idle hand that one rests one's chin.

sentences.text: Ọyẹ́ ni yó kìlọ̀ fún onítòbí.
sentences.en: It is the harmattan that will teach the person who has only a loin cloth a lesson.

sentences.text: Pà-pà lójú lẹ́ẹ̀kínní, pà-pà lójú lẹ́ẹ̀kejì; bójú náà ò bá fọ́, bàì-bàì ní ń dà.
sentences.en: A blow to the eye the first time, and a blow to the eye a second time; if the eye does not go blind it will only see dimly.

sentences.text: Páńdọ̀rọ̀ọ́ já, ará rọ ìyá ẹ̀.
sentences.en: The fruit of the sausage tree drops, “and” its mother knows relief.

sentences.text: Ṣàngó ò lè pa igi ńlá.
sentences.en: Ṣàngó cannot destroy a huge tree.

sentences.text: Ṣe kóo ní; àbá ò di tẹni; èèyàn ò ṣoògùn ọrọ̀.
sentences.en: Work in order that you might have; intentions do not become possessions; no one makes money by magic.

sentences.text: Ṣiṣeé rorò, jíjẹ ọ̀fẹ́.
sentences.en: Working is difficult; one would rather freeload.

sentences.text: Ṣòkòtò gbọọrọ ò dọlà; abíni lÉkòó ò dowó.
sentences.en: Long trousers do not amount to wealth; being born in Lagos does not ensure riches.

sentences.text: Ṣòkòtò tí ń ṣiṣẹ́ àrán, oko ní ń gbé.
sentences.en: The pants that do the work that purchases the velvet fabric stays on the farm.

sentences.text: Tàkúté tí yó pa Aláginjù á pẹ́ lóko kí wọ́n tó gbé e wálé.
sentences.en: The snare that will capture the lord of the wilderness will stay long in the bush before returning home.

sentences.text: Tàpò-tàpò là ń yọ jìgá; tewé-tewé là ń yán ẹ̀kọ.
sentences.en: With sac and all is how to remove jiggers; with its wrapping leaves is the way to buy corn meal.

sentences.text: Tẹ̀tẹ̀ ẹ̀gún ti lómi tẹ́lẹ̀ kójò tó rọ̀ sí i.
sentences.en: The prickly spinach was succulent before the rain fell on it.

sentences.text: Títa ríro là ń kọlà, bó bá jinná a di tẹni.
sentences.en: Facial scarification comes with a great deal of pain; when it heals its beauty becomes one's pride.

sentences.text: Tojú tìyẹ́ làparòó fi ń ríran.
sentences.en: It is with both its eyes and its feathers that the partridge sees.

sentences.text: Tọ̀sán tòru, imú ò gbélẹ̀; bó ba dákẹ́, a jẹ́ pé ó pin.
sentences.en: Day or night, the nose does not rest; if it stops, that means the end.

sentences.text: Wàhálà ló bí ìrọra; òṣì ló bí wàhálà.
sentences.en: Struggle gives birth to ease; destitution gives birth to struggle.

sentences.text: Wèrè èèyàn ní ń ru ẹrù wòran; ẹní ru ẹrù wòran ni wèrè èèyàn ń wò.
sentences.en: Only an imbecile carries a heavy load and stops to watch a spectacle; such a heavily-laden spectacle watcher is the sort of spectacle that attracts the attention of imbeciles.

sentences.text: Wíwẹ̀ là ń wẹ̀ ká tó jàre ọyẹ́.
sentences.en: Only by taking a cold shower can one shake off the chill of the harmattan.

sentences.text: Compare Wọ́n ní “Àwòko, o bú ọba.”
sentences.en: Previous Contents

sentences.text: A kì í pè é lẹ́rù ká pè é lọ́ṣọ̀ọ́.
sentences.en: One does not call it a burden and also call it an adornment.

sentences.text: A kì í rí ẹṣin ní ìso.
sentences.en: One does not find a horse on tether.

sentences.text: A kì í rí i ká tún sọ pé a ò ri mọ́.
sentences.en: One does not see a thing and then say one does not see it.

sentences.text: A kì í ró aṣọ ajé sídìí ká dájọ́ òdodo lẹ́bi.
sentences.en: One does not wear the ritual loincloth for presiding over a trial-by-ordeal and judge the righteous guilty.

sentences.text: A kì í so ẹran mẹ́ran kó kàn án pa.
sentences.en: One does not tie a goat with another goat and keep one from butting the other to death.

sentences.text: A kì í sọ̀rọ̀ ìkọ̀kọ̀ kó má diyàn ní gbangba.
sentences.en: One does not conspire in secret without the matter eventually causing a public argument.

sentences.text: A kì í ṣe ẹlẹ́jọ́ ní “N gbọ́?”
sentences.en: One does not ask the main litigant, “How about it?”

sentences.text: Àbàtá pani; àbàtá pani; ká ṣá sọ pé odòó gbéni lọ.
sentences.en: He died in the mire; he died in the mire; let us simply say that the person drowned.

sentences.text: Àbẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ ní ń fọ́jú onídàájọ́.
sentences.en: It is bribery that blinds a judge.

sentences.text: Adánu tí ń jẹ ilá: ó ní “Ẹ ò rí ilẹ̀ báyìí?”
sentences.en: Cleft-lipped person eating okro; he complains, “Can you believe what a mess the floor is?”

sentences.text: Àdàpè olè ní ń jẹ́ àfọwọ́rá.
sentences.en: It is simply a euphemism for theft to say àfọwọ́rá (literally, causing to disappear through the operations of the hand).

sentences.text: Àdàpè olè ní ń jẹ́ “ọmọọ̀ mi ń fẹ́wọ́.”
sentences.en: It is a euphemistic description of stealing to say, “My child's hands are uncontrollably nimble.”

sentences.text: Àdàpè ọ̀rọ̀ ò jẹ́ ká mọ ìtumọ̀ orúkọ.
sentences.en: Riddling makes it impossible for one to know the meanings of names.

sentences.text: A-dọ́gbọ́n-pàgùntàn-jẹ Ìlárá, ó ní ojú ẹ̀ ń ba òun lẹ́rù.
sentences.en: Person-who-schemes-to-kill-a-sheep-to-eat, native of Ìlárá, he says that he is afraid of its eyes.

sentences.text: Afasẹ́gbèjò ń tan araa rẹ̀ jẹ.
sentences.en: He who would collect rain water in a sieve deceives himself.

sentences.text: Afatarẹ́nilójú, alèe baále.
sentences.en: One-who-smears-one's-eyes-with-pepper, one's husband's concubine.

sentences.text: Afẹ́nilóbìnrin ò ro ire síni.
sentences.en: He-who-has-an-affair-with-one's-wife harbors no good will towards one.

sentences.text: Afìkọ̀kọ̀jalè, bí ọba ayé ò rí ọ, tọ̀rún rí ọ.
sentences.en: You-who-steal-in-secret, if an earthly king does not see you, the heavenly king sees you.

sentences.text: Afọ́jú àjànàkú, kò mọ igi, kò mọ èèyàn.
sentences.en: A blind elephant does not know a man from a tree.

sentences.text: Àfọwọ́rá ní ń jẹ́ olè.
sentences.en: Employing-the-hands-to-make-things-disappear is called stealing.

sentences.text: Agada ò morí alágbẹ̀dẹ.
sentences.en: The sword cannot tell the smith's head from others.

sentences.text: Àgbàdo kì í ṣe èèyàn; ta ní ń rí ọmọ lẹ́yìn eèsún.
sentences.en: The maize plant is not human; who ever saw children on the back of elephant grass?

sentences.text: Àgbàká lodi ń gba ìlú.
sentences.en: It is completely that a fortification wall encircles a town.

sentences.text: Àgbàká nigbà ń gba ọ̀pẹ.
sentences.en: It is completely that the climbing rope encircles the palm-tree.

sentences.text: Àgbẹ̀ gbóko róṣù.
sentences.en: A farmer stays on the farm and sees the moon.

sentences.text: A-gbẹ́jọ́-ẹnìkan-dájọ́, òṣìkà èèyàn.
sentences.en: He-who-decides-a-case-after-hearing-only-one-side, (is) the dean of wicked persons.

sentences.text: Àgbọ́ìgbọ́tán Ègùn, ìjà ní ń dá sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: Imperfect understanding of Ègùn (a language to the west of Yoruba) brings nothing but dissension.

sentences.text: Àì-fẹ́-àlejòó-ṣe là ń wí pé “Ọ̀rẹ́ ọ̀rẹ́ẹ̀ mí dé”; ká ṣáà ti wí pé, “Ọ̀rẹ́ẹ̀ mí dé.”
sentences.en: Reluctance-to-extend-hospitality makes one say, “My friend's friend has arrived”; one should simply say, “My friend has arrived.”

sentences.text: Àìfẹ̀sọ̀ké ìbòsí ni kò ṣéé gbè.
sentences.en: It is an alarm that is raised without moderation that finds no helpers.

sentences.text: Ajá tí ò létí ò ṣéé dẹ̀gbẹ́.
sentences.en: A dog without ears is no good for stalking prey.

sentences.text: Ajá ti erée rẹ̀ẹ́ bá dánilójú là ń dẹ sí ehoro.
sentences.en: It is a dog in whose speed one has faith that one sics at a hare.

sentences.text: Àjàlá, ta ní nà ọ́? Ìwọ náà kọ́ un?
sentences.en: Ajala, who whipped you? It is none other than you, isn't it?

sentences.text: Àjò àìwuniíyún là ń dÍfá sí.
sentences.en: It is a journey one does not want to make that one consults the oracle about.

sentences.text: A-kápò-má-ṣọdẹ, ọ̀tá ẹranko, ọ̀tá èèyàn.
sentences.en: He-who-carries-a-hunting-bag-but-does-not-hunt, enemy alike of man and beast.

sentences.text: Àkàsọ̀ faratilẹ̀ faratilé; bí ẹni tí a fẹ̀yìntì óò bá yẹni a wí fúnni.
sentences.en: A ladder rests on the ground and leans on the house; if the person one leans on must remove his support he should warn one.

sentences.text: Akíni ń jẹ́ akíni; afinihàn ń jẹ́ afinihàn; èwo ni “Ọ kú, ará Ìjàyè!” lójúde Ògúnmọ́lá?
sentences.en: A person that will greet one should greet one, and a person that will betray one should do so; what is the meaning of “Hello, Ìjàyè person!” before Ògúnmọ́lá's house?

sentences.text: Alákatam̀pò ò mọ irú ẹran.
sentences.en: The user of a cross-bow does not know what type of game he shoots at.

sentences.text: Alápatà ò mọ irú ẹran.
sentences.en: The butcher does not know what type the animal is.

sentences.text: Amọ̀rànbini Ọ̀yọ́, bí o bá gbé kete lérí, wọn a ní oko lò ń lọ tàbí odò.
sentences.en: People-who-know-the-answer-yet-ask-the-question, natives of Ọyọ, if they see you carrying a water-pot they ask whether you are on your way to the farm or the stream.

sentences.text: Apajájẹẹ́ ní ẹ̀rù adìẹ ń ba òun.
sentences.en: The-person-who-kills-and-eats-dogs claims to be afraid of chickens.

sentences.text: Apani kì í jẹ́ ká mú idà kọjá nípàkọ́ òun.
sentences.en: A murderer never permits the passage of a sword behind his skull.

sentences.text: Àpèjúwe lalágbẹ̀dẹ ń rọ̀.
sentences.en: The blacksmith manufactures from a description.
