sentences.text: Ará Ìbàdàn kì í ságun; à ó rìn sẹ́yìn ni wọ́n ń wí.
sentences.en: Ibadan people do not run from war; what they say is, “We will fall back a little.”

sentences.text: Arítẹnimọ̀ọ́wí, ó fi àpáàdì ràbàtà bo tirẹ̀ mọ́lẹ̀.
sentences.en: He-who-eagerly-speaks-of-one's-problems, he covers his own with a huge potsherd.

sentences.text: Àrókanlẹ̀ laṣọ ayaba; àwàkanlẹ̀ ni ti yàrà.
sentences.en: Wrapping-from-waist-to-the-floor is the style of the queen's wrapper; digging-down-to-the-deepest-bottom is the requirement of yàrà, the dry moat.

sentences.text: Arúgbó oǹdágbèsè, ó ní mélòó ni òun ó dùúró san níbẹ̀?
sentences.en: The old person who incurs debt, he says how much of it will he be around to repay?

sentences.text: Àsọ̀rọ̀àìlàdí ló pa Elempe ìṣáájú tó ní igbá wúwo ju àwo.
sentences.en: Speaking-without-explaining killed the first Elempe who said that calabash was heavier than china.

sentences.text: Àṣá ò gbádìẹ níkọ̀kọ̀; gbangba làṣá ń gbádìẹ.
sentences.en: The kite does not snatch chicks in secret, it snatches them openly.

sentences.text: Aṣeburúkú tẹsẹ̀ mọ́nà.
sentences.en: The evil doer makes a brisk exit.

sentences.text: A-ṣọ̀tún-ṣòsì-má-ba-ibìkan-jẹ́; irọ́ la ó bàá níbẹ̀.
sentences.en: One-who-is-tight-with-the-right-and-tight-with-left-without-alienating-either; what one will find in that characterization is a lie.

sentences.text: Àwárí lobìnrin ń wá nǹkan ọbẹ̀.
sentences.en: Seeking-until-finding is how a woman seeks ingredients for stew.

sentences.text: Àwíyé nIfẹ̀ ń fọ̀; gbangba lorò ń pẹran.
sentences.en: Explicitly is the way Ifẹ̀ speaks; it is openly that Orò kills animals.

sentences.text: Àyè kì í há adìẹ kó má dèé ìdí àbaa rẹ̀.
sentences.en: The space is never so tight that a chicken will not be able to reach its incubating nest.

sentences.text: Bí a bá ká okó mọ́ obìnrin nídìí á ní kùkú ni
sentences.en: The space is never so tight that a chicken will not be able to reach its incubating nest.

sentences.text: Bí a bá ń yọ́lẹ̀ dà, ohun abẹ́nú a máa yọ́ni ṣe.
sentences.en: If one engages secretly in treachery, secret disasters befall one.

sentences.text: Bí ẹnú bá jẹ, ojú á tì.
sentences.en: If the mouth has eaten, the eyes shut down.

sentences.text: Bí ìgbín bá fà, ìkarahun a tẹ̀lé e.
sentences.en: When the snail crawls, its shell follows.

sentences.text: Bí ìkàá bá ń rojọ́, ìkà kọ́ ni yó dàá a.
sentences.en: If the wicked person states a case, it is not the wicked person that will judge it.

sentences.text: Bí o finú ṣìkà tí o fòde ṣòótọ́, ọba séríkí á rín ọ rín ọ.
sentences.en: If you hide wickedness inside you and display a kindly disposition, God above will laugh hard at you.

sentences.text: Bí o rí i, wà pé o ò rí; ọkọ́ fún ọ lówó, àlé gbà á ná.
sentences.en: If you saw it you would say you did not; your husband gave you money and your lover spends it.

sentences.text: Bí ó ti wù kó pẹ́ tó, olóòótọ́ ò níí sùn sípò ìkà.
sentences.en: However long it takes, a truthful person will not wind up in the bed made for the wicked.

sentences.text: Bí obìnrín bá máa dán èké wò, a da aṣọ dúdú bora.
sentences.en: When a woman wishes to engage in mischief, she wears dark clothing.

sentences.text: Bí ojú bá sé ojú; kí ohùn má yẹ ohùn.
sentences.en: If eyes no longer see eyes, let the voice not miss the voice.

sentences.text: Bí olókùnrùn yó bàá kú, kó má purọ́ mọ́ àlapà; omitooro kì í korò.
sentences.en: If an invalid is approaching death, he should not lie about the melon-seed loaf; stew is never bitter.

sentences.text: Bí òru bí òru ní ń ṣe aláṣọdúdú.
sentences.en: Longing for night-time, longing for night-time is the tendency of the person in dark clothing.

sentences.text: Bí ọgbọ́n bá tán nínú, a tún òmíràn dá.
sentences.en: When an elder has exhausted all his wisdom, he turns to another wisdom.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọdé bá mọ igbá-di-ogóje, kò lè mọ èrò-kò-wájà.
sentences.en: If a youth knows two-hundred-becomes-one-hundred-and-forty, he cannot know traders-refuse-to-come-to-the-market.

sentences.text: Bí ọmọdé bá ri oyin, a ju àkàrà nù.
sentences.en: When a child sees honey, he throws away bean fritters.

sentences.text: Dúkìa tí a fi èrú kójọ kò mú ká dolówó.
sentences.en: The treasure one gathers by foul means will not make one rich.

sentences.text: “Ebí ń pa mí” ò ṣéé fìfé wí.
sentences.en: “I am hungry” is not a message that whistling can convey.

sentences.text: Eegun tí a bá so mọ́ ajá lọ́rùn, kì í ṣán an.
sentences.en: A dog does not eat a bone tied to its neck.

sentences.text: Èké Ìbídùn, tí ń kí eégún “Kú àtijọ́.”
sentences.en: Lying Ìbídùn, who greets a masquerader with, “It's been quite a while!”

sentences.text: Èké lojú ó tì bó dọ̀la.
sentences.en: The devious will reap shame in the future.

sentences.text: Èké mọ ilée rẹ̀ ó wó; ọ̀dàlẹ́ mọ tirẹ̀ ó bì dànù.
sentences.en: The devious person builds a house and it collapses; the treacherous person builds one and it tumbles in ruins.

sentences.text: Elékèé lèké ń yè; oun a bá ṣe ní ń yéni.
sentences.en: Only a devious person knows what he or she is about; each person alone is privy to what he or she has done.

sentences.text: Eléweé ní iyènú; àìní mọ ìwàá hù.
sentences.en: A person who has children must be responsible; one who does not must know how to behave.

sentences.text: Èlùbọ́ lo wáá rà; ọmọ ẹrán ṣe dénú igbá?
sentences.en: You came to buy yam-flour; how did a kid find its way into your calabash?

sentences.text: Èrò ò kí baálẹ̀, baálé ló ńkí.
sentences.en: The guest does not pay homage to the chief, only to the host.

sentences.text: Etí, gbọ́ èkejì kí o tó dájọ́.
sentences.en: Ear, hear the other side before passing judgement.

sentences.text: Etí tó gbọ́ àlọ ni yó gbọ̀ọ́ àbọ̀.
sentences.en: The same ears that heard about the departure will hear about the return.

sentences.text: Ewúrẹ́ ní òun ò mọlé odì; ẹni òún bá ṣẹ̀ kó bi òun.
sentences.en: The goat says it does not set aside any house as an enemy's; whoever it has offended should ask it why.

sentences.text: Ẹgẹ́ ò ṣákìí; ẹní bá bọ́ sábẹẹ rẹ̀, a pa á kú pátá-pátá.
sentences.en: The ẹgẹ́ trap never misses; whatever passes beneath it it strikes dead.

sentences.text: Ẹgbẹ̀tàlá: bí a ò bá là á, kì í yéni.
sentences.en: Ẹgbẹ̀tàlá: if one does not explain it, no one understands what it means.

sentences.text: Ẹ-kòì-fẹ́-mi-kù, tó ta ajáa rẹ̀ lókòó.
sentences.en: You-have-not-seen-the-last-of-me, who sold his dog for twenty cowries.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀là lọ̀rọ̀; bí a ò bá là á rírú ní ń rú.
sentences.en: Statements must be clarified; if they are not, they become muddy...

sentences.text: Ẹ̀là lọ̀rọ̀; bí a ò bá là á rírú ní ń rú.
sentences.en: Statements must be clarified; if they are not, they become muddy...

sentences.text: Ẹlẹ́rìí ní ń yanjú ẹjọ́; ẹlẹ́rìí kì í ṣe elégbè.
sentences.en: It is a witness that clears up a case; a witness is not a partisan.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀ẹ̀mejì letí ọlọ́jà ń gbọ́rọ̀.
sentences.en: The ears of the king hear everything twice.

sentences.text: Ẹni a kò fẹ́ nilée rẹ̀ ń jìnna lójú ẹni.
sentences.en: It is a person one does not love whose house is distant in one's estimation.

sentences.text: Ẹní bá sùn là ń jí, a kì í jí apirọrọ.
sentences.en: One wakes only those that sleep; one does not wake those pretending to sleep.

sentences.text: Ẹní gbé àrùn pamọ́ kọjá ore oníṣègùn.
sentences.en: Whoever conceals a disease is beyond help from a doctor.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a nà ní kùmọ̀ mẹ́fà, tó ní ọ̀kan ṣoṣo ló ba òun, níbo nìyókùú sọnù sí?
sentences.en: A person who is hit six times with a club and says only one blow landed; where did the other blows disappear to?

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó sá là ń lé.
sentences.en: People chase only those who flee.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó ṣe ojú kò da bí ẹni tó ṣe ẹ̀yìn.
sentences.en: The person who honors one in one's presence is nothing like the person who honors one in one's absence.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó fẹ́ kúure, kó hùwà rere.
sentences.en: Whoever wishes to die a decent death, let him or her live decently.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó sùn tó ní òún kú, tó bá jí, ta ni yó wìí fún?
sentences.en: The person who is asleep but spreads the word that he or she is dead, when he or she awakens whom will he or she tell?

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó gbépo lájà ò jalè bí ẹni tó gbà á sílẹ̀ fún un.
sentences.en: The person who removes oil from the rafter is less a thief than the person who helps him set it on the floor.

sentences.text: Ẹnìkan kì í yọ̀ kí ilẹ̀ ó sẹ́.
sentences.en: When a person slips, the earth may not deny responsibility or knowledge.

sentences.text: Ẹnu òpùrọ́ kì í ṣẹ̀jẹ̀.
sentences.en: The liar's mouth does not bleed.

sentences.text: Ẹnuu rẹ̀ ní ń dá igba, tí ń dá ọ̀ọ́dúnrún.
sentences.en: His or her mouth is the same one that proposes two hundred and proposes three hundred.

sentences.text: Ẹran tí a kì í jẹ, a kì í fi eyín pín in.
sentences.en: Meat that one does not eat, one does not bite into allotments with one's teeth.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀tàn kì í ṣe ọgbọ́n.
sentences.en: Deceit is no wisdom.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀wà yí kò dùn, ẹ̀wà yí kò dùn, àáṣó ìpàkọ́ ń mì tìtì.
sentences.en: These beans are not delicious, these beans are not delicious, yet the coiffure at the occiput is shaking vigorously.

sentences.text: Fi inú ṣìkà, fi òde ṣòótọ́; ẹni tí ḿbini kò níí ṣàì bini.
sentences.en: Hide wickedness in you and affect a benevolent comportment; the one who calls people to account will not forget.

sentences.text: Gbangba là ń ṣe gbàǹgbà; bẹ́ṣín bá kú, ìta gbangba là ń sin í sí.
sentences.en: One performs one's great feats in the open; if a horse dies, one buries it in a wide open space.

sentences.text: Gbangba làṣá ń ta.
sentences.en: The hawk always spreads its wings to the fullest.

sentences.text: Gbangba lÒgèdèǹgbé ń ṣawo.
sentences.en: Ògèdèm̀gbé always performs his rituals in the open.

sentences.text: Ìbáà tínrín, okùn òtítọ́ kì í já; bí irọ́ tó ìrókò, wíwó ní ń wó.
sentences.en: Even if it is flimsy, the thread of truth never snaps; even though a lie might the girth of an ìrókò tree, it inevitably crashes.

sentences.text: Igbó kan náà lọdẹ ń dẹ.
sentences.en: It is in the same forest that a hunter hunts (or all hunters hunt).

sentences.text: Ìjòkó là ń bá eèbà.
sentences.en: The oil pot is ever found in a sitting position.

sentences.text: Ìkòkò kì í ṣelé ìgbín; ṣe ló dè ìgbín mọ́lẹ̀.
sentences.en: The pot is no shelter for the snail; all it does is trap the snail.

sentences.text: Ilé ahun ò gba ahun; ọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀ ahun ò gbàlejò; ahún kọ́lé ẹ̀ tán ó yọ ọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀ níbàdí.
sentences.en: The tortoise's house is not large enough for it; the tortoise's porch is not large enough to receive visitors; the tortoise built its house and adds a porch at the rear.

sentences.text: Ìmàlé gbààwẹ̀ ó lóun ò gbétọ́ mì; ta ní ń ṣe ẹlẹ́rìí fún un?
sentences.en: The muslim fasts and swears he did not swallow his saliva; who is to corroborate his story?

sentences.text: Ìmàlé sọ̀rọ̀ òjó kù, ó ní Ọlọ́run jẹ́rìí òun.
sentences.en: The muslim says something and thunder rumbles; he says the Almighty is corroborating his statement.

sentences.text: Ìmùlẹ̀ ò gbọdọ̀ tan ara wọn jẹ; ìmọ̀ ẹnìkan ò yàn.
sentences.en: Those who enter into a covenant must not betray one another; one person's counsel is not enough by itself.

sentences.text: Ìpẹ́pẹ́rẹ́ ìgò méje; bí kò bá pé méje ara kì í gbà á.
sentences.en: Seven thrifling bottles; fewer than seven and one cannot endure the thought.

sentences.text: Ìrókò tó bá gbàbọ̀dè, bíbẹ́ ni.
sentences.en: Whichever ìrókò tree becomes involved in treachery gets felled.

sentences.text: Irọ́ ni “Má jẹ̀ẹ́nìkan ó gbọ́”; òótọ́ ni “Ẹni o rí o bi.”
sentences.en: “Breathe not a word of it to anyone” denotes a lie; “Ask anyone you please” indicates the truth.

sentences.text: “Jẹ́ kí n fìdí hẹ́ ẹ” ẹ́ gbàjòkó; àfòmọ́ di onílé.
sentences.en: “Permit me to perch by you” takes the whole seat; the parasite becomes the host.

sentences.text: Kí olówó wá, kí aláwìn wá; à-rà-àì-san ni ò sunwọ̀n.
sentences.en: Let the purchaser with cash come and let the purchaser on credit come; only buying without “eventually” paying is bad.

sentences.text: “Kò dùn mí, kò dùn mí”; àgbàlagbà ń bú ọpa lẹ́ẹ̀mẹfà nítorí iyán àná.
sentences.en: “I am not upset, I am not upset!” Yet a grown man swears angrily six times because of last night's pounded yam.

sentences.text: Kò sí ohun tí a ò lè fi òru ṣe; ẹ̀rù ọ̀sán là ń bà.
sentences.en: There is nothing one cannot do in the dead of night; the light of day alone is what one fears.

sentences.text: Kò ṣeku kò ṣẹyẹ ò jẹ́ kí àjàò sanwó òde.
sentences.en: Being neither a rat nor a bird keeps àjàò (a bird-like animal) from having to pay poll tax.

sentences.text: Má sẹ̀ẹ́ kí ọ̀ràn má pọ̀.
sentences.en: Do not deny your responsibility; that way the problem will be minimized.

sentences.text: “Mo kò ó” kì í ṣe àìní àpèjúwe.
sentences.en: “I met him” is an incomplete statement without further elaboration.

sentences.text: Nì palaba, ní wonko, ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ á ṣèkan.
sentences.en: Either sunken or swollen, the cheeks will be one or the other.

sentences.text: “Ó fò sókè ó pẹ́ títí,” irọ́ ló ń pa.
sentences.en: “He jumped up and stayed aloft almost for ever”: that is a lie.

sentences.text: Ó jọ gàtè, kò jọ gàtè, ó fẹsẹ̀ méjèèjì tiro rìn.
sentences.en: It may seem like staggering, and it may not seem like staggering, but he is tipping forward on tiptoes.

sentences.text: O kò pọ̀ ọ́, bẹ́ẹ̀ni o ò gbé e mì.
sentences.en: You do not spit it out, and yet you do not swallow it.

sentences.text: “Ó mọ́ mi lọ́wọ́” ní ń di olè.
sentences.en: “It is an exact fit for my hand” leads to thievery.

sentences.text: O mú oori lọ́wọ́ ọ̀tún, o mú kùmọ̀ lọ́wọ́ òsì, o ní kí Orímáfọ̀ọ́ wá gba oúnjẹ.
sentences.en: You hold corn loaf in your right hand and hold a cudgel in your left hand, and you call to Orímáfọ̀ọ́ to come take the food from you.

sentences.text: Ó pẹ́ títí ni “A-bẹnu-bí-ẹnu-ọ̀bọ”; ká ṣá sọ pé, “Ìwọ Lámọnrín, ọ̀bọ ni ọ́.”
sentences.en: It is mere circumlocution to say “A person has a mouth like a monkey's”; one should rather say, “You, so-and-so, you are a monkey.”

sentences.text: Ó ta ọfà sókè, ó ṣí odó borí.
sentences.en: He shot an arrow towards the sky and covers his head with a mortar.

sentences.text: Obìnrin abàlèmẹ́fà: àlè mẹ́fà ò mọ ara wọn.
sentences.en: A woman who has six lovers: the six lovers never know about one another.

sentences.text: Obìnrin-ín bímọ fúnni kò pé kó má pani; obìnrin ò bímọ fúnni kò pé kó má pani.
sentences.en: That a woman has had one's child does not mean she cannot kill one; that a woman has not had one's child does not mean she may not kill one.

sentences.text: Obìnrin-ín pẹ́ lọ́jà ó fìgbójú wọlé.
sentences.en: A woman tarried too long at the market and returns home with a brazen face.

sentences.text: Obìnrin-ín re ilé àlè, ó fi ilé ìyá ẹ̀ tan ọkọ jẹ.
sentences.en: A woman goes to her lover's house and uses her mother's home to deceive her husband.

sentences.text: Odídẹrẹ́ ẹyẹ òkun, àlùkò ẹyẹ ọ̀sà; bí a bá jẹun gbé, ká má jẹ̀ẹ́ùn gbé.
sentences.en: The parrot is a bird of the sea, and the kingfisher a bird of the lagoon; even though we might forget that we once partook in the food, let us never forget what we covenanted.

sentences.text: Òfìífìí là ń rí, a ò rí òkodoro; òkodoro ń bọ̀, baba gbangba.
sentences.en: All we see is shadows, not clarity; but clarity will come, father of all openness.

sentences.text: Ògèdèǹgbé irọ́ kì í dáni síyẹ̀wù; gbangba ní ń dáni sí.
sentences.en: An audacious lie does not trip one in one's closet; it exposes one in a public place.

sentences.text: Ohun tí a ò fẹ́ kéèyàn ó mọ̀ là ńṣe lábẹ́lẹ̀.
sentences.en: It is what one wishes to keep a secret that one does in private.

sentences.text: Ojo díẹ̀, akin díẹ̀; ìyà ní ń kó jẹni.
sentences.en: A little cowardice, a little bravery; all it brings one is trouble.

sentences.text: Òjò ọ̀gànjọ́ ò pa ẹni rere; bí kò pa jalè-jalè a pa yíde-yíde.
sentences.en: A midnight rain does not beat a decent person; if the person it beats is not a habitual thief he/she will be a habitual “night” wanderer.

sentences.text: Ojú gba-n-gba là ńta awọ gbà-ǹ-gbà.
sentences.en: It is out in the open that one spreads a huge skin.

sentences.text: Ojú kì í fẹ́nikù kó hu ibi.
sentences.en: The eyes do not, because they do not see one, engage in evil against one.

sentences.text: Ojú lobìnrin-ín mọ̀.
sentences.en: Women know only the face.

sentences.text: Ojú lọ̀rọ̀ọ́ wà.
sentences.en: Discourse is in the eyes.

sentences.text: Ojú olóbì la ti ń jèrè obì.
sentences.en: It is in the presence and with the knowledge of the kola-nut seller that one receives a gratuitous addition to one's purchase.

sentences.text: Ojú tó ti mọni rí kì í wí pe òun ò mọni mọ́.
sentences.en: The eyes that used to recognize one cannot say they no longer recognize one.

sentences.text: Òkété, báyìí nìwà ẹ; o báFá mulẹ̀ o daFá.
sentences.en: So, giant bush rat, such is your character; you made a pact with Ifá and you betrayed Ifá.

sentences.text: Òkété ní ọjọ́ gbogbo lòún mọ̀, òun ò mọ ọjọ́ mìíràn.
sentences.en: The large bush rat says it knows everyday, but not some other day.

sentences.text: Òkóbó kì í bímọ sítòsí.
sentences.en: The eunuch never has children close by.

sentences.text: Olòfòófó ò gbẹ́gbàá; ibi ọpẹ́ ní ń mọ.
sentences.en: The tattler does not earn six pence; thanks are all he gets.

sentences.text: Olóòótọ́ ìlú nìkà ìlú.
sentences.en: The honest person in a town is the ogre of the town.

sentences.text: Olóòótọ́ kì í sùn sípò ìkà.
sentences.en: The honest person will not sleep in the place prepared for the wicked person.

sentences.text: Òǹrorò lẹ̀gbọ́n òfófó.
sentences.en: Lack of compassion is the elder of back-biting.

sentences.text: “Orí jẹ́ kí ń pé méjì” obìnrin ò dénú.
sentences.en: “May my head grant that I have a partner” as a woman's prayer is not sincere.

sentences.text: Òtítọ́ dọ́jà ó kùtà; owó lọ́wọ́ là ń ra èké.
sentences.en: Truth arrives at the market but finds no buyer; it is with ready cash, though, that people buy falsehood.

sentences.text: Òtítọ́ kì í kú ká fi irọ́ jọba.
sentences.en: The truth does not die to be replaced as king by the lie.

sentences.text: Òtítọ́ kì í ṣìnà; irọ́ ní ń forí gbọgbẹ́.
sentences.en: Truth never goes awry; it is falsehood that earns a gash on the head.

sentences.text: Òtítọ́ korò; bí omi tooro nirọ́ rí.
sentences.en: Truth is bitter; falsehood is like meat stew.

sentences.text: Òtítọ́ lolórí ìwà.
sentences.en: Truthfulness is the chief of attributes.

sentences.text: Òtítọ́ ní ń tú ẹrù ìkà palẹ̀.
sentences.en: It is truth that unpacks the load of the wicked for all to see.

sentences.text: Owó lobìnrin-ín mọ̀.
sentences.en: Women care only about money.

sentences.text: Ọbẹ̀ẹ́ dùn, ọbẹ̀ ò dùn, iyán tán nígbá.
sentences.en: The stew is delicious, the stew is not delicious; the pounded yams meal is completely gone from the dish.

sentences.text: Ọ̀nà irọ́ kì í pẹ́ẹ́ pin.
sentences.en: The path of deceit soon ends.

sentences.text: Ọ̀mọ̀rán bèèrè ọ̀ràn wò; Ìjàpá ní, “Ẹni tí wọ́n pa lánàá, kàà kú tán?”
sentences.en: The sage asks for information; Àjàpá the trickster asks, “About the person who was killed yesterday, is he already dead?”

sentences.text: “Ọ̀ràn yí ò dùn mí”: ẹ̀ẹ̀kanṣoṣo là ń wí i.
sentences.en: “This matter does not hurt me”: stating it only once suffices.

sentences.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ ìkọ̀kọ̀, ní gbangba ní ń bọ̀.
sentences.en: Secret matters have open exposure as their ultimate destination.

sentences.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ ò pariwo.
sentences.en: The matter in question does not make a noise.

sentences.text: Ọ̀tá ẹni kì í pòdù ọ̀yà.
sentences.en: One's enemy never kills a huge cane-rat.

sentences.text: Pàkìtí ṣe bí òkú wọ̀lú; labalábá ṣe bí ẹyẹ jáko.
sentences.en: The coarse mat enters the town like a corpse; the butterfly enters the bush like a bird.

sentences.text: Pátá-pátá; là ń fọ́jú, kùm̀bọ̀-kumbọ là ń dẹ́tẹ̀; ojú à-fọ́-ì-fọ́-tán ìjà ní ń dá sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: One's blindness should be absolute, and one's leprosy should pervade the whole body; half-blindness only brings dissensions.

sentences.text: Pátá-pátá leégún ń faṣọ borí;.
sentences.en: It is completely that the masquerader covers his head with his shroud.

sentences.text: Pẹ̀yìndà kí o ríṣe èké, fara pamọ́ kí o rí bí aṣení ti ń sọ.
sentences.en: Turn your back you and you will discover how the deceitful person behaves; hide and you will find out what the detractor is saying.

sentences.text: Pípọn niyì idẹ; ẹ̀jẹ́ niyì oògun.
sentences.en: Redness is the glory of brass; efficaciousness is the glory of medicine.

sentences.text: Pọ̀ǹgbà-pọngba là ń bá odi.
sentences.en: Firmly planted and unshakable is the way one finds the city fortification.

sentences.text: Purọ kóo níyì; bí a bá jáni tán, ẹ̀tẹ́ ní ń dà.
sentences.en: Lie and become renowned; once you have been found out the result is disgrace.

sentences.text: Rìkíṣí pa wọ́n pọ̀ wọ́n dọ̀rẹ́; kò lọ́jọ́ kò lóṣù ọ̀rẹ́ bàjẹ́.
sentences.en: Intrigue brought them together and they became friends; it did not take days, let alone months, before the friendship ended.

sentences.text: Rìkíṣí pin, alábòsí lọ.
sentences.en: When the intrigue is terminated, and the devious person takes his leave.

sentences.text: Sàráà baba ẹbọ.
sentences.en: Alms are the ultimate sacrifice.

sentences.text: Ṣìgìdì ò lẹ́nu fọhùn; irọ́ ń purọ́ fúnrọ́.
sentences.en: The earthen idol has no mouth to speak; lies are lying to lies.

sentences.text: Ṣìgìdì tí ò sọ̀rọ̀, a ò mẹni tí ń gbè.
sentences.en: The earthen idol that does not speak, no one knows whose side it is on.

sentences.text: Ta là bá rí báwí bí ẹní fọmọ fọ́kọ lóru, tí ò jẹ́ kílẹ̀ mọ́?
sentences.en: Whom should one blame, if not the person who delivered a child to a husband in the middle of the night without waiting until daylight.

sentences.text: Ta la domi sí lára? Ta lòrìṣà ń gùn?
sentences.en: Who is the one on whom water was poured? Who is the one being mounted by the god?

sentences.text: Ta leṣinṣin ìbá gbè bí kò ṣe elégbò?
sentences.en: Who else will the flies flock after if not the person with open sores.

sentences.text: Ta ló dè ọ́ tí ò ń kakọ?
sentences.en: Who has tied you down and thus forced you to confess your guilt?

sentences.text: Ta ní ń ṣoògùn lódò tí lábẹ-lábẹ ò gbọ́?
sentences.en: Who is concocting a medicine by the river about which the lábẹlábẹ plant is ignorant?

sentences.text: “Wá jẹun.” “N ò jẹ.” Ó fọgọ́rùnún òkèlè tọ́ ọbẹ̀ wò.
sentences.en: “Come join me at my meal.” “Thank you, but no.” Still he eats a hundred mouthfuls, just to taste the stew.

sentences.text: A kì í dùbúlẹ̀ ṣubú.
sentences.en: One does not fall from a prone position.

sentences.text: A kì í fi àìmọ̀nà dá pàdé-m̀-pàdé.
sentences.en: One does not play the rendezvous game without knowing one's way.

sentences.text: Abúni ò tó abẹ̀rín; bẹ́ẹ̀ni abẹ̀rín ò mọ ẹ̀yìn ọ̀la.
sentences.en: The person who insults one is not as bad as the person who derides one; yet the person who derides one does not know what the future may bring.

sentences.text: Adìẹ́ yẹ̀gẹ̀, a ṣe bí ó ṣubú.
sentences.en: The chicken lists to one side, we think it has fallen.

sentences.text: A-fi-tirẹ̀-sílẹ̀-gbọ́-tẹniẹlẹ́ni, Ọlọ́run ní ń ba gbọ́ tirẹ̀.
sentences.en: He-who-neglects-his-affairs-to-care-for-others'-affairs, it is God that takes care of his affairs.

sentences.text: Àgbà ṣoore má wo bẹ̀.
sentences.en: Elder, do a favor and remove your eyes from it.

sentences.text: Àgbò ò ṣéé mú; ọ̀dá ò ṣéé mú; ohun gbogbo ní ń tóbi lójú ahun.
sentences.en: A ram is too much to give; a gelded animal is too much to give; everything is excessive in the sight of a miser.

sentences.text: Àì-fi-ǹ-kan-pe-ǹ-kan ní ń ba nǹkan jẹ́.
sentences.en: It is failure-to-count-anything-as-significant that ruins things.

sentences.text: Àìmète, àìmèrò, lọmọ ìyá mẹ́fàá fi ń kú sóko ẹgbàafà.
sentences.en: Lack of resourcefulness and lack of thoughtfulness cause six siblings to die as pawns for only twelve thousand cowries.

sentences.text: Àjẹ́gbà ni ti kọ̀ǹkọ̀.
sentences.en: Croaking-in-relays is the mark of frogs.

sentences.text: Akẹ́yinjẹ ò mọ̀ pé ìdí ń ro adìẹ.
sentences.en: The person who gathers eggs to eat does not know that the chicken's orifice hurts.

sentences.text: A-lágbára-má-mèrò, baba ọ̀lẹ́.
sentences.en: He-who-has-strength-but-lacks-discretion, father of laziness.

sentences.text: A-láì-mète-mèrò ọkọ tó fi adìẹ ìyàwó bọ orí ìyálé; bí baálé bá jẹ́ ìkà, èwo ni tòrìṣà?
sentences.en: The shiftless, thoughtless husband who makes the junior wife's chicken as a sacrifice to the senior wife's head; if the husband is wicked, what about the god?

sentences.text: Aláràjẹ ò mọ ọdún; a-biṣu-ú-ta-bí-igi.
sentences.en: He who purchases the food he eats cares not what the season is; his yams always flourish like trees.

sentences.text: Arúgbó ṣoge rí; àkísàá lògbà rí.
sentences.en: The old person was once a dandy; the rag was once in fashion.

sentences.text: Àṣẹ Ọ̀yọ́ kì í ró “Gbà”, àfi “Múwá.”
sentences.en: The order from Ọ̀yọ́ never sounds “Gbà” (meaning “Take!”), only “Múwá (meaning “Bring.”)

sentences.text: Àṣíríi náwó-náwó kì í tú lójú ahun.
sentences.en: The big spender is never disgraced in the presence of the miser.

sentences.text: Aṣiwèrè ló bí ìyá ọ̀bọ.
sentences.en: It was an imbecile that gave birth to the mother of the monkey.

sentences.text: Ayídóborí tafà sókè: ojú Olúwaá tó wọn.
sentences.en: Those who cover their heads with mortars and shoot arrows into the sky: God's eyes encompass them all.

sentences.text: Bámijókòó làbíkú ń jẹ́; ẹni tí ò bímọ rí ò gbọdọ̀ sọ Ọmọ́láriwo.
sentences.en: Bámijókòó (Sit-with-me) is the name one gives an àbíkú; a person who has never had a child does not name a child Ọmọ́láriwo.

sentences.text: Bí a bá gé igi nígbó, ká fi ọ̀ràn ro ara ẹni wò.
sentences.en: When one fells a tree in the forest, one should apply the matter to oneself.

sentences.text: Bí a bá rí òkú ìkà nílẹ̀, tí a fi ẹsẹ̀ tá; ìkàá di méji.
sentences.en: If one sees the corpse of a wicked person on the ground and one kicks it, there are then two wicked people.

sentences.text: Bí o ṣe rere yó yọ sí ọ lára; bí o kò ṣe rere yó yọ sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: If your deeds are good the benefits return to you; if your deeds are not good they will be apparent to all.

sentences.text: Bí ó ti ń dun ọmọ ẹyẹ, bẹ́ẹ̀ ló ń dun ọmọ èèyàn
sentences.en: As the young of birds hurt, so the young of humans hurt.

sentences.text: “Èrò tètè jí;” “Èrò jẹ́ ilẹ̀ ó mọ́”; tèrò là ń srò.
sentences.en: “Traveller, get up early”; “Traveller, wait until light”; it's all out of solicitousness for the traveller's welfare.

sentences.text: Ẹ ní ká má tafà; kí ni a ó fi lé ogun? Kànnà-kànnà la fi lé Boko.
sentences.en: You forbid us to shoot arrows, so with what shall we repel invaders? In the past the Boko were repelled with catapaults.

sentences.text: Ẹní fowó lògbà ló káyé já.
sentences.en: It is the person who uses his/her money to enjoy life that lives well.

sentences.text: Ẹní lówó kó ṣe bí ọba; àrà wo lahún fẹ́ fi owó dá?
sentences.en: Whoever has riches should act like a king; what kind of feat can a miser perform with money?

sentences.text: Ẹní mọ owóó lò lowó ń bá gbé.
sentences.en: It is the person who knows how to use wealth that wealth attaches to.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bá máa bímọ á yọ̀ fọ́lọ́mọ.
sentences.en: Whoever would have children of her own must rejoice with those who already have.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó gòkè, kó fa ọ̀rẹ́ẹ rẹ̀ lọ́wọ́; ẹni tó rí jẹ, kó fún ọ̀rẹ́ẹ rẹ̀ jẹ.
sentences.en: Whoever has reached the top, let him or her pull his or her friend by the hand; whoever has food to eat, let him or her share it with his or her friend.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó bèèrè ọ̀rọ̀ ló fẹ́ ìdíi rẹ̀ ẹ́gbọ́.
sentences.en: Whoever asks about a matter genuinely wishes to know its causes.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí a ṣe lóore tí kò dúpẹ́, bí ọlọ́ṣà kóni lẹ́rù ni.
sentences.en: A person whom one does a favor but who shows no gratitude is like a robber who has stolen one's goods.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó so ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ parí ọ̀ṣọ́; ẹni tó fúnni lọ́mọ parí oore.
sentences.en: The person who adorns herself with beads has done the ultimate in self-beautifying; the person who gives one a child (in marriage) has done the ultimate in favor.

sentences.text: Ẹni tí ó ṣe ìbàjẹ́ èèyàn-án ṣe ìbàjẹ́ araa rẹ̀.
sentences.en: Whoever defames others defames himself or herself.

sentences.text: Ẹyẹlé fi ẹ̀sín-in rẹ̀ pamọ́, ó ń ṣe ẹ̀sín adìẹ.
sentences.en: The pigeon hides its own disgrace and goes ridiculing the chicken.

sentences.text: Ìbàjẹ́ iṣu nìbàjẹ́ ọ̀bẹ; ẹni tó ṣe ìbàjẹ́ èèyàn-án ṣe ìbàjẹ́ ara ẹ̀.
sentences.en: The blemish of the yam is the blemish of the knife; whoever besmirches other people's names besmirches his/her own.

sentences.text: Igbá olóore kì í fọ́; àwo olóore kì í fàya; towó tọmọ ní ń ya ilé olóore.
sentences.en: The calabash of a kind-heated person never breaks; the china plate of a kind-hearted person never cracks; both riches and children ever converge in the home of a kind-hearted person.

sentences.text: Igbá onípẹ̀lẹ́ kì í fọ́; àwo onípẹ̀lẹ́ kì í fàya.
sentences.en: The calabash belonging to a patient person never breaks; the china plate belonging to a patient person never cracks.

sentences.text: Ilé ọ̀ṣọnú àyàyó; ta ní jẹ́ yalé ahun-káhun?
sentences.en: To visit the home of a generous person is to be plied with food aplenty; who would think of visiting a miser?

sentences.text: Inú búburú, oògùn òṣì.
sentences.en: Ill will “is the” medicine that ensures misfortune.

sentences.text: Ìyàwó jẹ ọkà jẹ igbá.
sentences.en: The wife ate the yam-flour meal and ate the calabash with it.

sentences.text: ÌKÉDE KÁRÍAYÉ FÚN Ẹ̀TỌ́ ỌMỌNÌYÀN
sentences.en: UNIVERSAL DECLARATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS

sentences.text: Bí ó ti jẹ́ pé ó ṣe pàtàkì kí ìdàgbàsókè ìbáṣepọ̀ ti ọ̀rẹ́‐sí‐ọ̀rẹ́ wà láàrin àwọn orílẹ̀‐èdè,
sentences.en: Whereas it is essential to promote the development of friendly relations between nations,

sentences.text: Gbogbo ènìyàn ni a bí ní òmìnira; iyì àti ẹ̀tọ́ kọ̀ọ̀kan sì dọ́gba.
sentences.en: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.

sentences.text: Ẹnì kọ̀ọ̀kan ló ní ẹ̀tọ́ láti wà láàyè, ẹ̀tọ́ sí òmìnira àti ẹ̀tọ́ sí ààbò ara rẹ̀.
sentences.en: Everyone has the right to life, liberty and the security of person.

sentences.text: Gbogbo ènìyàn ló dọ́gba lábẹ́ òfin. Wọ́n sì ní ẹ̀tọ́ sí àà bò lábẹ́ òfin láìsí ìyàsọ́tọ̀ kankan.
sentences.en: All are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to equal protection of the law.

sentences.text: Ẹnì kọ̀ọ̀kan ló ní ẹ̀tọ́ sí ààbò lábẹ́ òfin kúrò lọ́wọ́ irú àyọjúràn tàbí ìbanijẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
sentences.en: Everyone has the right to the protection of the law against such interference or attacks.

sentences.text: Ẹnì kọ̀ọ̀kan ló ní ẹ̀tọ́ láti jẹ́ ọmọ orílẹ̀‐èdè kan.
sentences.en: Everyone has the right to a nationality.

sentences.text: A kò lè ṣàdédé gba ohun ìní ẹnì kan lọ́wọ́ rẹ̀ láìnídìí.
sentences.en: No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his property.

sentences.text: A kò lè fi ipá mú ẹnìkẹ́ni dara pọ̀ mọ́ ẹgbẹ́ kankan.
sentences.en: No one may be compelled to belong to an association.

sentences.text: Ẹnì kọ̀ọ̀kan ló ní ẹ̀tọ́ tó dọ́gba láti ṣe iṣẹ́ ìjọba ní orílẹ̀‐èdè rẹ̀.
sentences.en: Everyone has the right to equal access to public service in his country.

sentences.text: A ní láti pèsè ìtọ́jú àti ìrànlọ́wọ́ pàtàkì fún àwọn abiyamọ àti àwọn ọmọdé.
sentences.en: Motherhood and childhood are entitled to special care and assistance.

sentences.text: Ẹnì kọ̀ọ̀kan ló ní ẹ̀tọ́ láti kọ́ ẹ̀kọ́.
sentences.en: Everyone has the right to education.

sentences.text: Ó kéré tán, ẹ̀kọ́ gbọdọ̀ jẹ́ ọ̀fẹ́ ní àwọn ilé‐ẹ̀kọ́ alákọ̀ọ́bẹ̀rẹ̀.
sentences.en: Education shall be free, at least in the elementary and fundamental stages.

sentences.text: Ẹkọ́ ní ilé‐ẹ̀kọ́ alákọ̀ọ́bẹ̀rẹ̀ yìí sì gbọdọ̀ jẹ́ dandan.
sentences.en: Elementary education shall be compulsory.

sentences.text: Ìkejì, a nílò láti bèrè ìbéèrè nípa ojúṣe.
sentences.en: Second, we need to ask questions about responsibility.

sentences.text: Ìkẹ́ta, a nílò láti bèrè ìbéèrè nípa ìdọ́gba.

sentences.en: Global inequality is a wrenching, intensifying problem.

sentences.text: Ṣùgbọ́n ó túmọ sí ìpín àìṣedédé alágbára àwọn àǹfààní fún ìgbeayé pípẹ́, alálàáfíà, onítẹ́lọ́rùn.
sentences.en: But it actually means a profoundly unjust distribution of the chances for a long, healthy, fulfilling life.

sentences.en: It does more than all of the foreign aid programs in the world combined.

sentences.text: Níbo ni àwọn ìbéèrè tuntun wọ̀nyí nípa ẹ̀tọ́ àwọn òṣìṣẹ́, nípa ojúṣe àti nípa ìdógba ń múwa lọ?

sentences.text: Àwọn ìbéèrè wọ̀nyí kọ ìkáàánú, wọ́n sì gba ìṣedédé.
sentences.en: These questions reject pity, and they embrace justice.

sentences.text: Àwọn ìbéèrè wọ̀nyí kọ ìpínyà àwọn alátìlẹyìn ọmọ-ìlú àti àwọn alátìlẹyìn àpapọ̀ nípa àwa kojú àwọn.

sentences.text: Ọkàn wa wà lọ́dọ̀ gbogbo àwọn tí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí kàn, a sì ń gbàdúrà fún wọn.
sentences.en: Our thoughts and prayers are with all those affected by this devastating monsoon.

sentences.text: Àlàyé tí ẹ̀ka ọ́fíìsì ṣe rèé:
sentences.en: The branch has provided the following details.

sentences.text: Ìpínlẹ̀ Gujarat: Ní ìlú Vadodara, àwọn akéde márùnlélógóje (ni àkúnya omi náà ba ilé wọn jẹ́.
sentences.en: Gujarat: In the city of Vadodara, a total of 145 publishers were affected by the floodwaters.

sentences.text: Àmọ́, mìmì kan ò mi ọ́fíìsì àwọn atúmọ̀ èdè Gujarati tó wà ní ìlú Vadodara.
sentences.en: The Gujarati remote translation office, which is located in Vadodara, was not damaged.

sentences.text: Ìpínlẹ̀ Maharashtra: Ní ìlú Mumbai, ìdílé mẹ́fà ni àkúnya omi náà ba ilé wọn jẹ́.
sentences.en: Maharashtra: In Mumbai, the homes of six families were affected.

sentences.text: Àwọn ará ní ìlú kan tó wà nítòsí gbà wọ́n sílé.
sentences.en: Brothers in a nearby city provided temporary accommodations.

sentences.text: Ìpínlẹ̀ Karnataka: Ìdílé mẹ́fà ni àkúnya omi náà ti mú kí wọ́n sá fi ilé wọn sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: Karnataka: Six families were displaced by the floods.

sentences.text: Ìpínlẹ̀ yìí ni ẹ̀ka ọ́fíìsì wà, àmọ́ àkúnya omi yìí ò ṣe jàǹbá èyíkéyìí fún ẹ̀ka ọ́fíìsì náà.
sentences.en: The branch office is located in this state, but it was not affected by the heavy rains or flooding.

sentences.text: Ìgbìmọ̀ Tó Ń Ṣètò Ìrànwọ́ Nígbà Àjálù ti ń bójú tó ọ̀rọ̀ náà.
sentences.en: A Disaster Relief Committee is assessing the situation.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀ka ọ́fíìsì ti ń darí ètò ìrànwọ́ láwọn ibi tọ́rọ̀ kàn.
sentences.en: The branch office is coordinating the relief efforts in the affected areas.

sentences.text: Àdúrà wa ni pé kí Jèhófà má ṣe fi àwọn ará wa yìí sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: We pray that Jehovah will continue to be with our brothers affected by the flooding.

sentences.text: À ń fojú sọ́nà fún ìgbà tó jẹ́ pé “ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àlàáfíà” ló máa wà níbi gbogbo dípò àjálù.​
sentences.en: We look forward to the time when natural disasters will be replaced by an “abundance of peace.

sentences.text: Àwọn ìjọ àwọn Ẹlẹ́rìí Jèhófà tó wà ní Íńdíà ń ṣèrànwọ́ fáwọn ará wọn tí àjálù ṣẹlẹ̀ sí.
sentences.en: Congregations of Jehovah’s Witnesses within India are providing necessary relief aid to their fellow worshippers.

sentences.text: Ní November 16, 2018, ìjì tí wọ́n pè ní Gaja ṣọṣẹ́ gan-an ní ìpínlẹ̀ Tamil Nadu lórílẹ̀-èdè Íńdíà.
sentences.en: On November 16, 2018, Cyclone Gaja devastated the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

sentences.text: Ilé ọ̀kan lára àwọn ará wa nílùú Mannargudi, ní Tamil Nadu rèé. Igi wó lu ilé náà.
sentences.en: The home of one of our brothers in Mannargudi, Tamil Nadu, that was damaged by a fallen tree.

sentences.text: Àmọ́, ilé àwọn ará wa méjìdínlógójì (38) àti Gbọ̀ngàn Ìjọba méjì ló bà jẹ́.
sentences.en: However, 38 homes of our brothers and 2 Kingdom Halls were damaged.

sentences.text: Iṣẹ́ ìtúmọ̀ èdè kì í ṣe iṣẹ́ tí ẹnì kan lè dá ṣe.
sentences.en: Translation work depends heavily on collaboration.

sentences.text: Ní Friday, September 28, ìmìtìtì ilẹ̀ tó lágbára wáyé ní erékùṣù Sulawesi lórílẹ̀-èdè Indonéṣíà.
sentences.en: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck the Indonesian island of Sulawesi on Friday, September 28.

sentences.text: Àwọn díẹ̀ ló fara pa, wọ́n sì ní láti lọ sílé ìwòsàn.
sentences.en: A few publishers sustained injuries and needed to be treated at a hospital.

sentences.text: Ilé tí Ìjọ Palu ti ń ṣèpàdé náà tún bà jẹ́.
sentences.en: The building that the Palu Congregation uses to hold their meetings was also damaged.

sentences.text: Òjò yìí fa omíyalé, àwọn tó pa lé ní ọgọ́rùn-ún kan (100), ọ̀pọ̀ ilé ló sì gbá lọ.
sentences.en: The rains triggered a flash flood that killed more than 100 people and washed away several homes.

sentences.text: Ó dùn wá pé arákùnrin wa kan kú nígbà tí omi gbé ilé rẹ̀ lọ.
sentences.en: Sadly, one of our brothers died when his home was swept away in the flood.

sentences.text: Omi náà sì tún ba ilé mẹ́ta míì tó jẹ́ ti àwọn ará wa jẹ́.
sentences.en: Three other homes of Witness families were severely damaged.

sentences.text: A ti dá Ìgbìmọ̀ Tó Ń Ṣètò Ìrànwọ́ Nígbà Àjálù sílẹ̀ láti pèsè ohun táwọn ará nílò.
sentences.en: A Disaster Relief Committee has been formed to organize the relief work.

sentences.text: Wọ́n sì tún wo bí ìránlọ́wọ́ táwọn ará nílò ṣe máa pọ̀ tó.
sentences.en: They are also evaluating the extent of relief aid needed.

sentences.text: À ń rántí gbogbo àwọn ará tí àjálù yìí ṣẹlẹ̀ sí nínú àdúrà wa.
sentences.en: Our prayers are with all the brothers who have been affected by this disaster.

sentences.text: Bákan náà, ọwọ́ ìjì yìí ba Gbọ̀ngàn Ìjọba mọ́kànlélógójì (41) jẹ́ káàkiri àwọn agbègbè míì nílẹ̀ Japan.
sentences.en: An additional 41 Kingdom Halls sustained damage as the storm passed through other regions of Japan.

sentences.text: Àwọn ará yọ̀ǹda ara wọn láti palẹ̀ ìdọ̀tí mọ́ kúrò nínú Gbọ̀ngàn Ìjọba tó wà lókè.
sentences.en: Volunteers remove debris from the Kingdom Hall pictured in the lead image.

sentences.text: Ní báyìí, àtúnṣe ń lọ lọ́wọ́ lórí Gbọ̀ngàn Ìjọba kan.
sentences.en: An additional Kingdom Hall is in the process of being repaired.

sentences.text: Àwòrán Gbọ̀ngàn Ìjọba kan ṣáájú àti lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n tún un ṣe.
sentences.en: Before and after photographs of a Kingdom Hall in Ehime.

sentences.text: Àwòrán ìdílé Abe láti agbègbè Ehime lẹ́yìn táwọn ará parí títún ilé wọn tí omíyalé bà jẹ́ ṣe.
sentences.en: The Abe family from Ehime pictured after the brothers completed repairs on their flood-damaged home.

sentences.text: Arákùnrin Jackson tún fi àsìkò náà bá ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan àwọn tí àjálù náà kàn sọ̀rọ̀ ìtùnú.
sentences.en: Brother Jackson also took time to speak consolingly to individual victims of the disaster.

sentences.text: Wọ́n tọ́jú arábìnrin wa tó fara pa yìí nílé ìwòsàn, ara rẹ̀ sì ti ń balẹ̀ báyìí.
sentences.en: The injured sister was treated at a hospital and is now recovering.

sentences.text: Kò mọ síbẹ̀ o, omíyalé yìí tún ba Gbọ̀ngàn Ìjọba mọ́kànlá àti Gbọ̀ngàn Àpéjọ kan jẹ́.
sentences.en: Also, 11 Kingdom Halls and an Assembly Hall were damaged by the floodwaters.

sentences.text: """Ní September 6, 2018, ìmìtìtì ilẹ̀ tó lágbára wáyé ní Hokkaido, erékùṣù kan ní gúúsù orílẹ̀-èdè Japan."
sentences.en: """A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck Hokkaido, the northern island of Japan, on September 6, 2018."

sentences.text: Ọgọ́rùn-ún (100) ilé àwọn ará wa àti Gbọ̀ngàn Ìjọba mẹ́rin ló bà jẹ́.
sentences.en: A total of 100 homes of Witnesses and 4 Kingdom Halls were damaged.

sentences.text: Ní ìlú Okinawa àti Kyushu, àwọn tó ju àádọ́ta (50) lọ ló fara pa.
sentences.en: In Okinawa and Kyushu, more than 50 people were injured.

sentences.text: Yàtọ̀ síyẹn, ilé àwọn arákùnrin wa tó bà jẹ́ lé ní àádọ́ta (50).
sentences.en: Over 50 homes of our brothers sustained damage.

sentences.text: Ẹ̀ka ọ́fíìsì wa ní Japan sọ pé kò sí Ẹlẹ́rìí Jèhófà kankan tó bá ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà lọ.
sentences.en: The Japan branch has confirmed that no Jehovah’s Witnesses died.

sentences.text: Àyẹ̀wò àkọ́kọ́ tí wọ́n ṣe fi hàn pé Gbọ̀ngàn Ìjọba mẹ́rìnlélógójì (44) ló bà jẹ́.
sentences.en: Initial assessments also indicate that 44 Kingdom Halls have been damaged.

sentences.text: Gbọ̀ngàn ìwòran Noevir Stadium Kobe
sentences.en: The Noevir Stadium Kobe

sentences.text: Inú àwọn ará ń dùn bí wọ́n ṣe gba Bíbélì Ìtumọ̀ Ayé Tuntun tiwọn
sentences.en: Brothers and sisters happy to receive their personal copy of the revised New World Translation

sentences.text: Ọdún márùndínláàádọ́ta (45) sẹ́yìn la kọ́kọ́ mú Bíbélì Ìtumọ̀ Ayé Tuntun jáde lórílẹ̀-èdè Japan.
sentences.en: The New World Translation has a history in Japan that goes back 45 years. In 1973, Brother Lyman Swingle, who served on the Governing Body, released the Japanese-language New World Translation of the Christian Greek Scriptures at the “Divine Victory” International Assembly in Osaka, Japan.

sentences.text: Ó kéré tán, ilé mọ́kànlélọ́gọ́rin (81) tó jẹ́ tàwọn ará wa ló bà jẹ́.
sentences.en: There are no reports of fatalities among our brothers; however, one sister was injured.

sentences.text: """Ní September 9, 2019 ìjì líle tó ń jẹ́ Faxai jà nítòsí Tokyo, lórílẹ̀-èdè Japan."
sentences.en: """On September 9, 2019, powerful Typhoon Faxai made landfall near Tokyo, Japan."

sentences.text: Ó kéré tán èèyàn mẹ́ta ló pàdánù ẹ̀mí wọn.
sentences.en: At least three people were killed.

sentences.text: Ibẹ̀ ló wà báyìí, tí ara rẹ̀ ti ń yá díẹ̀díẹ̀.
sentences.en: Brother Akhmedov, 61, has been in prison since January 18, 2017, for merely practicing his faith.

sentences.text: "Gbogbo wa là ń yọ̀ torí pé Jèhófà ti gba ìránṣẹ́ rẹ̀ olóòótọ́ sílẹ̀.​—2 Sámúẹ́lì 22:2."""
sentences.en: "We all rejoice that Jehovah rescued his loyal servant.—2 Samuel 22:2."""

sentences.text: Torí pé ó kàn ń sọ ohun tó gbà gbọ́ fáwọn míì ni àwọn aláṣẹ ṣe mú un.
sentences.en: Authorities had arrested him merely for sharing his religious beliefs with others.

sentences.text: A ti gé e kúrú, a sì kọ́ ọ lọ́nà tó máa jẹ́ kó ṣe kedere.
sentences.en: This is a condensed transcript of the conversation that has been edited for clarity.

sentences.text: OPI: Arákùnrin Akhmedov, a máa kọ́kọ́ fẹ́ mọ̀ sí i nípa yín.
sentences.en: OPI: To begin with, we would like to learn more about you, Brother Akhmedov.

sentences.text: Ìgbà wo lẹ di Ẹlẹ́rìí Jèhófà?
sentences.en: When did you become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses?

sentences.text: Kí n tó kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ òtítọ́, mi ò gbà pé Ọlọ́run wà.
sentences.en: Before I learned the truth, I was an atheist.

sentences.text: Ọ̀pọ̀ ọdún ni mi ò fi gba Ọlọ́run gbọ́, mi ò sì ṣe ẹ̀sìn kankan.
sentences.en: For many years, I didn’t believe in anyone or anything.

sentences.text: Lọ́jọ́ tá a kọ́kọ́ jọ sọ̀rọ̀, mo sọ fún un pé: ‘Ìbéèrè kan ṣoṣo ni màá bi ẹ́.
sentences.en: During our first discussion, I told him: ‘I am going to ask you only one question.

sentences.text: Tí ìdáhùn rẹ bá tẹ́ mi lọ́rùn, àá dọ̀rẹ́, àá sì jọ máa bá ọ̀rọ̀ wa lọ.
sentences.en: If I’m satisfied with your answer, we’ll be friends and continue our discussions.

sentences.text: Mo wá bi Arákùnrin Veslav léèrè ohun tó máa ń ṣẹlẹ̀ sí àwọn tó ti kú.
sentences.en: I then asked Brother Veslav what happens to the dead.

sentences.text: Nígbà tí mo kà á, mo rí i pé òtítọ́ nìyí.
sentences.en: When I read the verse, I realized that this was the truth.

sentences.text: Torí náà mo gbà pé kó máa wá, kó sì máa kọ́ mi kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ Bíbélì.
sentences.en: I agreed to meet him again and study the Bible.

sentences.text: Bẹ́ ẹ ṣe kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ Bíbélì nìyẹn, tẹ́ ẹ sì ṣèrìbọmi lọ́dún 2005.
sentences.en: So, you studied the Bible and were eventually baptized in 2005.

sentences.text: Ẹ jẹ́ ká fi ìyókù lẹ̀ ná, ká sọ̀rọ̀ nípa ohun tó ṣẹlẹ̀ káwọn aláṣẹ tó mú yín.
sentences.en: Now let’s fast forward to the events that preceded your arrest.

sentences.text: Láàárín oṣù mélòó kan, ẹ máa ń lọ bá wọn jíròrò látinú Bíbélì.
sentences.en: Over the course of a few months, you met with them several times to discuss the Bible.

sentences.text: Mafiza Akhmedov: Ìgbà kan wà témi náà wà níbi tí wọ́n ti ń ṣe ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́.
sentences.en: Mafiza Akhmedov: Once, I also sat in on their Bible study.

sentences.text: Àmọ́ mo rí i pé ohun tí mo sọ bà wọ́n, ara wọn ò sì lélẹ̀.
sentences.en: My comments clearly made them uncomfortable.

sentences.text: TA: Ìgbà tí ìgbẹ́jọ́ bẹ̀rẹ̀ ni mo tó mọ̀ pé àwọn ọlọ́pàá KNB ni wọ́n ń bá ṣiṣẹ́.
sentences.en: TA: I only learned that they were cooperating with the KNB during the court hearing.

sentences.text: Àmọ́ ohun tó wá ṣẹlẹ̀ yà mí lẹ́nu, síbẹ̀ mi ò bẹ̀rù.
sentences.en: I was quite surprised by the turn of events, but I was not afraid.

sentences.text: Báwo ló ṣe rí lára yín?
sentences.en: How did that verdict affect you?

sentences.text: Torí náà, mo pinnu pé bó ti wù kó pẹ́ tó, màá dúró.
sentences.en: I was determined to wait as long as it took.

sentences.text: Arábìnrin Mafiza, báwo lọ̀rọ̀ yìí ṣe rí lára yín lásìkò yẹn?
sentences.en: Mafiza, how did you feel during this time?

sentences.text: MA: Ẹ̀rù bà mí gan-an, ìbànújẹ́ sì dorí mi kodò.
sentences.en: MA: I was terrified and deeply depressed.

sentences.text: Kí lohun míì tó tún ràn yín lọ́wọ́ nígbà tí ọkọ yín wà lẹ́wọ̀n?
sentences.en: What else helped you during the time your husband was imprisoned?

sentences.text: MA: Àwọn ará lọ́kùnrin lóbìnrin ràn mí lọ́wọ́ gan-an.
sentences.en: MA: The brothers and sisters really helped me.

sentences.text: Kódà, àwọn ọ̀tẹlẹ̀múyẹ́ ń ṣọ́ ilé wa, wọ́n sì ń ṣọ́ àwọn nǹkan tá à ń ṣe.
sentences.en: The KNB were monitoring our house and activities.

sentences.text: Àmọ́ lọ́jọ́ kan, alàgbà kan àti ìyàwó ẹ̀ wá wò mí, ìṣírí ńlá gbáà ló jẹ́ fún mi.
sentences.en: Then one day, an elder and his wife came to visit, and it was a tremendous boost for me.

sentences.text: Mo bi wọ́n pé, ‘Ṣé ẹ̀rù ò bà yín láti wá síbí ni?’
sentences.en: When I asked them, ‘Aren’t you afraid to come here?’

sentences.text: Wọ́n dáhùn pé, ‘Kí ló fẹ́ máa bà wá lẹ́rù?
sentences.en: They responded, ‘Why would we be afraid?

sentences.text: Níbi táyé dé yìí, kò ṣòro rárá fáwọn aláṣẹ láti rí wa mú.
sentences.en: Nowadays, the authorities can track us through our phones.

sentences.text: Wọ́n de Arákùnrin Akhmedov mọ́ bẹ́ẹ̀dì nílé ìwòsàn ní Almaty kó tó di pé wọ́n tú u sílẹ̀.
sentences.en: Brother Akhmedov chained to a hospital bed in Almaty shortly before his release.

sentences.text: Mo sì rí bó ṣe dáhùn àdúrà mi.
sentences.en: His answers to my prayers were obvious.

sentences.text: Kò fi mí sílẹ̀, torí mi ò mọ̀ ọ́n lára pé mo dá wà nínú ẹ̀wọ̀n.
sentences.en: He supported me, and I did not feel that I was alone in prison.

sentences.text: Kíka Bíbélì náà ràn mí lọ́wọ́.
sentences.en: Bible reading also assisted me.

sentences.text: Nínú ọ̀kan lára àwọn ọgbà ẹ̀wọ̀n yẹn, Bíbélì wà lárọ̀ọ́wọ́tó mi ní gbogbo ìgbà.
sentences.en: In one of the prisons, I had a Bible available to me at all times.

sentences.text: Mo tún rántí ọ̀rọ̀ arákùnrin tó kọ́ mi lẹ́kọ̀ọ́ Bíbélì.
sentences.en: I also remembered the words of the brother who studied the Bible with me.

sentences.text: Ó máa ń sọ pé kò yẹ kí ìṣòro tá à ń kojú máa dẹ́rù bà wá.
sentences.en: He used to say that we should not be afraid of the challenges we face. I remember asking him: ‘Why should I not be afraid?

sentences.text: Mo rántí pé mo bi wọ́n pé: ‘Báwo ni mi ò ṣe ní bẹ̀rù?
sentences.en: What if the challenge is difficult and terrifying?’

sentences.text: Mo bẹ̀rù ọgbà ẹ̀wọ̀n gan-an.
sentences.en: I was terrified of prisons.

sentences.text: Ṣé àǹfààní ẹ̀ wá yọ láti wàásù fún àwọn kan nígbà tẹ́ ẹ wà lẹ́wọ̀n?
sentences.en: So did you get a chance to witness to some while you were in prison?

sentences.text: Ó wá bi mí pé, ‘Kí lorúkọ Ọlọ́run?’ Mo ní, ‘Jèhófà lorúkọ Ọlọ́run.’
sentences.en: When I came into his office, he said, ‘I know that you are one of Jehovah’s Witnesses, so don’t even think about preaching to me!’ To which I replied, ‘I have no such intention.’

sentences.text: Ó wá béèrè pé, ‘Kí ló wá dé táwọn Oníṣọ́ọ̀ṣì Ọ́tọ́dọ́ọ̀sì fi gbà pé òun ni Ọlọ́run?’
sentences.en: He continued, ‘Then, who is Jesus? Isn’t he God?’ I said, ‘No, he is God’s son.’

sentences.text: Mo ní, ‘Àwọn náà ni wọ́n máa lè dáhùn ẹ̀.’
sentences.en: He then asked, ‘Why, then, do Orthodox Christians believe he is God?’ And I said, ‘You should ask them about that.’

sentences.text: Dókítà kan tó jẹ́ afìṣemọ̀rònú ẹ̀dá wá ṣèbẹ̀wò sọ́dọ̀ àwọn ẹlẹ́wọ̀n.
sentences.en: A psychologist had come to the prison to visit the inmates.

sentences.text: Gbogbo wa la láǹfààní láti sọ èrò wa.
sentences.en: Everyone had an opportunity to share their opinion.

sentences.text: Dókítà náà béèrè pé, ‘Èrò ta nìyẹn?’ Mo ní, ‘Èrò Jèhófà Ọlọ́run ni, ẹni tó dá ọmọ aráyé.
sentences.en: The psychologist asked, ‘Whose opinion is that?’ To which I replied, ‘It is the opinion of Jehovah God, the one who created mankind.

sentences.text: Èèyàn méjì ló sọ pé wọ́n á ṣègbéyàwó; wọn ò ju méjì lọ.’
sentences.en: It mentions only two people; no more.’

sentences.text: Mo ní: ‘Jésù ló sọ̀rọ̀ yìí.
sentences.en: I said: ‘These are the words of Jesus.

passages.title: Thousands march in London calling for David Cameron's resignation over tax affairs ⚠
paragraphs: Ìflrúnú hàn bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ago mọ́kànlá (UTC+1) ní Whitehall ní wájú ẹnu ọ̀nà ilé iṣẹ́ ọlọ́pàá sí òpópónà Downing, ilé àrẹ orílẹ̀ èdè. Ní kété lẹ́yìn agogo mọ́kànlá, àwọn tó ń fi èhónú hàn dí ojú pópónà ọ̀nà tóbá àríwá jádé ní gbòngàn funfun.

Ní aago mọ́kànlá kọjá ogún ìsẹ́jù, iléeṣẹ́ ọlọ́ọ̀pá tí ní káwọn olùsèfẹ̀hónúhàn sún sẹ́yìn, sọ pé wọ́n nílò láti sètò ìfẹ̀hónúhàn pẹ̀lú súnkẹrẹ fàkẹrẹ tó ń kó jọ. Ní nǹkan bí i aago mọ́kànlá kọjá ìṣẹ́jú mọ́kàndínlọ́gbọ̀n, ìfẹ̀hónù dé Whitehall, kọjá Trafalgar lójú ọ̀nà èbúté, kọjá Aldwych ó tún lọ sí òkè Kingsway lójúọ̀nà Holborn níbití ẹgbẹ́ Conservative ti ń se ètò ọlọ́dọọdún láwọn yàrá ilé ìtura ńlá Grand Connaught .
en: The protest started around 11:00 local time (UTC+1) on Whitehall opposite the police-guarded entrance to Downing Street, the Prime Minister's official residence. Just after 11:00, protesters blocked traffic on the northbound carriage in Whitehall.

At 11:20, the police asked the protesters to move back on to the pavement, stating that they needed to balance the right to protest with the traffic building up. Around 11:29, the protest moved up Whitehall, past Trafalgar Square, along the Strand, passing by Aldwych and up Kingsway towards Holborn where the Conservative Party were holding their Spring Forum in the Grand Connaught Rooms hotel.

Nadal ní àmì ayò 88% ní bọ́ọ̀lù náà tó sì gba àmì ayò 76 ní abala àkọ́kọ́. Lẹ́yìn ìdìje, Ọba Clay ní “inú mi dùn láti padà sínú ìdíje tó gbẹ̀yìn àwọn ètò ńlá. Mo wá láti gbìyànjú kí n lè jẹri.”
en: Nadal's head to head record against the Canadian is 7–2. He recently lost against Raonic in the Brisbane Open.

Nadal bagged 88% net points in the match winning 76 points in the first serve. After the match, King of Clay said, "I am just excited about being back in the final rounds of the most important events. I am here to try to win this."

passages.title: Investigation of Deutsche Bank headquarters spills into second day ⚠
paragraphs: “Pépà Panama” jẹ́ bí àkójọ ọ̀rọ̀ fún àwọn ìwé mílíọ̀nù mẹ́wàá láti iléeṣẹ́ òfin Panama Mossack Fonseca, èyí tó hàn de fáwọn oníròyìn lọ́dun 2016. Awon iIwe naa fihan ile ifowopamo merinla to ran awon onisowo olola pa ilopo bilioni owo Amerika mo lati le sa fun owo ori ati awon ofin miin.

Ìwé ìròyìn Ilẹ̀ gẹ̀ẹ́sì The Guardian da lábàá pé kí ilé ìfowópama Deutsche darí ìdámkta ti àwọn ilé iṣk shell tó tó 1200 tí wọ́n lò láti jẹ́ kí èyí ṣe é ṣe. Ìfẹ̀hónúhàn wáyé káàkiri àgbáyé, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìbánijẹ́jọ́ ọ̀daràn áti àwọn òlórí ìjọba Iceland àti Pakistan kọ̀wé fìposílè.
en: "Panama Papers" is an umbrella term for roughly ten million documents from Panamanian law firm Mossack Fonseca, leaked to the press in spring 2016. The documents showed fourteen banks helped wealthy clients hide billions of US dollars of wealth to avoid taxes and other regulations.

British newspaper The Guardian suggested Deutsche Bank controlled roughly a third of the 1200 shell companies used to accomplish this. There were protests worldwide, several criminal prosecutions, and the leaders of the governments of Iceland and Pakistan both resigned.

passages.title: Ma Ying-jeou wins 2008 Taiwan presidential election ⚠
paragraphs: A bi ni Hong Kong. Ma kẹkọ ni ile iwe giga New York ati ile ẹkọ imọ ofin Harvard bẹẹni o si fi igba kan ni iwe igbelu Ameria “kaadi alawọ ewe”. Hsieh fi soro nigba ibo pe ma le sa kuro ninu ilu nigba wahala.
Hsieh náà jiyàn pé Ma tó má n rẹwà nínú àwòrán jẹ́ àṣà ju oge lọ. Pẹ̀lú pẹ̀lú àwọn ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan an Ma yege dada lori itage ti o já fún ìbálòpọ̀ fini fini pẹ̀lú òkè odò Ṣáínà.
en: Born in Hong Kong, Ma studied at New York University and Harvard Law School and once held an American permanent resident "green card". Hsieh implied during the election that Ma might flee the country during a time of crisis.
Hsieh also argued that the photogenic Ma was more style than substance. Despite these accusations, Ma won handily on a platform advocating closer ties with the Chinese mainland.

passages.title: National Hockey League news: March 22, 2008 ⚠
paragraphs: Agbábọ̀lù Tòní ní Alex Overchkin ti Washington Capitals. Ó gbá góòlù 2, asisti 2 ni eré tí Wọ́ṣíntíni ti borí àwọn Trasha Atlanta pẹ̀lú 5-3.

Ìrànwọ́ alẹ́ àkọ́kọ́ Ovechkin nínú ìborí ẹrẹ́ ibi-afẹ́dẹ́ nípasẹ̀ rookie Nicklas Backstrom; àmì ayo rẹ̀ kejì ní alé nàà ní ọgọ́ta rẹ ní abala yẹn,tó jẹ́ òṣèrè àkọ́kọ́ ;tó ma gba ọgọ́ta tàbí jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ ní abala náà láti 1995-96,nígbàtí Jagr àti Mario Lemieux dé ìpèle tó ní àmì.
en: Today's Player of the Day is Alex Ovechkin of the Washington Capitals. He had 2 goals and 2 assists in Washington's 5-3 win over the Atlanta Thrashers.

Ovechkin's first assist of the night was on the game-winning goal by rookie Nicklas Backstrom; his second goal of the night was his 60th of the season, becoming the first player to score 60 or more goals in a season since 1995-96, when Jaromir Jagr and Mario Lemieux each reached that milestone.

passages.title: American children's show Reading Rainbow ends 26 year run ⚠
paragraphs: Ètò PBS ní tó àmì ẹ̀yẹ Emmy tó lé ní dọ́sìnì méjì, Ó sì ma ń kéré jú òpópónà Sesame àti agbègbè ọ̀gbẹ́ni Rogers lọ. Ìkọ̀ọ̀kan ẹ́písòòdù yìí yó ò fojúsun àkórí nínú ìwé kan pàtó, tí a ó sì má a sàmúnlò àwọn àkórí yìí nípa lílo ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìtàn.

Àfihàn kọ̀ọ̀kan náà yíò tún gba àwọn ọmọ ní ìmòràn lórí àwọn ìwé láti múlò tí wọn bá lọ sí yàrá ìkàwẹ́. Johanu Granti, lati WNED Bufalo (o n ka oju redio ile Osumo) wipe “Kika Osumo ko awon omode idi ti o ye ki won fi kawe,...ife iwe - [ere naa] fisokan aawon omode lati gbe iwe ka..”
Àwọn kan gbàgbọ́, pẹ̀lú john Grant, pé àti funding crunch àti sísún ní ẹ̀kọ́ ìmòye ètò orí amóhùnmáwòrán dási láti parí eré náà.
en: The PBS show has more than two-dozen Emmy awards, and its run is shorter only than Sesame Street and Mister Rogers' Neighborhood. Each episode of the show would focus on a theme in a specific book and then explore that theme through multiple stories.

Each show would also provide recommendations for books that children should look for when they went to their library. John Grant, from WNED Buffalo (Reading Rainbow's home station) said "Reading Rainbow taught kids why to read,... the love of reading — [the show] encouraged kids to pick up a book and to read."
It is believed by some, including John Grant, that both the funding crunch and a shift in the philosophy of educational television programming contributed to ending the series.

passages.title: Judge orders Baltimore City prison to produce plan for improvement
paragraphs: Láàrin oṣù mẹ́ta tó kọjá, àwọn bí i ọgọ́rin tí wọ́n fi páńpẹ́ òfin gbé ni wọ́n ti dásílẹ̀ kúrò ní ọgbà Central Booking láláì fojú balé ẹjọ́. Nínú osù kẹrin ọdún yí adájó Glynn pa àṣę ìkánilọ́wọ́kò onígbàkanná pé kí ilé iṣẹ́ náà tú àwọn tí wọ́n tí dè mọ́lẹ̀ fún wákàtí mẹ́rìnlélógún sílẹ̀ lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n gbà wọ́n sọ́dọ̀ tí wọn ò dę rí ìdájọ́ gbà láti ọ̀dọ̀ kọmíṣọ́nà kọ́ọ̀tú.

Kọmíṣíọ́nà se àgbékalẹ̀ owó ìtanràn, tí ó bá bọ́ si, tí ó sì fì ẹ̀sùn tí agbófinró fi kàn múnlẹ̀. Ẹ̀sùn náà ni ó gbé wọnú ẹ̀rọ ayárabíàsá ìpínlẹ̀ tíwọ́n ti ń taná wádìí ẹ̀sùn náà. Ìgbẹ́jọ́ náa sàmí ẹ̀tọ́ afurasí sí ṣíṣe ęjọ́ ní kíá kíá.
en: In the last 3 months, over 80 arrestees were released from the Central Booking facility without being formally charged. In April this year, a temporary restaining order was issued by Judge Glynn against the facility to enforce the release of those held more than 24 hours after their intake who did not receive a hearing by a court commissioner.

The commissioner sets bail, if granted, and formalizes the charges filed by the arresting officer. The charges are then entered into the state's computer system where the case is tracked. The hearing also marks the date for the suspect’s right to a speedy trial.

passages.title: Huge Gay Pride parade held in Brazil
paragraphs: Brazil jẹ orílẹ̀-èdè ìlú ìjọ ẹlẹ́sin Róòmù tó pọ̀jù lọ làgbáyé, bẹ́ẹ̀ sì ní ìjọ ẹlẹ́sìn Róòmù tako ìgbéyàwó akọ pẹ̀lú akọ tàbí abo pẹ̀lú abo . Àpérò àpapọ̀ orílẹ̀èdè Brazil ti jíròrò lórí ìlànà òfin fún ọdún mẹ́wàá àti pé irú ìgbéyàwó ìlú yìí ní ó bá òfin mun ní Rio Grande do Sul.

Olórí ìlú tẹ́lẹ̀ Mata Suplicy ló kọ òfin náà. Òfin tówàlọ́nà náà ti wà lọ́wọ́ Robato Jefasini, lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n ṣàtúnṣe sí. Àwọn afẹ̀hohnúhàn lérò láti gba ìfọwọ́bọ̀wé tó tó 1.2 miliọnu láti fi ṣọwọ́ sí àpérò orílẹ̀èdè ni oṣu kejìl.
en: Brazil is the largest Roman Catholic country on Earth, and the Roman Catholic Church has consistently opposed the legalization of same-sex marriage in the country. The National Congress of Brazil has debated legalization for 10 years, and such civil marriages are currently only legal in Rio Grande do Sul.

The original bill was drafted by former mayor of São Paulo, Marta Suplicy. The proposed legislation, after being amended, is now in the hands of Roberto Jefferson. Protesters hope to collect a petition of 1.2 million signatures to present to the National Congress in November.

passages.title: War between top lawyers in Greece ⚠
paragraphs: Wọ́n ti ti gbajúgbajà amòfin ilẹ Greek, Sakis Kechagioglou àti George Nikolakopoulos mọ́ àhámọ́ ọgbà ẹ̀wọ̀n Korydallus ti Athens, níbí wọ́n se ní wọ́n jẹ̀bi ẹ̀sùn ìwà jẹgúdújẹrá àti àjẹbánu. Fún ìdí èyí,wọ́n ti se àgbéga ìbanilórúkọjẹ́ ńlá tó wáyé láàrin ìlú Greek látara ìlàlójú sáwọn ìwà tí kò bófin mun táwọn adájọ́, agbẹ́jọ́rò, alágbàwí, àtàwọn amòfin ti hù láwọn ọdún tó ti kọjá sẹ́yìn.

Ní ọ̀sẹ̀ díè sẹ́yìn, lẹyìn ìròyìn tí akọròyìn Makis Triantafylopoulos sẹ àtèjádẹ rẹ nínú gbajúgbajà àfihàn tẹlifísàn “Zoungla” ní Alpha TV, ọmọ ẹgbé ilẹ́ ìgbimọ̀ asòfin àti agbẹjórò, Petros Mantouvalos gba ìdáláre bi àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ míràn nínú ofiisi rẹ se lọ́wọ́ nínú ìwà ìbàjẹ́ àti ìlòdì sófin. Síwájú si, adájọ́ gíga Kalousis ti wà lẹ́wòn nítorí o jẹ̀bi èsùn íwá ájẹbánu àti íwá ìbàjẹ́.
en: The famous Greek lawyers, Sakis Kechagioglou and George Nikolakopoulos have been imprisoned in the Athens' jail of Korydallus, as they were found guilty of graft and corruption. As a result of this, a big scandal within the Greek legal community has been raised through the exposure of illegal actions that judges, lawyers, solicitors and attorneys have done during the previous years.

A few weeks ago, after the information published by the journalist Makis Triantafylopoulos in his popular Television show "Zoungla" in Alpha TV, the member of Parliament and lawyer, Petros Mantouvalos was abdicated as members of his office had been involved in illegal graft and corruption. Moreover, top judge Evangelos Kalousis is imprisoned as he found guilty of corruption and degenerate behaviour.

passages.title: Another arrest in Minnesota school shooting
paragraphs: Ìròyìn tàn ká ní agbègbè Red Lake lónìí pé bí ìsìnkú Jeff Weise àti àwọn mẹta nínú mẹsan tó farakásá wáyé wípé ọwọ́ tẹ akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ míràn ní ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú ìbọn yínyìn ní ilé ìwé ti ọjọ̀ kankọkànlélógún Oṣù Kẹta. Àwọn aláṣẹ sọ díẹ́ níorí iṣẹ́ tí wọ́n sì jẹ́rìsí mímú tí wọ́n mú wọn.

Àmọ́sá, èèyàn kan tó mọ̀ nípa ìwaàdí sọ fún iléeṣẹ́ Minneapolis Star-Tribune wípé Louis Jourdain tó jẹ́ ọmọọdún mẹ́rìndínlógún alága ẹ̀yà Red Lake, Floyd Jourdain ni. A kò mọ̀ ní àkókò yí àwọn àyípadà tí wọ́n ma ṣe àti nkan tó jẹ́kí wọ́n rí ọmọ okùnrin náà gbámú, ṣùgbọ́n ètò ilé ẹjọ́ fún ọ̀dọ́ ti bẹ̀rẹ̀.
en: News spread in the Red Lake community today as funerals for Jeff Weise and three of the nine victims were held that another student was arrested in connection with the school shootings of March 21. Authorities said little officially beyond confirming today's arrest.

However, a source with knowledge of the investigation told the Minneapolis Star-Tribune that it was Louis Jourdain, 16-year old son of Red Lake Tribal Chairman Floyd Jourdain. It is not known at this time what charges will be laid or what led authorities to the boy but juvenile proceedings have begun in federal court.

passages.title: Russian military cargo jet crash kills eleven in Siberia
paragraphs: Ọkọ̀ òfuruufún náà ti darí si Irkutsk pèlú àwọn ikọ ọmọ ogun abélé ni ìsàkósa re. A dá ìwádi lẹ̀ lati ṣe ìwád.

Il-76 ṣe pàtàkì púpọ̀ sí ikọ̀ ológun Russia àti Soviet láti 1970, bẹ́ẹ̀ náà sì ni ó ti rí ìjàǹbá ní Russia ní oṣù tó kọjá. Ní ọjọ́ keje osù kẹwàá, ẹ̀rọ ya ibi ìgbéra sọ́tọ, lálàì farapa. ilẹ̀ Russia bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní II-76s ní kéte tí ìjàm̀bá sẹlẹ̀.
en: The aircraft had been headed to Irkutsk and was being operated by interior troops. An inquiry was established to investigate.

The Il-76 has been a major component of both the Russian and Soviet military since the 1970s, and had already seen a serious accident in Russia last month. On October 7 an engine separated on takeoff, without injuries. Russia briefly grounded Il-76s after that accident.

passages.title: Oil spill in Alaska closes 800 miles of pipeline ⚠
paragraphs: Ẹgbẹ̀rin máìlì ọ̀nà ilé epo Trans-Alaska ni ó di títì pa, látàrí ẹgbẹgbẹ̀rún àgbá epo rọ̀bì to jò dànaù ni gúsù Fairbanks, ni Alaska. Ìkùnà iná lẹ́yìn àdánwò dédé lóri ètò àṣẹ-iná, ṣokùnfa kí ihò ìrọ̀rùn ṣí sílẹ̀ epo rọ̀bí sì jò sẹ́gbẹ́ ìdí epo Forti Grili 9.
Ṣíṣí ìdè ná sílẹ̀ jẹ́ kí ;ó ní ìtúsílẹ̀ fún ẹ̀rọ àti ìṣàn epo sí táǹkì 'tó lè di àgbá epo 55,000 mú (2.3 million gallons. Ní ọ̀sán ọjọ́rú, táǹkì náà jò bóyá nítorí thermal expansion nínu táǹkì.
ipele keji aye ikeru si miran ti o ni anfani lati gba 104,500 bareli ko i ti kun de enu.
en: 800 miles of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System were closed down following a spill of thousands of barrels of crude oil south of Fairbanks, Alaska. A power failure following a routine fire-command system test caused relief valves to open and crude oil overflowed near the Fort Greely pump station 9.

The valves opening allowed a pressure release for the system and oil flowed on a pad to a tank that can hold 55,000 barrels (2.3 million gallons). As of Wednesday afternoon, the tank vents were still leaking probably from thermal expansion inside the tank.
Another secondary containment area below the tanks capable of holding 104,500 barrels was not yet filled to capacity.

passages.title: Effect of sanctions 'like war' says Iran's Ahmadinejad ⚠
paragraphs: Ọ̀rọ̀ ọ̀hún lórí ètò amóhùnmáwòrán, ni ìgbà àkọ́kọ́ tí abẹnugan àgbà ilẹ̀ Iran kan gbà pé ìbáwí tí wọn fi léde ní ip. Wọn ti se àgbékalẹ̀ òfin fi de ìwọ̀n owó bẹ́ẹ̀ àjọ ìsọ̀kan ilẹ̀ yúròpù sì ti gbegi lé títa epo rọ̀bì sí ìta, ní èyí tí ètò ọrọ̀ ajé àwọn ara Iran fi ń gbà ìdá ọgọ́rin nínú owó̀ ilẹ̀ òkèrè wọn tó ń wọlé.

Nínú àkọọ́lẹ̀ olóosòṣù rẹ tó jáde gbèyìǹ, OPEC ní ìkó epo jáde ti já wálẹ̀ fún bí i dẹ́kéèdèméjì bíi mílíọ̀nù mẹ́jì ó lé ẹgbẹ̀rin ẹgbẹ̀rún àgbá lóòjọ́. Alakoso ilu Ayatola Ali Kamneyi ti fi ifojule epo robi we “idẹkun” to bẹrẹ ki rogbodiyan musulumi ti Irani bẹrẹ ni 1979 ati ti o jẹ nkan ti o yẹ ki ilu gba ara rẹ la lọwọ e.
en: The comments, live on television, were the first time that senior Iranian sources have admitted that the sanctions are having any effect. They include financial restrictions and a ban by the European Union on the export of crude oil, from which the Iranian economy receives 80% of its foreign income.

In its most recent monthly report, OPEC said exports of crude had fallen to their lowest level for two decades at 2.8 million barrels per day. The country's supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has described the dependency on oil as "a trap" dating from before Iran's Islamic revolution in 1979 and from which the country should free itself.

passages.title: Distributed computing to get "interstellar project" ⚠
paragraphs: Bí kápísù bá dé inú ayé tí ó wọ inú afẹ́fẹ́, àti ní ǹkan bi í aago márùn ún òwúrọ̀ (àkókò ìlà òrùn) èyí ni wọ́n ń retí wípé yíó sàfihàn eré ráńpẹ́ fáwọn èèyàn tó wà ní àríwá California, Oregon, Nevada, àti Utah. Kapsuli naa a jo bii irawo to n fo koja ofurufu.

Kápísù náà yíò rìn bí i kìlómítà méjìlá ó lé mẹ́jọ tàbí máàlì mẹ́jọ láàrin ìṣẹ́jú kan, ó yára tó láti lọ sí San Francisco títí lọ Los Angeles láàrin ìṣẹ́jú kan. Stardust yíò gbé àkọsílẹ̀ tí ó ga jùlọ kalẹ̀ pẹ̀lú bí ó se ba àkọ́sílẹ̀ ti oṣù karùn ún ọdún 1969 jẹ́ ní àkókò ìpadàbọ̀ Apollo X.
“O ma si lo sori apa iwo orun Kalifonia Ariwa o de ma tan ina si oku orun lati Kalifonia tit de aarin Orgoni lo si Nefada ati Idaho sinu Uta,” Tom Duxbury, oludari ise ErupeIrawo wi.
en: When the capsule gets to Earth and enters the atmosphere, at about 5am (eastern time), it is expected to put on quite a light show for folks in Northern California, Oregon, Nevada, and Utah. The capsule will look much like a shooting star going across the sky.

The capsule will be traveling at about 12.8 km or 8 miles per second, fast enough to go from San Francisco to Los Angeles in one minute. Stardust will set a new all-time record for being the fastest spacecraft to return to Earth, breaking the previous record set in May of 1969 during the return of the Apollo X command module.

“It will move over the west coast of northern California and will light the sky from California through central Oregon and on through Nevada and Idaho and into Utah,” Tom Duxbury, Stardust's project manager said.

passages.title: The Onion: An interview with 'America's Finest News Source'
paragraphs: Sááju Ètò Ojoojúmọ́ àtì Àbábọ̀ Colbert, Heck àti Johnson ti ma ń wòye àgbéjáde tí yíó fara jọ ìròyìn—àti ìjábọ̀ ìròyìn—nígbàtí wọ́n jẹ́ akẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ ní UW ní 1988. Láti ìgbà tí wọ́n dáa sílẹ̀ Alubosa ti di ìròyìn ẹlẹ́fẹ́ tó dáju, pẹ̀lú ìtẹ̀jáde, saiti to fa ojú alejò 5,000,000 ọ̀tọ̀tọ̀ ní Owara, ipolowo tara eni, ilé iṢẹ́ ìròyìn tò ṢiṢe fún wákàtí 24, Podkasti, àti ìwé ìmọ̀ ayé - Atlasi ti a Ṣẹ̀ tún gbéjáde tí apé ni “Aye wa tí ò ní Làakáyè”.

Al Gore áti ọ̀gágun Tommy Franks láìfọtápè ka àwọn àkọlẹ́ ti´ oníkàlùkùn fẹ́ràn (Ti Gore jé ìgbà tí Onion sọ ìròyìn wípẹ́ òhun áti Tipper n ní ìbálòpọ̀ tó dàra jùlo ní ayé wọn lẹ́yìn ìjákulẹ̀ nínú ìdìbò fún ààrẹ áti igbá kẹji ti 2000). Púpọ̀ nínú àwọn oǹkọ̀wé wọn ti lọ ní ipa lórí ìròyìn ìfiniṣẹ̀fẹ̀ Jon Stewart àti Stephen Colbert.
en: Long before The Daily Show and The Colbert Report, Heck and Johnson envisioned a publication that would parody the news—and news reporting—when they were students at UW in 1988. Since its inception, The Onion has become a veritable news parody empire, with a print edition, a website that drew 5,000,000 unique visitors in the month of October, personal ads, a 24 hour news network, podcasts, and a recently launched world atlas called Our Dumb World.

Al Gore and General Tommy Franks casually rattle off their favorite headlines (Gore's was when The Onion reported he and Tipper were having the best sex of their lives after his 2000 Electoral College defeat). Many of their writers have gone on to wield great influence on Jon Stewart and Stephen Colbert's news parody shows.

passages.title: Red tide affects South Padre Island, Mexico ⚠
paragraphs: Àìsàn Red tide ma ń wáyé bí̀ Karenia brevis bá wọ́pọ̀ ju bí ó se yẹ lọ, ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ àdéyébá tí wọ́n pè ní kòkòrò inú omi. Àwọn ohun àdáyébá lè kórajọ láti pèsè ààyè tó dára, èyí tí yíó fún àwọn ewé yìí láàyè àti pọ̀ níye dáradára.
Àwọn ewé ń pèsè oró tó lè sèpalára sọ́fun àwọn èèyàn àti ẹja. Eja maa n saba ku nitori awon oro to ropo ninu omi.
Àwọn omi tí kò dára tí atẹ́gùn àti ìjì ti gbé lọ sínu afẹ́fẹ́ lè ṣe ìpalára fénìyàn tí ó bá fà á símú.
en: Red tide is caused by a higher than normal concentration of Karenia brevis, a naturally-occurring single-celled marine organism. Natural factors can intersect to produce ideal conditions, allowing this algae to increase in number dramatically.
The algae produces a neurotoxin that can disable nerves in both humans and fish. Fish often die because of the high concentrations of the toxin in the waters.
Humans can be affected by breathing affected water taken into the air by wind and waves.

passages.title: Nationalised bank Northern Rock sold to Virgin Money ⚠
paragraphs: Ilé ìfowópamọ́ Northern Rock ti di ti ará ìlú ní ọdún 2008, lẹ́yìn ìlanilójú pé iléẹṣẹ́ náà ti gba ìrànwọ́ pàjáwìrì láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba ilẹ̀ UK. Northen Rock ti béèrè fún àtìlẹyìn látàrí ohun tó ṣẹlẹ̀ nínú àjálù ẹ̀yáwo aláìleèsanpadà ní ọdún 2007.

Ẹgbẹ́ Virgin ti Sir Richard Branson ní ìdù fún ǹkan ti ilé ìfowópamọ́ ti kọ̀ sílẹ̀ ṣáájú ìyípòpadà ilé ìfowópamọ́. Nígbàtí ètò ìsọdi orílẹ̀èdè wáyé lọ́dún 2010, wọ́n pín ilé ìfowópamọ́sí gíga Northern Rock plc kúrò lára ‘báńkì burúkú’ Northern Rock (ìsàkóso ohun ìní).
Wúndíá ti ra “ilé ìfowópamọ́sí” ti Northern Rock, kì í se iléeṣẹ́ tó ń sàkóso ohun ìní.
en: The Northern Rock bank had been nationalised in 2008 following the revelation that the company had received emergency support from the UK Government. Northern Rock had required support due to its exposure during the subprime mortgage crisis in 2007.

Sir Richard Branson's Virgin Group had a bid for the bank rejected prior to the bank’s nationalisation. In 2010, while nationalised, the current high street bank Northern Rock plc was split from the ‘bad bank’, Northern Rock (Asset Management).
Virgin have only purchased the ‘good bank’ of Northern Rock, not the asset management company.

passages.title: Meteorites in Morocco found to be from Mars ⚠
paragraphs: Eyi ni yio je igba karun ninu itan ti awon eniyan ti se akiyesi pe awon oun ti a fi idi re mu le pelu kemica lati je ohun ija n jabo si ori ile aye. Láàrin orísìírìsìí òkúta àti àwọn nǹkan tí ye wọ́n tó ẹgbẹ̀rún mẹ́rìnlélógún tí a mọ̀ tí ó sọ̀kalẹ̀ sílé ayé láti ojú òfúrufú bí i mẹ́rìnlélógún ni a ti fìdí rẹ múlẹ̀ láti jẹ martian..

Maarundinlogun lára awon òkúta wọ̀nyí ni òjò mitiyo Agëmọ tó kọjá fà. Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn àpáta tó ṣọ̀wọ́n ní ayé ní wọ́n ń tà láàrin ẹgbẹ̀rún mọ́kànlá dọ́là ti lẹ̀ US sí ẹgbẹ̀rún méjìlélógún ó lé ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́gbẹ̀ta dọ́là fún ounce kan, èyí tí ó dàbí ìlọ́pọ mẹ́wàá jú iye góòlù lọ.
en: This is believed to be the fifth time in history that people have observed what turned out to be chemically confirmed martian material falling to Earth. Out of the approximately 24,000 known meteorites to have fallen to Earth, only about 34 have been verified to be martian in origin.

Fifteen of these rocks are attributed to the meteorite shower last July. Some of the rocks, which are very rare on Earth, are being sold from US$11,000 to $22,500 per ounce, which is about ten times more than the cost of gold.

passages.title: Matt Kenseth wins third NASCAR Sprint Cup race of 2012 ⚠
paragraphs: Lẹ́yìn ere náà Keseloski ṣi wà nípo kíní Ìdíje Awakọ̀ pẹ̀lú pointi 2,250. Ojú àmì méje ló fi dín, John gbé ipò kejì pẹ̀lú 2,243.

Ni ipo keta Amlini ni dinku pointi 20, sugbon o saju Boya pelu maarun. Kani ati Truesi, Jr. gba ipo karun ati kefa pelu 2,220 ati 2,207 ni kookan won. Stewart, Gordon, Kenseth, àti Harvick parí ìdíje olúborí awakọ ní ipò mẹ́wàá àkọ́kọ́̀ níbi eréje se ku mẹ́rin ní sáà .
en: Following the race, Keselowski remains the Drivers' Championship leader with 2,250 points. Seven points behind, Johnson is second with 2,243.

In third, Hamlin is twenty points behind, but five ahead of Bowyer. Kahne and Truex, Jr. are fifth and sixth respectively with 2,220 and 2,207 points. Stewart, Gordon, Kenseth, and Harvick round out the top-ten positions for the Drivers' Championship with four races remaining in the season.

passages.title: US Navy ship damages Tubbataha Reef National Park ⚠
paragraphs: Ọmo ogun US tún sọ pé wọ́n ṣe ìwádìí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà. Won tubo foro le pe, “Awon to alaakoso oko oju omi ti n sa agbara won lati mo ona to dara ju lati yo oko naa laisi ifarapa.
Maini oniwonn Afenja ma n takoiwon oko oju omi, oko naa wa loju ona to n lo si Puweto Princesa ni Palawaani. A fún Ẹgbẹ́ Keje àwọn Sójà Ojú Omi Amerika tó wà ní Sasebo Nagasaki, Jépaani.
en: The US Navy also said they were investigating the incident. They also said in a statement, "The crew is currently working to determine the best method of safely extracting the ship".
An Avenger class mine countermeasures ship, the ship was on its way to Puerto Princesa in Palawan. It is assigned to the U.S. Navy’s Seventh Fleet and based in Sasebo, Nagasaki in Japan.

passages.title: Texas governor and health officials address public regarding Ebola case ⚠
paragraphs: Pelu awon osise naa, o da awon olugbe Tegsasi loju pe won ti n gbe awon igbese lati daabo bo ailewu awujo eda. Perry dìídì sọ wípé, “àwọn ibi díẹ̀ ló wà ni ayé tí ó ni ohun tí wọn nílò láti kọjú ìṣòro ọ̀rọ̀ yì.”
Gómìnà náà tún sọpé, Lónìí, a gbọ́ pé a ti rí àwọn ọmọ ilé ìwé tó ti farakan aláìsàn náà.” Ó tún tẹ̀síwájú sọ wípé “ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí lágbára. Fọkànbalẹ̀ wípé ètò wa ti ń síṣẹ́ bí ó se y.”
en: Accompanied by those officials, he assured Texas citizens that steps were being taken to protect the public's safety. Perry specifically said, "There are few places in the world better equipped to meet the challenge that is posed in this case."

The governor also stated, "Today, we learned that some school aged children have been identified as having had contact with the patient." He went on to say, "This case is serious. Rest assured that our system is working as well as it should."

passages.title: Beverly Hall, indicted public school superintendent, dies aged 68 ⚠
paragraphs: Nígbàtí o lò ní Atlanta ó rí ìyìn àwọn ìdánilójú pàtàkì gbà wọ́n dẹ̀ daamo fún iṣé àtinúdá to ṣe fún ìwé kíkọ́ ti ìlú. Ní ọdún 2009 wọ́n fún ní oyè Alábójútó àgbà Orílẹ̀ èdè ti Ọdún.
Ní àsìkò àmì ẹ̀yẹ̀ náà, ilé-ẹkọ́ Atlanta ti rí ìlọsíwájú lórí èsì ìdánwò. Leyin igba die, iwe iroyin to je ti ofin ti Atlanta gbe iroyinto safihan isoro pelu esi abajade.

Ìjábọ̀ ṣàfihàn èsì ìdánwó pé ó ti tètè lọ sókè, ò sí jẹ́ kí ilé ìwé náà kófìrí àwọn ìṣòro abẹ́lé ṣùgbọ́n wọn kò ṣiṣk lórí ìwádìí wọn. Ẹ̀rí fi hàn wípé wọn ti fi ọwọ́ kan àwọn bébà àyẹ̀wò àti Gbọǹgàn pẹ̀lú àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ètò ẹ̀kọ́ mẹ́rìnlelọ́gbọ̀n ní ọdún 201.
en: She gained critical acclaim during her time in Atlanta and was recognized for innovative urban education. In 2009 she was awarded the title of National Superintendent of the Year.
At the time of the award, Atlanta schools had seen a large improvement on test scores. Shortly after, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution published a report showing problems with test results.

The report showed test scores had increased implausibly fast, and alleged the school internally detected problems but didn't act on the findings. Evidence thereafter indicated test papers were tampered with Hall, along with 34 other education officials, was indicted in 2013.

passages.title: President of Costa Rica contracts H1N1 swine flu ⚠
paragraphs: Àbájádẹ àyèwò fihàn pé Arias ti kó aàrùn náà ní íwọn bíntín, Òjísé Ààrẹ Rodrigo Arias fi síta. Ara ààrẹ̀ ti balẹ̀, lóòótọ́ ó sì má a wà ní ìyaraẹnisọ́tọ̀ nílé fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọjọ́.
“Leyin iba ati egbo onafun, araa mi ya lati se gbogbo ise naa lati ilu pelu ero ibanisoro ati ayelujara.  “Mo ní ìrẹ̀tí láti padà sí ibi isẹ́ mi ní Ọjọ́ Ajé,” Arias wi nínú àtẹ̀jádẹ.
en: Arias tested positive for a mild case of the virus, Presidential Minister Rodrigo Arias said. The president's condition is stable, though he will be isolated at home for several days.
"Apart from the fever and a sore throat, I feel well and in good shape to carry out my work by telecommuting. I expect to return to all my duties on Monday," Arias said in a statement.

passages.title: Remnants of Hurricane Felicia affect Hawaii
paragraphs: Felisia, to fi ìgbà kan jẹ ìjì to wà lórí Abala 4 ní Ojú Ìwọ̀n Ìjì Nla ti Saffir-Simpson, rẹlẹ̀ sí ìjì nla ti ọ̀nà òòorùn kí o to papà fónká ní Ọjọ́ Ìségun. Ìyókù rẹ̀ má dàbí òjò ní island, ṣùgbọ́n kòsí omiyalé tí a ti gbọ́.
Ìwọ́n ojò rírọ̀ náà, tó dé 6.34 ní Oahu, ní wọ́n ṣàpèjúwè gẹ́gẹ́ bí èyí tóní “àǹfàn.” Mọ̀nàmọ́ná tí ó ṣe dédé àti àrá ní ó tẹ̀lé díẹ̀ nínu òjò tí ó rọ̀.
en: Felicia, once a Category 4 storm on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Scale, weakened to a tropical depression before dissipating Tuesday. Its remnants produced showers across most of the islands, though as of yet, no damage or flooding has been reported.
The precipitation, reaching 6.34 inches at a gauge on Oahu, was described as "beneficial". Some of the rainfall was accompanied by thunderstorms and frequent lightning.

passages.title: Tourist plane crash in Papua New Guinea leaves thirteen dead
paragraphs: Ọkọ̀ ojú òfúrufú Twin Otter ti ń gbìyànjú à ti balẹ̀ sí Kokoda ní àná bí i àwọn bàálù PNG CG4684, àmọ́ ó ti sẹ́rí padà lẹ́ẹ̀kan. Bí ìṣẹ́jú mewa kí o tó wàlẹ̀ ò pòorá ní gbà tí o n lọlẹ̀ lẹ́ẹ̀kej.

Won ri ibi tí ìjàmbá ti ṣẹlẹ̀ lóní ò dẹ́ ṣòró láti débẹ̀ torí olopa méjì ní wọ́n fisílẹ̀ sínu igbó láti rìn dé ibẹ̀ láti wá àwọn tí ó yẹ̀ rí. Ojú ọjọ tí kò dára tó fa ìbọ́lẹ̀ pàjáwìrì náà lótú dínà ìwárí rẹ̀ náà.
en: The Twin Otter had been trying to land at Kokoda yesterday as Airlines PNG Flight CG4684, but had aborted once already. About ten minutes before it was due to land from its second approach it disapeared.

The crash site was located today and is so inaccessable that two policemen were dropped into the jungle in order to hike to the scene and seek survivors. The search had been hampered by the same bad weather that had caused the aborted landing.

passages.title: Gas explosion reported in Hammersmith, London ⚠
paragraphs: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí àwọn ìjábọ̀, ilé kan ní òpópónà Macbeth gbiná látàrí gáàsì afẹ́fẹ́ tó jò. Aládarí pẹ̀lú iléeṣẹ́ gáàsì ń jábọ̀ sí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ lẹ́yìn tí alájọgbé pè nípa gáàsì tó ń jò.
Ní ìgbà tí àwọn aṣojú dé, ilé náà gbaná. Kò jábọ̀ ìṣeléṣe púpọ̀, ṣùgbọ́n ó kéré jù àwọn ènìyàn márùn tó wà níbẹ̀ ní àkókò tí gbàmù náà ṣẹlẹ̀ ní wọ́n ṣàyẹ̀wò ìyàlẹ́nu fún.
Kò sí èyàn kan kan nílé ná. Nigba naa, bii awon olugbe 100 ni won le kuro ni agbegbe.
en: According to reports, an apartment on Macbeth Street exploded due to a gas leak. An official with the gas company was reporting to the scene after a neighbor called about a gas leak.
When the official arrived, the apartment exploded. No major injuries were reported, but at least five people on scene at the time of the explosion were treated for symptoms of shock.
No one was inside the apartment. At the time, nearly 100 residents were evacuated from the area.

passages.title: Golf and rugby set to return to the Olympic Games ⚠
paragraphs: Won ti fe da golfi ati rugby pada si Ere Olimpiki. Àwọn aláṣẹ Ìgbìmọ̀ Olympic làgbáláayé ninú ìpàdé tí o wáyé ni Berlin lónìí dìbò láti ṣe àfikún eré-ìdárayá nínú ìpàdé ìgbìmọ̀ aláṣẹ. Rugby, pàápàá ẹgbẹ́ Rugby àti golf ni wọ́n sàyàn nínú àwọn eré ìdárayá mìíràn bíi márùn ún tí wọ́n gbé kalẹ̀ láti kópa nínú ìdíje Olympics.

Eré́ ìdárayà ẹlẹ́gẹ́dẹ́, jíja ẹ̀sẹ́ àti pẹ̀lú ìpá àti sisare ohun táyà lẹ́sẹ̀ bàtà gbìyànjú láti jẹ́ òkan lára ́àwọǹ ètò Olympicgẹ́gẹ́ bi bọlu àfọwọ́gbá ati onì fùkẹ̀fùkẹ̀,́ àwọǹ èyí tí a yọkúrò nípa ìdìbò kúrò nínú àwọn eré Olympici ní ọdún 200. Gbogbo ìgbìmọ̀ IOC gbọ́dọ̀ tún buwọ́lu ìbò náà nínú ìpàdé oṣù kẹwàá ní Copenhagen.
en: Both golf and rugby are set to return to the Olympic Games. The International Olympic Committee voted to include the sports at its executive board meeting in Berlin today. Rugby, specifically rugby union, and golf were selected over five other sports to be considered to participate in the Olympics.
