Èyí dẹ̀ ti mú èrè tó pọ̀ wá. Fún àpẹẹrẹ, ní ọdún 2018, ààrẹ orílẹ̀-èdè South Korea gba ìdájọ́ ẹ̀wọn odún mẹ́ẹ̀dọ́gbọ̀n fún àwọn ẹ̀sùn tó níṣe pẹ̀lú ìwà-ìbàjẹ́. Èyí kì bá tí ṣẹlẹ̀ ní bíi ẹ̀wá ọdún sẹ́yìn nígbà tí orílẹ̀-èdè náà kúṣẹ̀ tó sì wà lábẹ́ ìjọba apàṣẹ wàá.
en: When you looked at South Korea's institutions, even as late as the 1980s, they were on par with some of the poorest and most corrupt African countries at the time. But as companies like Samsung, Kia, Hyundai invested in innovations that made things much more affordable for so many more people, South Korea ultimately became prosperous. As the country grew prosperous, it was able to transition from an authoritarian government to a democratic government and has been able to reinvest in building its institutions.

And this has paid off tremendously. For instance, in 2018, South Korea's president was sentenced to 25 years in prison on corruption-related charges. This could never have happened decades ago when the country was poor and ruled by an authoritarian government.

passages.title: MENYO passage 301
paragraphs: Kìí ṣe ǹkan tí mò ń sọ nìyẹn rárá. Ǹkan tí mò ń dá lábàá, bó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ wí pé, ni wí pé ìwà-ìbàjẹ́, pàápàá jùlọ fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ènìyànn ní àwòn orílẹ̀-èdè tí wọ́n kúṣẹ̀, ní wọ́n ń yà sílẹ̀. Ó jẹ́ ohun-ìlò kan ní ààyè níbi tójẹ́ wí pé ànfàní diẹ̀ ló wà láti yanjú ìṣòro.

Dídókówò nínu ìṣẹ̀da tó máa ń jẹ́ kí àwọn èròjà túbọ̀ rọjú fún ọ̀pọ̀ ènìyàn kò ní kojú ọ̀wọ́n yìí nìkan ṣùgbọ́n yóò pèse ọ̀nà ìpawó wọlé fún àwọn ìjọba láti dawó padà sínú ọrọ̀-ajé láti ró ilé-iṣẹ́ wọn lágbára. Èyí ni oríkèé pàtàkì tí ó sọnù nínu àyo ìdàgbàsókè ọrọ̀-ajé tí yóò ràn wá lọ́wọ́ láti mú àdínkù bá ìwà-ìbàjẹ́ nígbẹ́yìn. Ẹ mọ̀, mo sọ ìrètí nù nínu orílẹ̀-èdè Nàìjíríà nígbà tí mo wà lọ́mọ odún mẹ́rìn-dín-lógún.
en: That's not what I'm saying at all. What I'm suggesting, though, is that corruption, especially for most people in poor countries, is a work-around. It's a utility in a place where there are fewer better options to solve a problem.

Investing in innovations that make products much more affordable for many people not only attacks this scarcity but it creates a sustainable source of revenue for governments to reinvest into the economies to strengthen their institutions. This is the critical missing piece in the economic development puzzle that will ultimately help us reduce corruption. You know, I lost hope in Nigeria when I was 16.

passages.title: MENYO passage 302
paragraphs: Bàbá mi jẹ́ ọmọ orílẹ̀-èdè tí wọ́n ń pè ní Botswana ní gúúsù ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀. Díẹ̀ ló fi tóbi ju orílẹ̀-ède Germany lọ. Ní ọdún yìí a ṣe ayẹyẹ àdọ́ta ọdún ìdúró ṣinṣin ọmìnira wa.
Ó sì ní àwọn ìpinnu ìtẹ̀síẃjú àwùjọ gidi. Orílẹ̀-èdè ìyá mi ni ìlu-ọba Swaziland. Ó jẹ́ orílẹ̀-èdè tó kéré púpọ̀, tí ohun náà wà ní gúúsù ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀.
en: My father's from a country called Botswana in southern Africa. It's only slightly bigger than Germany. This year we celebrate our 50th year of stable democracy.
And it has some very progressive social policies. My mother's country is the Kingdom of Swaziland. It's a very, very small country, also in southern Africa.

passages.title: MENYO passage 303
paragraphs: Nígbà tí mo wà lọ́mọdé, mo máa ń rí ìyàtọ̀ náà. Òjó máa ń rọ̀ púpọ̀ ní orílẹ̀-èdè kan, kìí rọ̀ tó bẹ́ẹ̀ ní ìkejì. Ṣùgbọ́n yàtọ̀ sí èyí, mi ò tilẹ̀ mọ̀ ìdi tó fi pọn dandan pé àwọn òbí mi wá láti àyè méjì ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀.
Sùgbọ́n yóò padà nípa ọ̀tọ̀ lára mi. Ṣé ẹ ríi, wọ́n bími ní orílẹ̀-èdè kan wọ́n sì rè mí ní ìkejì. Nígbà tí a kó lọ sí orílẹ̀-ède Botswana, mo jẹ́ ọmọ òpónlo tó ń sọ SiSwati dijú láìsí ǹkan mìíràn.
en: And when I was a kid, I could see the difference. It rained a lot in one country, it didn't rain quite as much in the other. But outside of that, I didn't really realize why it mattered that my parents were from two different places.

But it would go on to have a very peculiar effect on me. You see, I was born in one country and raised in the other. When we moved to Botswana, I was a toddler who spoke fluent SiSwati and nothing else.

passages.title: MENYO passage 304
paragraphs: Ilè Adúláwọ̀ ní mẹ́fà nínú àwọn ààyè àwọn atìpó tó tóbi jù lágbàyé. Ǹkan tó jẹ́ ìṣòro ọmọ orílẹ̀-ède Burundi nígbà kan ti di ìṣòro ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀. Sí èmi, kò sí ǹkan tó ń jẹ́ ìṣòro orílẹ̀-ède sudan tàbí orílẹ̀-ède South Africa tàbí ìṣòro orílẹ̀-ède kenya, ìṣòro ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ nìkan ni nítorí nígbẹ́yìn, a jọ́ ń pín ìṣòro náà ni.

Nítorí náà tí a bá jọ pín àwọn ìṣòro náà, kí ló dé tí a ò ṣiṣẹ́ dáadáa láti pín àwọn àṣeyọrí náà? Báwo la ṣe lè ṣe ìyẹn? Ó daa, ní àsìkò ọjọ́ iwájú, a lè pinnu nípa ṣíṣe àfikún sí òwò láàrin ilè Adúláwọ̀, pẹ̀lú yíyọ àwọn ibodè kúrò àti gbígbé ẹrù ru àwọn adarí wa láti ṣe ìmúṣẹ àwọn àdéhùn agbègbè tí wọ́n ti buwọ́ lù.
en: Africa has six of the world's largest refugee centers. What was once a Burundian problem becomes an African problem. So to me, there are no Sudanese problems or South African problems or Kenyan problems, only African problems because eventually, we share the turmoil.

So if we share the problems, why aren't we doing a better job of sharing the successes? How can we do that? Well, in the long term, we can shoot towards increasing inter-African trade, removing borders and putting pressure on leaders to fulfill regional agreements they've already signed.

passages.title: MENYO passage 305
paragraphs: Ta ni ìyẹn wá ń se ànfàní fún? Ó dáa, àwọn adarí nílẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀, ó fẹ́rẹ̀ jẹ́ ní àdáyanrí. Rárá, ohun tí mò ń sọ nípa rẹ̀ ni ìṣọ̀kan ilẹ̀ Africa àwọn ènìyan ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀.

Àwọn ọ̀dọ́ ọmọ ilẹ̀ adúláwọ̀ b́ii tèmi, tí a kún fún agbára ọgbọ́n àtinúdá, pẹ̀lú èro ìṣẹ̀dá. Ṣùgbọ́n pẹ̀lu ijọba tí ò da àti orílẹ̀-èdè tó ń ṣòjòjò, gbogbo èbùn yìí lè má wùlo. Ní ẹkùn tí àwọn adarí diẹ̀ ti wà ní ìjọba ju iye ọdún tí ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ará ìlú ti lò láyé, a nílò ǹkan tuntun lọ́nàkọnà, ǹkan tí yóò ṣiṣẹ́.
en: And who does that benefit? Well, African leaders, almost exclusively. No, what I'm talking about is the Pan-Africanism of the ordinary African.

Young Africans like me, we are bursting with creative energy, with innovative ideas. But with bad governance and shaky institutions, all of this potential could go to waste. On a continent where more than a handful of leaders have been in power longer than the majority of the populations has been alive, we are in desperate need of something new, something that works.

passages.title: MENYO passage 306
paragraphs: Àlá mi ni pé àwọn ọ̀dọ́ ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ yóò bẹ̀rẹ̀ síní mọ̀ pé gbogbo ẹkùn náà ni ibùsun wa, ni ilée wa. Lílo ìkàni ayélukára, a lè bẹ̀rè síní ronú papọ̀, a lè bẹ̀rẹ̀ síní ṣẹ̀da ohun-ọ̀tun lápapọ̀. "Nílẹ̀ adúláwọ̀, a máa ń sọ pé, ""tí ó bá fẹ́ yára lọ, o lè dá nìkan lọ, ṣùgbọ́n tí o bá fẹ́ rìn jìnà, ẹ kọ́wọ̀ọ́ rìn."

Mo dẹ̀ nígbàgbọ́ wí pé ìṣọ̀kan àwùjọ ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ ni ọ̀nà tí a lè fi jọ rìn jìnà lápapọ̀. Èyí dẹ̀ ti ń ṣẹlẹ̀. Ànfàni sí àwọn ìkànì ayélukára wọ̀nyí ti fún àwọn ọ̀dọ́ nílẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ ní ǹkan tí a ti máa ń fi rògbòdìyàn gbà.
en: My dream is that young Africans begin to realize that the entire continent is our canvas, is our home. Using the Internet, we can begin to think collaboratively, we can begin to innovate together. "In Africa, we say, ""If you want to go fast, you go alone, but if you want to go far, you go together."

And I believe that social Pan-Africanism is how we can go far together. And this is already happening. Access to these online networks has given young Africans something we've always had to violently take: a voice.

passages.title: MENYO passage 307
paragraphs: A ṣe àtìlẹyìn fún àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ orílẹ̀-ède South Africa tí wọ́n ń ṣe ìwọ́de tako owó gegere ilé-ìwé gíga. A ṣe àtìlẹyìn fún àwọn obìnrin ní orílẹ̀-ède Zimbabwe tí wọ́n ń ṣe ìwọ́de lọ sí ilé aṣòfin. A ṣe àtìlẹyìn fún àwọn akọ̀ròyin orílẹ̀-ède Angólà tí wọ́n ń mú sí àtìmọ́lé lọ́nà tí ò bófin mu.

Fún ìgbà àkọ́kọ́, ẹ̀dun ọmọ ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ àti àfojúsùn ọmọ ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ ní ànfàní láti di rírí fún àwọn tí wọ́n lẹ̀ kẹ́dùn pẹ̀lú rẹ̀ jù: àwọn òwọn ọmọ ilẹ̀ Ad́láwọ̀ tókù. Mo nígbàgbọ́ pé pẹ̀lú ìrònú nípa ìṣọ̀kan àwùjọ ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ àti ìkàni ayélukára gẹ́gẹ́ bi irinṣẹ́, a lè bẹ̀rẹ̀ síní gba ara wa sílẹ̀, nígbẹ́yìn, láti gbarawa sílẹ̀. Ẹ ṣeun.
en: We support South African students who are marching against ridiculously high tertiary fees. We support Zimbabwean women who are marching to parliament. We support Angolan journalists who are being illegally detained.

For the first time ever, African pain and African aspiration has the ability to be witnessed by those who can empathize with it the most: other Africans. I believe that with a social Pan-Africanist thinking and using the Internet as a tool, we can begin to rescue each other, and ultimately, to rescue ourselves. Thank you.

passages.title: MENYO passage 308
paragraphs: Ẹ wá dúró, o bọ́síta nínú ọkọ̀ yín ẹ dẹ̀ ya àwòrán kan. "Ẹ wá wọ àdúgbò náà lọ, ẹ wá ń bèrè, ""kí ló ń ṣẹlẹ̀ níbí? "" ní àkọ́kọ́ àwọn ẹnìyan lọ́ra láti sọ fún yín." "Nigbà náà ni ẹnìkan sọ wí pé, ""Àwọn wọ̀nyí ni àwọn ikú kòkòro apa sójà ara ní àwùjọ wa láìpẹ́ yìí."
""" Kòkòro apa sójà ara ò dàbí àwọn aìsàn tókù; ó máa ń fa ìdẹ́yẹsí." Àwọn ènìyán máa ń lọ́ra láti sọ̀rọ̀ nípa rẹ̀ -- ìbẹ̀rù kan rọ̀ mọ. Màá sọ nípa kòkòro apa sójà ara lónì, nípa ikú, nípa ìdẹ́yẹsí.
en: And you stop, and you get out of your car and you take a picture. "And you go into the town, and you inquire, ""What's going on here? and people are initially reluctant to tell you." "And then someone says, ""These are the recent AIDS deaths in our community."

HIV isn't like other medical conditions; it's stigmatizing. People are reluctant to talk about it -- there's a fear associated with it. And I'm going to talk about HIV today, about the deaths, about the stigma.

passages.title: MENYO passage 309
paragraphs: Mílíọ́nù mẹ́tà-lé-lọ́gbọ̀n (33) àwọn ènìyàn ni wọ́n ń gbé pẹ̀lú kòkòro apa sójà ara lágbáyé lónì. Nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí, ìdá méjì nínú mẹ́ta, mílíọ́nù méjì-lé-lógún ni wọ́n ń gbé ní ìwọ̀-oòrun ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀. Mílíọ́nù kan lé ẹgbẹ̀rún lọ́nà erínwó ni àwọn aláboyún ní àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè tí ìpawó-wọlé wọn kére tàbí tó wà lágbede méjì tí wọ́n ń gbé pẹ̀lu kòkòro apa sójà ara nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí, ìdá àdọ́rùn wà ní iwọ̀-oòrun ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀.

A máa ń sọ́rọ̀ nípa ǹkan pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀-ìperí tó jọra wọn. Màá sọ̀rọ̀ nípa oyún ọdọọdún àti àwọn ìyá tí wọ́n ti ní kòkòro apa sójà ara. Orílẹ̀-ède Amẹ́ríkà -- orílẹ̀-èdè tó tóbi -- lọ́dọọdún, ẹgbẹ̀rún méje (7,000) àwọn ìyá tí wọ́n ní kòkòro apa sójà ara ni wọ́n bímọ.
en: There are 33 million people living with HIV in the world today. Of these, two-thirds, 22 million are living in sub-Saharan Africa. There are 1.4 million pregnant women in low- and middle-income countries living with HIV and of these, 90 percent are in sub-Saharan Africa.

We talk about things in relative terms. And I'm going to talk about annual pregnancies and HIV-positive mothers. The United States -- a large country -- each year, 7,000 mothers with HIV who give birth to a child.

passages.title: MENYO passage 310
paragraphs: Àkójọpọ̀ gbogbo iṣẹ́ ni, ó sì ń ṣiṣẹ́. Ní orílẹ̀ ède Amẹ́ríkà, láti ìgbà tí ìtọ́jú ti dé láàrín àsìko ọdún 1990, àdínkù tó tó ìdá ọgọ́rin ti dé bá iye àwọn ọmọ tó ní kòkòro apa sójà ara. Àwọn ìkókó tó dín ní ọgọ́rùn ni wọ́n ń bí pẹ̀lu kòkòro apa sójà ara lọ́dọọdún ní orílẹ̀-ède Amẹ́ríkà síbẹ̀, bákan náà, ẹgbẹ̀rún lọ́nà erínwó lé ọmọ ni wọ́n ń bí lọ́dọọdún lágbàyé lónì tó ní kòkòro apa sójà ara.
Kíni ìyẹn tumọ̀ sí? Ó túmọ̀ sí wí pé ọ̀rùn-lé-lẹ́gbẹ́rùn ọmọ ló ń ní àkóràn lójoojúmọ́ - ọ̀rùn-lé-lẹ́gbẹ́rùn (1,100) ọmọ lójoojúmọ́, ló ń ní àkóràn kòkòro apa sójà ara. Níbo ni wọ́n ti ń wá?
en: It's an entire package of services, and it works. So in the United States, since the advent of treatment in the middle of the 1990s, there's been an 80-percent decline in the number of HIV-infected children. Less than 100 babies are born with HIV each year in the United States and yet, still, over 400,000 children are born every year in the world today with HIV.
What does that mean? It means 1,100 children infected each day -- 1,100 children each day, infected with HIV. And where do they come from?

passages.title: MENYO passage 311
paragraphs: Ní ọjọ́ kànkan, ẹgbẹ̀rún kan àwọn ìkókó - ẹgbẹ̀rún kan àwọn ìkókó ni wọ́n ń bí lọ́jó kànkan pẹ̀lú kòkòro apa sójà ara ní ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀. Lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi, mo wo àwòran àgbáyé tó wà níbí àti ìpín kòkòro apa sójà ara ní ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ tó ti kọjá àyè. Ẹ jẹ́ kí á wo àwòrán orílẹ̀-èdè mìíràn.

Ilà fàdákà tírín tí ẹ rí níbí yìí, ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ nìyẹn. Bákan náà ni pẹ̀lú àwọn nọ́ọ́sì. Ọtítọ́ ibẹ̀ ni wí pé ìwò-oòrun ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀ ní ìdá mẹ́rìn-lé-lógún (24%) wàhálà ààrùn àgbáyé síbẹ̀ ìdá mẹ́ta àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ìlera àgbáyé péré.
en: And each day, a thousand babies -- a thousand babies are born each day with HIV in Africa. So again, I look at the globe here and the disproportionate share of HIV in Africa. And let's look at another map.

That thin sliver you see here, that's Africa. And it's the same with nurses. The truth is sub-Saharan Africa has 24 percent of the global disease burden and yet only three percent of the world's health care workers.

passages.title: MENYO passage 312
paragraphs: Èyí ni ìtọ́jú ajẹmọ́ ìṣègùn tó kọjá òògùn lásán. Àwọn ìyá tí wọ́n ń ṣiṣẹ́ fún wa, wọ́n wá láti àwọn agbègbè tí wọ́n ti ń ṣiṣẹ́. A gbà wọ́n -- wọ́n ń gba owó gẹ́gẹ́ bi akọ́ṣẹ́mọṣẹ́ lára ikọ̀ àwọn onímọ̀ ìlera, bíi àwọn oníṣégùn-òyìnbó àti àwọn nọ́ọ́sì.

A ṣí àpò-àṣùwọn ilé-ìfowópamọ́ fún wọn a dẹ̀ ń sanwó tààrà sínu àpò-àṣùwọn wọn, nítorí ààbó wà fún owó wọn; àwọn ọkùnrin ò lè gbà á lọ́wọ wọn. Wọ́n máa ń la ètò-ẹ̀kọ́ oní kọ̀ríkúlọ́ọ̀mù alágbára olósẹ̀ méjì tàbí mẹ́ta kọjá, ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́. Ní báyìí, àwọn oníṣégùn-òyìnbó àti àwọn nọ́ọ́sì -- àwọn náà ń gba ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́.
en: This is the medical care that goes beyond just medicines. So the mothers who work for us, they come from the communities in which they work. They're hired -- they're paid as professional members of the health care teams, just like doctors and nurses.

And we open bank accounts for them and they're paid directly into the accounts, because their money's protected; the men can't take it away from them. They go through two to three weeks of rigorous curriculum-based education, training. Now, doctors and nurses -- they too get trained.

passages.title: MENYO passage 313
paragraphs: Àwọn ọkùnrin kìí fi bẹ́ẹ̀ sí lára ìtọ́jú oyún. Ṣùgbọ́n ní orílẹ̀-ède Rwanda, ní orílẹ̀-èdè kan, wọ́n ti ní òfin pé obìnrin ò lè wá fún ìtọ́jú àyàfi tí ó bá mú bàba ọmọ wá pẹ̀lu rẹ̀ -- òfin yẹn nìyẹn. Nítorí náà bàbá àti ìyá, lápapọ̀, jọ máa ń la ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ àti àyẹ̀wò kọjá ni.
Bàbá àti ìyá, lápapọ̀, jọ máa ń gba èsì ni. Èyí sì ṣe pàtàkì láti rí ọ̀nà àbáyọ kúrò nínu ìdẹ́yẹsí. Sísọ ọ́ jáde ṣe pàtàkì púpọ̀ fún ìdènà.
en: Men are not frequently part of pregnancy care. But in Rwanda, in one country, they've got a policy that a woman can't come for care unless she brings the father of the baby with her -- that's the rule. And so the father and the mother, together, go through the counseling and the testing.
The father and the mother, together, they get the results. And this is so important in breaking through the stigma. Disclosure is so central to prevention.

passages.title: MENYO passage 314
paragraphs: "Ni ẹ̀gbọn rẹ̀ àgbà lóbìnrin yìí bá dìde ó ní, ""Èmi náà ń gbé pẹ̀lu kòkòrò náà, ojú sì ti ń tìmí." "Ni àbúro rẹ̀ lọ́kùnrin náà bá dìde ó ní, ""Èmi náà ní i." Mo lérò wí pé ẹ máa lémi kúrò nínú ẹbí ni.
Ẹ rí ibi tí èyí ń lọ. "Obìnrin tó gbẹ́yìn dìde ó ní, ""èmi náà ní i." Mo lérò wí pé ẹ máa kórìra mi ni.
en: And then this older sister stood up and said, I too am living with the virus, and I've been ashamed. And then her younger brother stood up and said, I'm also positive. I thought you were going to throw me out of the family.
And you see where this is going. "The last sister stood up and said, ""I'm also positive." I thought you were going to hate me.

passages.title: MENYO passage 315
paragraphs: "Mo sọ fún wọn, ""Ẹ máa yán-an yọ, ẹ ó sì re ọmọ tí ìléra rẹ̀ pé." """ Èrí ni mo jẹ́ pé ìrètí ń bẹ." Mitchell Besser: Ẹ rantí àwọn àwòrán tí mo fi hàn yín nípa ìwọ̀nba awọn oníṣégùn-òyìnbó àti àwọn nọ́ọ́sì tí wọ́n wà ní ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀.
Wàhálà ló sì jẹ́ sí ètò ìlera. Kódà bí a ṣe ń ní àyẹ̀wò àti òògùn si, a ò léè dọ́dọ̀ àwọn ènìyàn; a ò ní àwọn onímò-ìlera tó tó. À máa ń sọ̀rọ̀ nípa ǹkan tí à ń pè ní ìgbaṣẹ́ lọ́wọ́ ara ẹni.
en: "I tell them, ""You are going to make it, and you will raise a healthy baby." I am proof that there is hope. Mitchell Besser: Remember the images I showed you of how few doctors and nurses there are in Africa.
And it is a crisis in health care systems. Even as we have more tests and more drugs, we can't reach people; we don't have enough providers. So we talk in terms of what we call task-shifting.

passages.title: MENYO passage 316
paragraphs: Báwo ni ẹ ṣe lè pèse ètò ìlera gidi? A ti pinnu láti ṣe àtúnṣe ètò ìlera gẹ́gẹ́ bi oníṣégùn-òyìnbó, nọ́ọ́sì àti ìya olùbánidámọ́ràn. Nítorí náà ǹkan tí àwọn nọ́ọ́sì máa ń ṣe ni wí pé wọn máa ń sọ fún àwọn ìya olùbánidámọ́ràn pé kọ́ ṣàlàye bi wọn yóò ṣe lo òògùn, àti ewu rẹ̀.

Wọ́n máa ń ṣe ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ nípa fífún ìkókó lóunjẹ, ìfètò-sẹ́bí, ìbálópọ̀ aláìléwu, àwọn iṣẹ́ tí àwọn nọ́ọ́sì ò ní àkókò fún. A padà síbi ìdèna àkóràn ìyá sí ọmọ. Gbogbo àgbáyé ń rí àwọn ètò wọ̀nyí gẹ́gẹ́ bi afárá sí ẹ̀kúnrẹ́rẹ́ ìlera ìyá àti ọmọ.
en: How do you build a better health care system? We've chosen to redefine the health care system as a doctor, a nurse and a mentor mother. And so what nurses do is that they ask the mentor mothers to explain how to take the drugs, the side effects.

They delegate education about infant feeding, family planning, safer sex, actions that nurses simple just don't have time for. So we go back to the prevention of mother to child transmission. The world is increasingly seeing these programs as the bridge to comprehensive maternal and child health.

passages.title: MENYO passage 317
paragraphs: Àkọ́kọ́, ní ìpele aláìsàn -- àwọn ìya àti àwọn ọmọ dídáábòbo àwọn ọmọ kúrò níbi kíkó kòkòro apa sójà ara, mímú kí àwọn ìyá wà láláàfíà láti rè wọ́n. Ìkejì, àwọn àwùjọ -- ríró àwọn obìnrin lágbára. Wọ́n di adarí láàrín àwùjọ wọn.
Wọ́n mú àyípadà bá bí àwọn àwùjọ ṣe ń ronú -- a nílò láti mú àyípadà bá ìhà kíkọ sí kòkòro apa sójà ara A nílò láti mú àyípadà bá ìhà kíkọ sí àwọn obìnrin ní ilẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀. A ní láti ṣe ìyẹn.
en: The first, at the patient level -- mothers and babies keeping babies from getting HIV, keeping mothers healthy to raise them. The second, communities -- empowering women. They become leaders within their communities.
They change the way communities think -- we need to change attitudes to HIV. We need to change attitudes to women in Africa. We have to do that.

passages.title: MENYO passage 318
paragraphs: Àwọn aláìsàn nígbà kan rí tí wọ́n ń ṣe ìtọ́jú àwọn tó ń ṣáìsàn lọ́wọ́. Àti ìrónilágbára nípasẹ ìgbanisíṣẹ́ -- mímú àdínkù bá ìdẹ́yẹsí. (fọ́rán aláwòrán) Obìnrin Asọ̀tàn: ìrètí wà, ìrètí pé lọ́jọ́ kan a ó borí ìjà yìí kojú kòkòro apa sójà ara àti ìsọdọ̀lẹ àjẹsára.
Èyàn kànkan gbọ́dọ̀ mọ ipo kòkòro apa sójà ara wọn. Àwọn tí wọn ò ní kòkòro apa sójà ara gbọ́dọ̀ mọ bí wọn ò ṣe ní kó o. Àwọn tí wọ́n ní kòkòro apa sójà ara gbọ́dọ̀ mọ bí wọn ó ṣe ṣe ìtọ́jú ara wọn.
en: Past patients taking care of present patients. And empowerment through employment -- reducing stigma. (Video) Female Narrator: There is hope, hope that one day we shall win this fight against HIV and AIDS.
Each person must know their HIV status. Those who are HIV-negative must know how to stay negative. Those who are HIV-infected must know how to take care of themselves.

passages.title: MENYO passage 319
paragraphs: Àwọn ìyá tí wọ́n ń ṣe ìtọ́jú fún àwọn ìyá. Àyípadà ni. Ẹ ṣeun.
Bí àwọn obìnrin ṣe ń mú àyípadà bá orílẹ̀-ède Rwanda. Mo padà sí ilé mi ní orílẹ̀-ède Rwanda ní odún méjì lẹ́yin ìṣekúpani ẹlẹ́yàmẹ̀yà ọdún 1994 kojúu Tutsi. Orílẹ̀-èdè náà ti bàjẹ́.
en: Mothers caring for mothers. It's transformational. Thank you.
How women are revolutionizing Rwanda I came back to my home of Rwanda two years after the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. The country was devastated.

passages.title: MENYO passage 320
paragraphs: Nítorí mo ní ìfọkànsìn sí ìdájọ́ àwùjọ àti ìdọ́gba, àwọn aṣètọ́jú-ọmọdé márùn-ún ló sí wà fún mílíọ́nù àwọn ọmọdé ní orílẹ̀-ède Rwanda, mo pinnu láti dúró. Ṣùgbọ́n lára àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n ṣe kóríyá fún ìpinnu mi láti dúró, àwọn obìnrin takun-takun wà ní orílẹ̀-ède Rwanda, àwọn obìnrin kan tí wọ́n ti kojú ìṣekúpani ẹlẹ́yámẹ̀yà tí wọ́n sì yè é. Wọ́n ní láti borí ìnira aláìgbàgbọ́ àti ìyà.

Àwọn kan nínú wọn ń tọ́mọ tí wọ́n lóyún wọn látara ìfipábánilòpọ̀. Àwọn mìíràn ń kú díèdíè pẹ̀lú kòkòro apa sójà ara wọ́n sì tún dáríji àwọn tí wọ́n hu ìwà ìbàjẹ́ náà, tí wọ́n fínú-fẹ́dọ̀ kó ààrùn ràn wọn pẹ̀lu lílo kòkòro apa sójà ara àti ìfipábánilòpọ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bi ohun ìjà. Nítorí áà, wọ́n ṣe ìwúrí fún mi.
en: And because I'm really dedicated to social justice and equity, and there were only five pediatricians in total for millions of children in Rwanda, I decided to stay. But among the people who have motivated my decision to stay, there were some fantastic women of Rwanda, some women who had faced the genocide and survived it. They had to overcome unbelievable pain and suffering.

Some of them were raising children conceived through rape. Others were dying slowly with HIV and forgave the perpetrators, who voluntarily infected them using HIV and rape as a weapon. So, they inspired me.

passages.title: MENYO passage 321
paragraphs: Ẹ dè lè bi ara yín ibi tí àyípadà èro-ọkàn yìí ti gbé orílẹ̀-ède wa dé. Ní orílẹ̀-ède Rwanda lónì, àwa la ní ìdá àwọn obìnrin tó pọ́jù ní ilé-aṣòfin. Ẹ dúró dìgbà tí màá sọ ìda rẹ̀ fún yín -- ìdá mọ́kàn-lé-láàdọ́ta (61%).

Ní orílẹ̀-èdè yìí, mẹ́rìn-lè-láàdọ́ta (54) ni. A ti mú àdínkù bá ikú ọmọdé pèlú ìdá márùn-lé-láàdọ́rin (75%), ikú ìyá pẹ̀lú ìdá ọgọ́rin (80%). Ní ìbèrè àsìko ọdún 2000, àwọn obìnrin mẹ́sàn ni wọ́n ń kú lójoojúmọ́ yíká ìrọbí àti oyún.
en: And you can ask yourself where this shift of mindset has brought our country. Today in Rwanda, we have the highest percentage of women in parliament. Wait till I tell you the percentage -- sixty-one percent.

In this country, it's 54. We have reduced child mortality by 75 percent, maternal mortality by 80 percent. In early 2000s, there were nine women who were dying every day around delivery and pregnancy.

passages.title: MENYO passage 322
paragraphs: Méjì ṣì tún pọ̀jù. Ṣùgbọ́n, ṣé mo gbàgbọ́ wí pé àwọn èsì yìí rí bẹ́ẹ̀ nítorí a ní ìdá àwọn obìnrin tó pọ̀ ní ipò agbára? Mo gbà. Ó wà -- bẹ́ẹ̀ ni -- ìwádìí kan wà ní àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè tó ṣì ń dágbà sókè tó fi hàn pé tí ẹ bá mú ìyàtọ̀ bá ipò àwọn obìnrin, ẹ ti mú ìy

Àdínkù tó ń lọ bí ìdá mẹ́tà-dín-láàdọ́ta (47%) nínu ikú ọmọdé. Kódà ní orílẹ̀-èdè yìí níbi tí a wà báyìí, òótọ́ ni. Nítorí náà a mọ̀ wí pé àwọn obìnrin, tí wọ́n bá lo ìmọ̀ọ́ṣe wọn ní ipò aṣíwájú, wọ́n máa mú àyípadà bá gbogbo ènìyàn tó wà ní ìkápá wọn.
en: Two is still too much. But, do I believe that those results are because we had a big number of women in power positions? I do. There is -- yes --there is a study in the developing world that shows that if you improve the status of women, you improve the status of the community where they live.

Up to 47 percent of decrease in child mortality. And even in this country where we are now, it's true. So we know that women, when they use their skills in leadership positions, they enhance the entire population they are in charge of.

passages.title: MENYO passage 323
paragraphs: Ìpè orílẹ̀-èdè ni sí ojúṣe rẹ Kí gbogbo ọwọ́ má dilẹ̀ Láti sọ ìlú Ìbàdàn, di ìlú tí ó mọ́ jùlọ
Nínú gbogbo àgbáyé Ẹ jáde ní ẹgbẹẹgbẹ̀rún yín Pèlú jígà, ṣọ́bìrì, ìgbálẹ̀ àti apẹ̀rẹ̀
en: It's a national call to duty All hands should be on deck To make Ibadan, the cleanest city
In the whole world Come out in your thousands With diggers, shovels, brooms and baskets

passages.title: MENYO passage 324
paragraphs: "ìdí nìyí tí ariwo ẹ̀rín Àlàmú ""ha ha ha ha"" fi ń pọ̀ sí i... Ṣùgbọ́n ó ti wá ń pọ̀jù fún ìtura àwọn ará àdúgbò rẹ̀." Fún ìdí èyí, àwọn ènìyàn bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í narùn ní méjì-méjì, mẹ́ta-mẹ́ta láti ẹnu ọ̀nà, ojú fèrèsé, láti ẹ̀yìn ògiri àti lá́ti ẹ̀yìnkùlé àwọn ilé tó yí i ká. Wọ́n ń fọ́wọ-lẹ́rán wo ògángán ilé Àlàmú, wọ́n sì ń mirí wọn tìkáàánú-tìkáàánú.

"""Èéṣe? Èéṣe? wọ́n ronú.......Èéṣe tí irú èyí fi ń ṣẹlẹ̀ sí arákùnrin yìí.""" """Ta ló kó irú èyí bá a?""" """Ọ̀dọ́mọkùnrin tó ní ọkọ̀ ayọ́kẹ́lẹ́ ńlá, tó ní ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ owó. Ọkùnrin tó ń rí oúnjẹ àjẹyó jẹ, tí ó sì ń ní ohun mímu àmuṣẹ́kù. Ilé ayé yìí ò mà rọrùn o."""
en: "That was why the ""ha ha ha ha"" sound of Alamu's grotesque laughter now reverberated... But evidently too loud now for his immediate neighbours"" comfort." And so human heads started appearing in twos and threes - at the doorsteps, at the window panes, from behind the walls, and at the balconies of the surrounding houses. They held their chins looking curiously in the direction of Alamu's flat, shaking their heads in pity.

"""Why? Why?"" they wondered, ""Why should this happen to this man?""" """Who brought this upon him?""" """A rich young man with a big car, a man with plenty of money. A man with enough to eat and enough to drink. This world is not easy."""

passages.title: MENYO passage 325
paragraphs: Kìí ṣe sàwáwù pẹ̀lú àwọn ènìyàn wọ̀nyí rárá. Ní ti gbígbafẹ́ àti ọgbọ́n orí ni ó mọ̀ pé gbọ̀ọ̀rọ̀-gbọọrọ ni òun fi jù wọ́n lọ. Kò sí ìdí fún ìbáṣepọ̀ tímọ́-tímọ́ kankan láàárín wọn.

Kódà, àwọn ará àdúgbò rẹ̀ yìí jẹ́ aláìmọ̀-ọ́n-kọ, mọ̀-ọ́n-kà, a fẹ́rẹ̀ é lè sọ pẹ́ wọn kò mọ nǹkankan rárá. Àlàmú sì jẹ́ alákọ̀wé tí ó ti lo ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọdún ayé rẹ̀ ní ìlú òyìnbó. Ilé alámọ̀ àti onísìmẹ́ǹtì díè díè ni ó dára jù nínú ilé tí àwọn ará oko yìí ń gbé. Ilé tí Àlàmú fi owó gbà yìí dá yàtọ̀, wọ́n kùn ún lọ́dà dáa dáa tí iná mọ̀nàmọ́ná sì wà níbẹ̀.
en: He was not in the same class with these people. Socially and intellectually, he knew he was far ahead of them There was no basis for any intimate association.

"Whereas his immediate neighbours were a pack of illiterates, knowing almost next to nothing, Alamu was a ""book man"" who had spent the beteer part of his life in the country of the white man." "Whereas these ""local"" people lived in a mud houses, or cemented brick houses at best." Alamu's hired flat stood out - well-painted and adequately electrified.

passages.title: MENYO passage 326
paragraphs: Ṣùgbọ́n Àlàmú mọ ìwọ̀n ara rẹ̀, ó mọ̀ pé ìdùnnú jìnnà sí òun, òun nìkan ló sì mọ ibi tí bàtà ti ń ta á lẹ́sẹ̀, kò sì ba ẹnikẹ́ni sọ̀rọ̀ nípa rẹ̀, ófi ètè rẹ̀ métè. Nígbàkugbà tí àwọn ará àdúgbò rẹ̀ bá ń kí i lówùúrọ̀, Àlàmú yóò fi ara dáhùn, bí i kó mi ẹnu, bíi kó ṣẹ́jú tàbí kí ó mirí, tàbí kí ó pòṣé ṣààrà sí wọn. Kíá, ni yóò rìn kúrò, á fò sínú ọkọ pijó rẹ̀, á fi ẹ̀yìn ọkọ̀ jáde láti inú ọgbà ìgbọ́kọ̀sí rẹ̀, á ki erémọ́lẹ̀, sí ọ̀nà ibi tí ó jẹ́ pé ọlọ́run nìkan ló mọ̀!

Ó ra ọkọ̀ náà lẹ́yìn tí ó ti ìlú Englandi dé sí ilé ní ọdún mẹ́ta sẹ́yìn - lẹ́yìn ìgbà díè tí ó di Aṣírò-ọrọ̀ àgbà ní iléeṣẹ́ Bajoks. Lẹ́yìn ọdún kan ni ó fẹ́ Làbákẹ́, ọmọbìnnrin tí ó pàdé, tí ó sì nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí nílùú England. Ìgbéyàwó wọn jẹ́ èyí tí wọ́n ti ba owó nínú jẹ́. Kété, lẹ́yìn ìgbéyàwó alárinrin rẹ̀ yìí ni Àlàmú bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í ṣàkíyèsí ihò ńlá nínú àpò rẹ̀.
en: But Alamu knew his own limitations, he knew he was far from being happy, he alone knew where the shoes pinched, he would not talk to anyone about it, he kept his lip sealed. Whenever the neighbours greeted him in the morning, Alamu would wink, grin,nod- or just hiss at them. Briskly he would hurry away on his toes, jump inside his peugoet car, back the car out of the garage, and race off - to God-knows where!

He got that car after his arrival in the country fromEngland three years ago - shortly after he took up the job of a senior Accountant with Bajoks Company Limited. A year later, he got married to Labake - the lady he met and fell in love with in England. Their wedding was lavish and expensive. Immediately after his society wedding, Alamu started noticing a big hole inside his own pocket.

passages.title: MENYO passage 327
paragraphs: Iye tó ń ná lórí ìyá rẹ̀ gan an ń kówó lọ, bẹ́ẹ̀náà ni ìtọ́jú ọkọ̀ rẹ̀ àti owó-oṣù ọmọ-ọ̀dọ̀ wọn. Kí á tó wá sọ owó-omi, owó-ilé, owó iná mọ̀nà-mọ́ná, owó-orí àti ìdápadà ẹ̀yáwó ọkọ̀ rẹ̀. Àpò Àlàmú ń jò gidigidi, ìparí oṣù sì ń jẹ́ àsìkò fún un láti làágùn tútù, ó jẹ́ àsìkò fún un láti lejú kí ó sì ranjú bí ó ṣe ń wo ètò ìṣúná owó rẹ̀ lésẹẹsẹ̀.

Lẹ́yìn tí ó bá ti gba owó oṣù rẹ̀, á wá wa ọkọ ayọ́kẹ́lẹ́ rẹ̀ bí i ọkọ̀ òfurufú elékùsọ́, á mú eré lọ ilé bí ẹ timọ̀. Nílé, á ti ara rẹ̀mọ́ yàrá, á mú ìwé ìjẹ́rìí-ẹni rẹ̀, á wá bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í ka àwọn ohun tó jẹ mọ́ ọn tí ó kọ sínú rẹ̀, láti ọjọ́ kìn-ín-ní oṣù títí di ọjọ́ tí ó kẹ́yìn. Gbogbo oṣù ni ó máa ń jọ ara wọn, ohun tó ṣẹlẹ̀ nínú oṣù kọ̀ọ̀kan máa ń jọ ara wọn pẹ̀lú ìyàtọ̀ díẹ̀ tàbí làínì ìyàtọ̀ kankan.
en: The expenses on his aged mother was one one big hole in the pocket. So also was the maintenance of his car, and the monthly allowance for their house maid. Not to talk of his regular bills: water rate, house rent, electricity bill, income tax, car loan, monthly deduction... Alamu's pocket was seriously leaking, month-end, to him, was, consequently, a time to shed cold sweat, a time to frown and knit the eyebrow as he went through his list of expenditure.

After taking his salary, Alamu would drive his car life a jet bomber, race home in lightning celerity. At home he would lock himself up inside the bedroom, pick up his diary and start reading out to himself the relevant comments he had scribbled inside it, from day one of the month, through to the last day. Every month was similar to the other, the situation was usually the same - with little or no modification.

passages.title: MENYO passage 328
paragraphs: "Àlàmú wòkè pẹ̀lú ojú tí ó kún fún ìbànújẹ́, ó dá sọ̀rọ̀ pé, ""mo gbọ́dọ̀ san owó rè níparí oṣù Agẹmọyìí, ẹ̀gbín kankan ò tún gbọdọ̀ ta lé mi fún èyí.""" Lẹ́yìn náà ni ó tún ṣí ojú ìwé mìíràn nínú ìwé ìjẹ́rìí-ẹni náà. """Làbákẹ́ kàn mí lábùkù lónìí, ọjọ́ kọkànlélógún oṣù Agẹmọ, ó lérí láti kó jáde. Owó ìtọ́jú ilé ni ó fàjà. Àti owó oúnjẹ Tinú kékeré..............ìnáw ótúntún?"

"Àpò náírà kan-àbọ̀ ni n ó tún máa yà sọ́tọ̀ láti oṣù kéje yìínáà lọ""" Ó tó gẹ́!.......... ó tó gẹ́!.........Àlàmú ké mọ́ ara rẹ̀, á pa ìwé òfònáà dé, á sì jù ú mọ́ ògiri yàrá rẹ̀. Ó tó gẹ́! Báwo ni n ó ṣe kó èyí já láìsí ìrànlọ́wọ́ agbára àìrí láti òkè wá? Níbo ni n ó ti rí adúrú owónáà? Kòṣeéṣe!
en: "Alamu looked up with a sorrow-laden eyes and mused to himself, ""I must pay him up at the end of this month of July, no further scorn should poured on me for this...""" Then, reading to himself from another page of the diary. Labake embarrassed me today 21st July threatened to pack out. Quarrel over house keeping allowance. And little Tinu's food stipend...My resolution?

"Three hundred naira to be set apart for this every month, beginning from this month of July.""" Enough!... Enough!... Alamu would shout to himself. He'd close up the accursed book and fling it furiously against the wall of his bedroom. Enough! How was he going to survive it all without the assistance of the invisible power from above? Where was he going to get all the money from? Impossible!

passages.title: MENYO passage 329
paragraphs: Làbákẹ́ kò ní ọkàn. Ó máa bú sẹ́kún ni bí ó bá rí bí ìṣòro tó bá wọn ṣe pọ̀ tó. Èyí kò sì ní daa. Àlàmú ti ṣe ìlérí fún ìyàwó rẹ̀, láti ọjọ́ ìgbéyàwó, pé kò ní sí ìdí fún un láti kábàámọ̀ tàbí kí ó sunkún. Ó ní ìdùnnú ni yóò jẹ́ títí. Tíìṣòro bá sì wà láti kojú, yóò sọ fún ìyàwó rẹ̀ pé òun kájú òṣùnwọ̀n. Á yanjú rẹ̀ bí i ọkùnrin - ọkùnrin gidi.

Àlàmú ṣojú fúrúpadà wọ inú ilé, ó mú magasíìnì ó sì bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í ṣí i láwẹ́láwẹ́ bí ó ṣe ń dúró de ilẹ̀kùn kíkàn, kí Làbáké wọlé, kí ó wò wò, kò lèè rí nǹkankan mújáde. Bí Àlàmú ṣe doríkọlẹ̀ kọjú mọ́ magasíìnì, ojú rẹ̀ pípọ́n kò níí hàn; àmì ìrẹ̀wẹ̀sì àti ìjìyà kò níí farahàn. Ohun kan tí ó yẹra fún ni ẹ̀rín aláriwo abàmì rẹ̀.
en: Labake was sentimental and tender-hearted. She would break down in tears at the magnitude of this present problem. And that would not be good. Alamu had promised his wife, right from the day of their wedding, that there would be no cause to make her regret or make her shed tears. "It was going to be sunshine and laughter all through. And if there were problems to grapple with, he'd told his wife he was up to the task. He would solve them like a man - a ""true"" man."

Alamu went back into the house with a disguised countenance, he picked up a magazine and started leafing through it while waiting for a knock on the door, let Labake come in, let her gaze and gaze, she would never make out anything. With Alamu's head bent over the magazine, those red eyeballs of his would be concealed; those lines of depression and torture across his contenance would never be revealed. One thing he would avoid was lapsing into that strange loud laugh.

passages.title: MENYO passage 330
paragraphs: Láìpẹ́, Àlàmú ń gbọ́ igbe àṣẹ tí ó ń pa fún Sènábù. Ariwo ṣíbí àti ife pẹ̀lú abọ́ ayọ́ alumí ń dé etí rẹ̀ náà - ó túra ká. Oúnjẹ wo ni Làbákẹ́ máa sè fún alẹ́? Oúnjẹ tó bá àsìkò náà mu ni láìsí àní-àní.

Oúnjẹ ìgbà ọwọ́n. Bóyá ẹ̀kọ pẹ̀lú ẹ̀fọ́ àti ẹja òkú-èkó pọ́ọ́kú tútù... tàbí kí ó jẹ́ ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ bíbọ̀ tí wọ́n wọ́n iyọ̀, ata àti epo sí. Kò sí àwáwí, ká ṣá ti rí nǹkan láti so ọkàn àti ara pọ̀. Pẹ̀lú ìrètí pé ohun gbogbo á dára kí ó tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í sú Làbákẹ́, kó sì tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í ṣàkíyèsí àyípadà gbogbo nǹkan.
en: Very soon, Alamu heard her shouting instructions to Zenabu. The loud clang of cups and spoons, and the resonant, metallic sound of the aluminium plates reached his ears also- and he heaved a sigh of relief. What meal was Labake going to prepare for the evening? A meal that would fit the mood of time no doubt.

Meal of a hard time. Perhaps eko with vegetables and the cheap frozen fish... Or it could be ordinary boiled plantain sprinkled with salt, pepper and red palm-oil... Well.. No complaint. Just something, anything - to keep body and soul together. With the hope that all would be well before Labake would be completely fed up with the situation at home and start noticing the change in the order of things.

passages.title: MENYO passage 331
paragraphs: Lẹ́yìn wíwá ojútùú síi, á wá pe ìyàwó rẹ̀ jókòó pẹ̀lú ìgbéraga láti kéde sí i. """Jókòó síbí kí o tẹ́tí sí mi Làbákẹ́, ìṣòro ti ń wà ṣùgbọ́n o ò mọ̀, mo fi ọ̀rọ̀náà pamọ́ fún ọ nítorí pé mo mọ irú ènìyàn tí o jẹ́." Wà á sunkún sunkún sunkún, inú rẹ kò ní ídùn, ìrẹ̀wẹ̀sì yóò sì dé bá ọ, ìdí nìyí ti mo fi kó wọn pamọ́ fún ọ, ṣùgbọ́n Làbákẹ́, má bẹ̀rù, ìṣòro náà ti kásẹ̀ ńlẹ̀.
Yin Olúwa lógo! Yóò sì tẹ̀síwájú láti máa ṣe bí ọkùnrin. Kò sì ní gbé ìbànújẹ́ tàbí àṣàrò rẹ̀ sójú. Nísinsìnyí, Àlàmú gún èjìká rẹ̀, ó ya ẹnu rẹ̀ gbàgà.........lẹ́yìn náà -
en: After solving it he would proudly call his wife and announce to her. """Sit down here and listen to me Labake, you didn't know, but there had been problems, I kept the problems away because I know your nature very well." You'll cry, cry and cry... Feel badly depressed, so I kept it away, but don't worry Labake, the problem has been solved...
"Praise God!""" Meanwhile, he would continue to play the man. Nevermore would he wear his sorrow and muse, so now, Alamu shrugged, parted his lips and opened wide his mouth... Then -

passages.title: MENYO passage 332
paragraphs: Ìgbà wo ni yóò ṣe gbogbo èyí dà? Èyí ni àwọn ìbéèrè tí Àlàmú ń bí ara rẹ̀ ní àbítúnbí. "Àwọn ìdáhùn tó ń tẹ̀lé e ni.......""kò ṣe é ṣe........""""kò ṣe é ṣe............""ṣé kì í ṣe ọkọ àti ìyàwó tí ó ń gbé abẹ́ òrùlé kan náà̀ ni wọ́n?"

Bí ó ṣe ń tiraka láti fi pamọ́ tó, bẹ́ẹ̀ náà ni ó ń fi ara rẹ̀ hàn tó. Síbẹ̀ síbẹ̀, ó tẹ̀síwájú láti gbìyànjú, kò sí ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ nínú ìgbìyànjú rárá. Nínú yàrá rẹ̀, yóò ti orí ara rẹ̀ bọ abẹ́ ìrọ̀rí rẹ̀, á sì máa sọ̀rọ̀ kẹ́lẹ́kẹ́lẹ́ sí ara rẹ̀.
en: For how long was he going to contain the situation all alone? These were the questions Alamu asked himself again and again. "And the answer that came each time was ""not practicable..."" ""not possible..."" Were they not husband and wife, living under the same roof, sharing the same flat?"

The more he struggled to hide, the more he revealed himself. Still he continued to try. No sin in trying really. Inside his room, he would bury his head under the pillow and talk in whispers to himself.

passages.title: MENYO passage 333
paragraphs: Tako ìfé-inú Àlàmú, ó rí i pé òun ti ń fi àwòrán nǹkan hàn Làbákẹ́ lọ́nà tààrà àti ẹ̀bùrú. Gbogbo re ló ń fi íhàn - gbogbo Ìhùwàsí rẹ̀ sí Làbákẹ́, gbogbo ìbára-ẹni-sọ̀rọ̀ ojoojúmọ́ wọ̣n. """Àlàmú, ṣé o rí onílé wa lanáà ?"""
"""Onílé?, níbo Làbákẹ́""" """Yé é mú mi ṣeré Àlàmú. Bí ó ṣe ń lọ, mo mọ̀ pé o rí i. O kàn ń sá pamọ́ ni." Ẹsẹ̀ rẹ ń hàn lábẹ́ ilẹ̀kùn ilé-ìtọ̀ níbití o ti ń sá pamọ́.
en: Against Alamu's wish, he found he was putting Labake in the full picture of things - directly or indirectly. Everything gave him away - his general behavior towards Labake, his daily conversation with her. """Did you not see the landlord yesterday Alamu?"""
"""Landlord? Where Labake?""" """Stop teasing Alamu. All along, I knew you saw him.You were mere dodging." Your legs showed behind the toilet door where you were hiding.

passages.title: MENYO passage 334
paragraphs: """Ẹẹẹẹẹnnnn.....Bẹ́ẹ̀ , Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni? Kílódé tí ojú Ọkùnrin náà ṣe le koko tí ó sì ń tọ́ka àìnínú dídùn sí wa?""" """Ó ní kí o wá rí òun lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀. Mo gbàgbé láti sọfún ẹ""" """Hùn, hùn ún, lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀? Hùn hùn, mo rí i bẹ́ẹ̀."""
Àyà Àlàmú já. ṣùgbọ́n ó tètètúnraṣe - ó rín ẹ̀rín sí i - ó ń fi Ọkùnrinn náà ṣeré. """Báwo ni o ṣe sanwófún un, ṣé kìṣì?"""
en: """Well yea yea? Why was the man looking so displeased and so angry?" "He said you should come and see him immediately. I forgot to mention that to you.""" """Hum, hum, Immediately? Hum, hum. I see."""
Alamu's heart missed a beat. But he quickly readjusted - laughing it over - playing the man! """How did you pay him, Alamu? By cash?"""

passages.title: MENYO passage 335
paragraphs: Làbákẹ́ yọ ìwé pélébé kan jad́e nínú báàgì ìfàlọ́wọ́ rẹ̀, ó sì mú un fún ọkọ rẹ̀. """Wo èyí. Sọ̀wédowó tí o fún mi fún owó ìtọ́jú ilé.""" """Kílódé tí ò ń mú un fún mi Làbákẹ́, mú un lọ........lọ sí ilé ifowópamọ́sí."""

"""Mo ti mú un lọ... ṣùgbọ́n ó ta padà. Kò sówó níbẹ̀""" """Ta padà kẹ̀?,"" Àlàmú fi sùúrù béèrè. Ó gba sọ̀wédowó náà lọ́wọ́ rẹ̀, ó ń kálòlò........""mà á wá.......wánǹkan ṣe sí i." Sọ̀wédowó tí Àlàmú fún onílé ti ta padà lẹ́èmẹ́ta!
en: Labake fished out from her small handbag a piece of paper, and handed it over to her husband. """See this. The cheque you issued to me for the house-keeping allowance.""" """Why give me Labake? Present it to... to.. to the bank."""

"""It has been presented... But now returned. It bounced.""" """Bounced?"" Alamu asked slowly. He took the cheque from Labake muttering, ""I'll see what else can be done.""" Alamu's landlord's cheque had bounced three times!

passages.title: MENYO passage 336
paragraphs: Lóòótọ́, títí ìgbà wo ni yóò fi nǹkan pamọ́ fún Làbákẹ́ dà? "Èsì dé, lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi lọ́gán ""Kì í ṣe fún oṣù kan mọ́ brọ̀dá!........kì í ṣe fún ọ̀sẹ̀ kan pàápàá!....""" Ohun kan wà tí ó ń tìí, kò jẹ́ kí ó ká páìṣe rẹ̀, ó ń sọ ọ́ di ọ̀dájú láìsí àní-àní.

Ìdí nìyí tó jẹ́ pé lẹ́yìn ọjọ́ mélòó kan, Àlàmú rí ara rẹ̀ tó ń dá àrà túntún... Ó gbé ife ọtí si ẹnu rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú ẹ̀gbọ̀n rìrì, ó gbá ife ọtínáà mú gírígírí pẹ̀lú ọwọ́ rẹ̀ méjèèjì, nítorí ó jọ wí pé gáà sìinú ọtí náà fẹ́ gbọ̀n ife náà kúrò ní ọwọ́ rẹ̀! Àwọn gáàsì yìí jọ ìjìinú òkun lójú rẹ̀! Ìjìinú ife!
en: For how long, really, was he going to succeed in Keeping Labake out of the whole situation? The answer came, once more with a note of finality: not for a month more brother!... not even for a week more!... There is a thing - an irresistible force - urging him on. Impelling him to loose control over his own action, and pushing him headlong into desperation. Inevitably.

That was why, a few days later, Alamu found himself breaking new ground... He held a mug firmly wth his two hands - because it appeared to him that the gentle ripples of the liquid content were soon going to shake the mug off his hands! The ripples inside looked to him like the gathering storm inside the deep ocean! A storm inside the mug.

passages.title: MENYO passage 337
paragraphs: Àlàmú tiraka láti má jẹ́ kí ohun ṣíṣàn náà padà wá sí ẹnu rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí èébì. Ó fi tipá tipá tì í wọ ìsàlẹ̀ ikùn rẹ̀. Láìsí àní-àní, inú àwọn aràn inú rẹ̀ dùn nínú lọ́hùn-ún... Òógùn ṣarajọ sí ìpọ̀nrí rẹ̀. Ojúrẹ̀ bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í wò bàìbàì.
Ójẹ́ kí orí rẹ̀ wú, óbẹ̀rẹ̀ si í pòòyì. Bí ó ṣe fẹ́ kí ó rí rè é. Ófẹ́ kí ọtí pa òun dáadáa.
en: Alamu struggled not to allow the liquid content to come back into his mouth in vomit. He forced it down down the tummy. The worms were no doubt happy inside the bowel and heard the faint chorus of some riotous revel... Perspiration gathered over his brow. His eyes started seeing double.
It made his head swim, he started reeling. That was the way he wanted it. He wanted to get intoxicated.

passages.title: MENYO passage 338
paragraphs: Èyí lè jẹ́ kí ó gbàgbé gbogbo ìdààmú rẹ̀, àti gbogbo ìtọ́jú ayé - bí ó bá tiè jẹ́ fún ìgbà díẹ̀. Òórùn ọtí borí òórùn inú ilé. Ó ti ojú fèrèsé yàrá Àlàmú w ọinú yàrá ìgbàfẹ wọn, ó sì gba ibẹ̀ wọ yàrá Làbákẹ́. Làbákẹ́ gbọ́ òórùn yìí, tì fura tì fura ó yọ́ kẹ́lẹ́-kẹ́lẹ́ lọ sí yàrá ọkọ rẹ̀, ó sì yọjú láti ibi ihò kọ́kọ́rọ́................ó fẹ́ ẹ̀ ẹ́ dákú pẹ̀lú ohun tí ó rí, ó ṣebí àlá ni òun ń lá.

Ó fi ọwọ́ bọ́ ojú rè láìmọye ìgbà. Ohùn ìgò ọtí tí ó ń kan ife Àlàmú jáde geere-ge, Làbákẹ́ sì rí i pékì í ṣe àlá ni òun ń lá rárá. Òótọ́ ni, òótọ́ pátápátá. Kòrókòró ni ó ń wo ọkọ rẹ̀ tí ó ń gbafẹ́ lórí àgbà-n-tara, ó sì ń mu ọtí rẹ̀ láìbìkítà - ó ń bá ara rẹ̀ sọ̀rọ̀, ó sì ń rín ẹ̀rín, ẹ̀rín àsàsàmọsì.
en: That would make him forget all the worries, all the cares of this material world - at least for some time. The smell of alcohol permeated the air inside the house. It escaped from the window panes in Alamu's room and invaded the sitting room and Labake's bedroom. Labake sniffed it in instinctively, her curiosity was immediately aroused, she tip-toed to her husband's bed room and peeped through the key hole... she nearly collapsed from what she saw, she was merely dreaming.

She rubbed her eyes several times. The sound of the beer bottle knocking on Alamu's mug came out compellingly loud and clear and Labake realized she was not dreaming at all. It was reality. Stark reality. There in front of her was her husband, relaxing in the easy chair and sipping his beer with complete abandon - talking to himself and laughing all along! - an outlandish loud laugh.

passages.title: MENYO passage 339
paragraphs: """Kí ni? Èyí? Ṣé èyí ni ò ń sọ?,"" ó béèrè ìbéèrè tí kò wúlò........ooooh! ọtí bíà. Kí lótún fẹ́ jẹ́ Làbá....... Làbákẹ́?""" Ó mí èémí líle. Èsì àìbìkítà Àlàmú ti mú ọ̀rọ̀ náà sú Làbákẹ́ pátápátá. """Ọtí nìyẹn Làbákẹ́,"" ó tún fàágùn, ""ṣé o.....o.....kò ní ojú láti ..........láti ríran ni?.....""Èsì àfojúdi Àlàmú bá Làbákẹ́ lójijì."

"""Ṣùgbọ́n, o ò fẹnu kan ọtí rí láyé rẹ Àlàmú?" """Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni..........nígbà náà ńkọ́? Ìgbà náà wá ń kọ́?"" Àlàmú fèsì padà, 'ó yẹ kí o mọ̀, ó yẹ kí o mọ̀." "Làbá.....Làbák......ẹm... Mo ní láti bẹ̀rẹ ẹ̀ lọ́jọ́ kan.. òní sì ni.........òní tí.......tí ẹm....fún ìdí èyí?........mo ní fún ìdí èyi!"""
en: """What ? This? You mean this?"" he asked rather unnecessarily, ""oh that's beer. What else can it be Laba... Labake?""" He breathed heavily. The casual tone of Alamu's reply completely put Labake off. """That's beer Labake,"" he stressed again, ""Haven't you... you eyes to...to see?"" Alamu's impudent remark caught her off-guard."

"""But you've never tasted beer all your life Alamu?""" "Yes... And therefore?... so therefore?"" Alamu snapped back, ""you should know... you should know." "Laba... Labak... em... I have to start it one day ...And it is today... Today that ... that em...so therefore?...i say so therefore!"""

passages.title: MENYO passage 340
paragraphs: """O ti ń fa sìgá náà""" Àlàmú kò dá a lóhùn. Ó gbójú kúrò, ó tanná sí sìgá, ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í fà á. Ópa ètè pọ̀, bí àpamọ́wọ́ onírin, èéfín tí ó ń fẹ́ jáde pẹ̀lú bátànì lọ sí òkè àjà. """Àlàmú!...... Àlàmú! Ṣé ìwọ rè é Àlàmú? ọtí àti sìgá?,"" Làbákẹ́ béèrè pẹ̀lú àìgbàgbọ́."

Àlàmú rẹ́rìn-ín pẹ̀lú àìbalẹ̀ àyà, ó sì tún sìgá rẹ̀ fà pẹ́ dáadáa. Ojú rẹ̀ ràn kankan. Báyìí èéfín sìgá pá a lórí, ó sì bẹ̀rẹ̀ ikọ́. """Forí... foríjìmí Làbákẹ́... hùn... ṣo rí i... ṣo rí i... ẹ̀... ǹ...""" """Rí kíni?"""
en: """You've started smoking too.""" Alamu did not answer. He looked away, lit the cigarette and start puffing at it. He brought together his lips, like a stringed purse, and the smoke he blew out formed an intricate, crisis-cross pattern on its way up the ceiling! """Alamu?... Alamu? Is that you Alamu? Drinking and smoking?"" Labake asked in disbelief."

Alamu laughed nervously and took another deep, long puff. His eyes bulged. This time the smoke went into the wrong way and he started coughing... """Ex... Excuse me Labake... Hum... you see...you see...em...""" """see what?"""

passages.title: MENYO passage 341
paragraphs: """Mo ní láti wà níbè hùn hùn hùn......tí mo bá ha ha ha ha.........sì dé bẹ̀............""" """Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni, mo gbọ́dọ̀ lọ síbẹ̀ kí n ẹm.....ẹ̀ ṣàlàyé ìrísí ẹm.......ẹm........dúró ná, àrídájú kékeré kan hùn...hùn....hùn....hùn ṣe pàtàkì báyìí........mo ní ìrètí láti yíwọn lọ́kàn padà ẹm....." "Èyí jẹ́ nǹkankan láti sọfúnwọn.....ẹm ẹm......ó dáa.....jẹ́ kí ó wá.....wá.....títí dalẹ́ nígbà tí n......ẹm.....ẹm."""

Kò sí ohun tí Làbákẹ́ lè ṣe láti jẹ́kí Àlàmú parí gbólóhùn rẹ̀. Bí ó bá ti fi gbogbo ara sọ̀rọ̀ bíi kíkan orí mọ́lẹ̀, kí ó nawọ́, kí ó kan tábìlì, ó ti parí gbólóhùn náà nìyẹn! Àmọ́, Làbákẹ́ ti rí àrídájú kan mú jáde nínú gbogbo èyí, òhun tí ó sìfúnka mọ́ nìyí. Gbogbo àkùdè gbólóhùn Àlàmú yìí níí ṣe pẹ̀lú lílọ sí ibìkan láti lọ rí ẹnìkan láti lọ mú ìlérí kan ṣe tàbí láti lọ ṣàlàyé nǹkan tàbí láti wá ojútùú sí ọ̀rọ̀ kan tàbí láti ta wọ́n lólobó nípa nǹkan...
en: "I will have to be there hum-hum-hum... And when ah-ah-ah get there...""" """Yes, I must go there, and em...e... explain the aspect of em...em..."" ""But wait - a little clarification is hum - hum- well... necessary here... I hope to convince em..." "This one thing to tell em... o.k. let it remain like... like... until tonight when I... em... em..."""

There was nothing Labake could do to make Alamu complete his sentence. He would gesticulate, nod his head, point a finger, tap the table and that would be the end of that sentence! But Labake got one fact out of it all, and that was what she now held unto. ALL Alamu's uncompleted sentences had to do with going somewhere to visit somebody to fulfil a promise, to offer an explanation about something to clarify an issue to supply a piece of information...

passages.title: MENYO passage 342
paragraphs: Làbákẹ́ sin Àlàmú lọ sí tíátà ní gbàgede Luchester láti lọ wòran ijó rẹ̀. Ó jẹ́ ìran tó dùn-ún wò. Josephine jó ijo náàdáadáa tó wú àwọn ènìyàn lórí. Inú Àlàmú dùn yàtọ̀ sí ti àwọn èrò ìwòran yòókù. Làbákẹ́ wo Àlàmú lójú, ó sì rí ìfẹ́ Josephine lójú rẹ̀, ó sì kìlòfún un lójú ẹsẹ̀. Ó sì ti rò ó wí pé Àlàmú ti gbọ́ràn. Ṣùgbọ́n lẹ́yìn ìgbà náà, Làbákẹ́ rí àwòrán Josephine mẹ́ta nínú àpò àyà aṣọ Àlàmú. Lọjọ́ míì ń Làbákẹ́ ká a ní ọgbà iṣẹ́re pẹ̀lú ọmọbìnrin náà.

Fún ọsẹ kan gbáko, ogun tútù wáyé láàárín Àlàmú pẹ̀lú Làbákẹ́. ṣùgbọ́n wọ́n parí ẹ̀ nígbẹ̀yìn gbẹ́yín. Aáwọ̀ mìíràn tó tún wáyé láàárín wọn wáyé nítorí Caroline, akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ìmọ̀-òfin láti ìlú Kẹ́ńyà. Làbákẹ́ káwọn ní gbàgede Trafalgar láàárín gùngùn ìlú Lọ́ńdọ́ọ̀nù, wọ́n ń fi ẹyẹlẹ́ ṣere tíwọ́n sì ń ya àwòrán lábẹ́ ère Nelson ńlá!
en: Labake had accompanied Alamu to the theatre at Leicester Square in London to watch Josephine perform that day. It was a good show. Graceful Josephine wriggled her shapely hips seductively, to the rhythmof the tom-tom, trumpet and the cymbal - to the admiration of the audience. Alamu was particularly excited. Labake looked at Alamu and saw in his eyes a slow burn of passion for Josephine and she had warned him there and then to take his time - to play it cool. Shye had thought that the end of it all - that the matter had been laid to rest. But at a latter day, Labake retrieved three of Josephine's pictures from inside the breast pocket of Alamu's coat... Then there was the day Labake caught him alone with Josephine at the park.

For one whole week a cold war raged between Alamu and Labake. But finally, they made up. The next quarrel with Alamu was over Caroline, a law student from Kenya. She caught them at Trafalgar Square in the heart of London, playing with pigeons and taking photographs below the giant Nelson Statue!

passages.title: MENYO passage 343
paragraphs: Ohùn ìmáàmù já geere lórí ariwo ẹ̀rọ amóhùndúngbẹ̀mù ní kùtùkùtù òwúrò ọjọ́ kan, tí ó ń pe àwọn ẹrú Ọlọ́run láti wá kírun. """Ẹ̀yin ọmọ Ànọ́bì ẹ dìde ń lẹ̀ kẹ́ẹ ké pe Allah" Kí ẹ sì wọ Al-jọ́n-ń-nà
Ibi àlàáfíà àti ìbùkùn ayérayé Ṣùgbọ́n ẹ̀yin ọmọ àṣètán-ń-nì, ẹ sùn lọbí igi Kí a sì tì yín sí Jáà-nọ́n-mọ̀
en: "The solitary voice of the Imam came out loud over the loud-speaker early one morning, summoning all ""servant of God"" to prayer." """Children of Ananbi wake up to worship Allah" And enter aljon-no
The place of eternal peace and blessedness But you children of Satan, sleep off like logs And be pushed like jaa-non-mo.

passages.title: MENYO passage 344
paragraphs: Irú àwọn ọkùnrin yìí ni ó wọlé wá pẹ̀lú Àlàmú , méjì irúwọn. Làbákẹ́ wo àwọn àlejò ọkọ rẹ̀ yìí tìfura tìfura. Kí ni ìbáṣepò Àlàmú pẹ̀lú irú àwọn ènìyàn yìí?

Ṣé kò léwu kí àwọn ènìyàn lásán kan tí wọn kò mọ̀ máa wọ irú ilé bíi tiwọn? Àwọn ọlọ́ṣà àti àwọn afipábánilòpọ̀ pọ̀ káàkiri ìgboro ní àsìkò yìí. Ìjábọ̀ ìwé-ìròyìn ojoojúmọ́, ń sọ̀rọ̀ nípa àwọn oníjàgídí jàgan yìí, tí wọ́n ń ṣe èyí tó wù wọ́n káàkiri ìlú.
en: These were the type of men who now came into the house with Alamu, two of them. Labake eyed her husband's visitors suspiciously. What was Alamu's business with the likes of these people?

Was it really safe having just anybody come inside a home like theirs?.... Robbers and rapists were very much around in town these days. Newspaper-reports everyday, spoke of the highway men having free days all about town.

passages.title: MENYO passage 345
paragraphs: Láàárín ìṣẹ́jú kan, ó ti wà níwájú ọkọ rẹ̀, ódúró ní ìfojú-rin-jú pẹ̀lú rẹ̀, ó ń retí àlàyé. """Ta ni àwọn ẹni yìí Àlàmú ? Kí ni ìdí tíwọ́n fi wà níbí? Kí ni ìtumọ̀ gbogbo èyí tí ò ń ṣe yìí?" """Dúró ...dúró Làbákẹ́...mo mú awọn ọkùnrin méjì náà wá,"" Àlàmú bẹ̀rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀ kẹ́lẹ́kẹ́lẹ́, ""láti wá ṣe àtúnṣe fáànù olókè, ẹ̀rọ amómitutù àti ẹ̀rọ amóhùn-màwòrán. Kò sí nǹkan mìíràn Làbákẹ́."""

Làbákẹ́ wo ọkọ rẹ̀ tìfura tìfura. Kí ni ìdí tí ó fi ní láti sọ̀rọ̀ kẹ́lẹ́kẹ́lẹ́? Kí ni ìdí tí ó fi ní láti sáré wọ yàrá rẹ̀ báyẹn? Kíá, awọn àlejò ti bẹ̀rẹ̀ iṣẹ́. Ní ìkọ̀ọ̀kan, wọ́n bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í tú awọn nǹkan náà sílẹ̀. Wọ́n gbé awọn ohun èèlò yìí wò fún bí i ìṣẹ́jú díẹ̀, ìṣẹ́jú mẹ́wàá tàbí jùbẹ́ẹ̀ lọ. Nígbẹ̀yìn gbẹ́yín, wọ́n bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í gbé awọn nǹkan wọ̀nyí kúrò nínú yàrá ìgbàlejò.
en: In a minute, she was standing face to face with him, demanding an explanation. """Who are these people, Alamu? Why are they here? And what is the meaning of all these you are doing?" """Wait... wait Labake... I brought in the two men', Alamu began, in whisper, ""to do some repair work on the ceiling fan, fridge and the television. Nothing more Labake'."

Labake looked curiously at her husband. Why did he have to talk to her in whispers? Why did he have to rush inside his room that way? Soon, the two visitors set at work. And one by one they started disconnecting the items. They fiddled with each of the items for some minutes - ten minutes or thereabout. Eventually, they started carrying the items out of the sitting room.

passages.title: MENYO passage 346
paragraphs: Làbákẹ́ dìídì tiraka láti dá omi ojú tí ó ti péjọ sí ojú rẹ̀, tí ó ti ń ṣe ìran rẹ̀ bàìbàì padà. Ṣùgbọ́n nígbà tí aruwo ẹ̀rín Àlàmú mìíràn tún dé etí ìgbó rẹ̀ láti yàrá Àlàmú, ó gba omi ojú wọ̀nyí láàyè láti yára ṣàn wá sí ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ rẹ̀ láìdáwọ́dúró. Bóyá o ti ń to ilé fún obìnrin mìíràn ní ìgboro. Ó sì tún mọ̀ọ́mọ̀ mú àwọn ọkùnrin ìgboro méjì yìí wá láti wá ṣe àṣepé ìtànjẹ rèf ún Làbákẹ́.

Ṣùgbọ́n ẹ̀rín abanilẹ́rù ọkọ rẹ̀. Ó sì ń dún sí i lọ́pọlọ tí ó sì ń dún síi bíi agogo ẹgbẹ̀rún lẹ́ẹ̀kan náà. Orí bẹ̀rẹ̀ si ífọ́ ọ gidi bíìgbà tó fẹ́ là síméjì. Nínú àwòrán tíwọ́n gbé kọ́ ògiri níwájú rẹ̀ gan-an ni Àlàmú wà, bí ó ṣe di ọwọ́ rẹ̀ mú tìfẹ́-tìfẹ́ lọ́jọ́ ìgbéyàwó wọn pẹ̀lú ẹ̀rín ìdùnnú lójú rẹ̀. Órẹwà púpọ̀. Ẹ̀rín àtọkànwá, ẹ̀rín tòótọ́. Ní alẹ́ àkọ́kọ́ lẹ́yìn ayẹyẹ ìgbéyàwó olówó iyebíye tíwọ́n ṣe, Àlàmú pariwo síi pẹ̀lú ayọ̀.
en: Labake fought desperately to keep back the tears which had now gathered inside her eyes, blurring her vision. But when the noise of Alamu's fresh outburst of laughter reached her ears from inside Alamu's room again, she allowed the gathering tears to rain down her cheeks in care-free torrents. He'd probably started to furnish the house of the other woman in town. And had deliberately brought in these two men of the city to make perfect this latest trick on her.

But that grotesque laugh of her husband's. It continued to re-echo in her brain coming to her forcefully again and again like the terrible clang of a thousand bells. Her head itches badly, threatening to split open. In the picture hanging on the wall just in front of her in the siting room was Alamu, holding her hand lovingly on their wedding day, a broad happy smile on his face. He looked handsome. The smile was real, natural and sincere. On their first night together after their expensive wedding ceremony, Alamu had shouted to her in joy.

passages.title: MENYO passage 347
paragraphs: Àlàmú kò sọfún àwọn ènìyàn rẹ̀ pé ó ti gba àmì ti rẹ̀gẹ́gẹ́ bí i aṣaralọ́ṣọ̀ọ́ nílùú Lọ́ńdọ́ọ̀nù. Kò sí ẹni tí ó rí gbogbo àwọn magasíinì àti ìwé ìròyìn tí Làbákẹ́ ti fara hàn gẹ́gẹ́ bíi omidan ológe àwòmáleèlọ. Ènìyàn kan ṣoṣo tó mọ̀ nípa gbogbo èyí ni Àdìó, ọ̀rẹ́ tímọ́tímọ́ Àlàmú tí ó jẹ́ akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ìmọ̀-òfin nígbà náà ní Lọ́ńdọ́ọ̀nù.

Díẹ̀ ló kù kí ìyá Àlàmú mọ irú iṣẹ́ tí Làbákẹ́ yàn láàyò láyé rẹ̀, lọ́jọ́ tí ó ń wo àwòrán inú ìwé ìfàwò ránsí rẹ̀ ní kété tí wọ́n ṣe ìgbéyàwó. Hùn hùn, ṣé ìyàwó rẹ rè é Àlàmú? Ṣé Làbákẹ́ rè é? ìyá àgbà náà ń bèèrè, ó nawó sí àwòrán ọmọbìnrin tí ó wọ ṣòkòtò jíǹsì tó lẹ̀ mọ́ ọn lára típẹ́ típẹ́ pẹ̀lú èwù péńpé tó fàyàá lẹ̀, ó sì rẹ́rìn-ín músẹ́.
en: Alamu did not tell his people that Labake had made her own small mark in London as a model. Nobody saw all those magazine and newspapers where Labake featured as pin-up girl. The only person who knew all the details was his bosom friend - Adio - who was then a law student in London.

But indirectly, Alamu's old mother nearly got to know of the professional aspect of Labake's life the day she was looking through Labake's photo album. That was shortly after their marriage. """Hum.., hum.. Is this your wife Alamu?" Is this Labake? the old woman asked, pointing to the enlarged picture of a lady wearing tight jeans, open-neck blouse, and smiling radiantly.

passages.title: MENYO passage 348
paragraphs: "Àwòrán tí ó pa ẹgbẹ̀rún méjì pọ́n-ùn bìrìtì kó sápò Làbákẹ́ tí ó sì yọrí sí lẹ́tà ìbu-ọlá-fún tó lé ní igba láti ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn òǹkàwé magasíìnì ""Man""s world"" tó mọ rírì káàkiri gbogbo Íngílandì." Wọ́n ń fẹ́ àdírẹ́sì. Wọ́n ń fẹ́ gbé e lọ jẹ oúnjẹ ọ̀sán, oúnjẹ alẹ́, láti jọ lọ ya àwòrán. Wọ́n ń fẹ́ gbà á lálejò, wọ́n ń fẹ́ fi àwòrán ráńṣẹ́ sí i àti bẹ́ẹ̀ bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ. "Màmá tẹ̀síwájú pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀ rẹ̀, ""wò ó Àlàmú, ìyàwó rẹ kì í bo àyà. Ó ń ṣí ọmú rẹ̀ sílẹ̀."

"Kò yẹ kí obìnrin ṣe eléyìí. Ìwọ fún ra à rẹ kò lè sọ fún ìyàwó rẹ kí ó de bọ́tíìnì aṣọ rẹ̀ dáadáa....""" Màmá tún ṣí ojú ìwé mìíràn nínú ìwé àwòrán náà: """Wá wò ó Àlàmú, wo ìyàwó rẹ bí ó ti ṣí ikùn sílẹ̀. Wo bí Làbákẹ́ ṣe yẹ itan, wo bí ó ṣe na ẹsẹ̀."
en: "The picture which earned Labake two thousand British pounds and resulted in over two hundred letters of adoration from the appreciative readers of ""Man's World' all over England." They wanted her address. They wanted to take her out for lunch, for dinner, to the pictures. They wanted her to visit them, to send her photographs - and so on and so on. """Look Alamu,"" Mama had continued, ""your wife does not cover her chest. She exposes her breasts."

"A woman should not do that. You yourself did not ask your wife to button up her blouse properly....""" Mama opened to another page of the album: And now, look, Alamu see your wife exposing her stomach. See the way Labake parts her thighs, the way she stretches out her legs'.

passages.title: MENYO passage 349
paragraphs: Ìbáṣepò rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú Làbákẹ́ kò dán mọ́rán rárá. "Ìgbàkigbà tí wọ́n bá pàdé, ọ̀rọ̀ wọn máa ń dà bíi òwe ""Àáyáà ti Ògúngbè,"" ọdẹ ni Ògúngbè, ó gẹ̀gùn sílẹ̀ de àáyá." Bí àáyá ti ń bọ̀, ó kóra ro, nítorí pé ó fura pé ewu ń bẹ nítòsí. Ó nàró, ó wò yíká.

Ògúngbè tó ń dúró dè é bẹ̀rẹ̀ mọ́lè. Nígbà tí àáyá kò rí nǹkan abàmì, ótún bẹ̀rẹ̀ mọ́lẹ̀. Ògúngbè tí ó ń ṣọ́ ọ náà nàró, ó ń gbaradì láti yìn ín ní bájínátù. Ìhùwàsí àti ìṣesí Màmá kò ṣe Làbákẹ́ ní nǹkan. Kò tiẹ̀ mì ín rárá. Ó ń fara mọ́ gbogbo ìwà màmá, inú Àlàmú sì dùn pé kò sí ìjà kankan. "Ìyálenu ni pé gbogbo wàhálà Làbákẹ́ kò nínǹkan ṣe pẹ̀lú màmá tàbí ẹlòmìíràn. Bí kò ṣe ọkùnrin tó gbé e wọlé fún ""ìgbà tó dára àti ìgbà tó burú."""
en: Her relationship with Labake was a patch- patch' one. And each time they met, it was the proverbial hunter Ogungbe meeting the cunning monkey of the savannah forest. The cunning monkey would stand high on his toes and strain his neck to fish out Ogungbe and escape imminent death,

But, clever man Ogungbe, on the other hand, would stoop low to the ground, almost kissing the dust, with his gun ready for the final kill. Mama's attitude, by and large, did not seem to worry Labake. It did not bother her - at least initially. She continued patching on with Mama and Alamu was very happy that, there was no confrontation. It was therefore an irony that all of Labake's worries had nothing to do with Mama or any other person. But with the very man who brought her in, for better for worse'.

passages.title: MENYO passage 350
paragraphs: Ẹ̀rọ amómitutù, amóhùn-máwòrán àti fáànù olókè ti ṣáájú rẹ̀ lọ. Bóyá àwọn àga ni yóò kàn, gáàsì ìdáná ti gbogbo rọ́ọ̀gì àti kápẹ́ẹ̀tì.......... Tó bá yá lọ́jọ́ kan, á wá ṣàkíyèsí pé Àlàmú fúnrare ti lọ, tí kò sí ní padà wá mọ́ láé. Kí ni ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ rẹ̀ gan-an tí Àlàmú fi wá fẹ́ figi gún àjọṣepọ̀ wọn.

Ìfòpinsí ìgbéyàwó lábẹ́ òfin gbọ́dọ̀ ní àtì lẹ́yìn, ìdí abájọ tí ó mún ádóko ní ilẹ́ ẹjọ́, láì jẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀ ilé-ẹjọ́ á sọwọ́ ẹjọ́ náà sílẹ̀, wọ́n á díye lé olùfìsun láti san. Òun gan an ni óyẹkí ó pé Àlàmú lẹ́jọ́fún ìkọ̀sílẹ̀ ìtànjẹ. Láìsí àní-àní, irú ẹjọ́ bẹ́ẹ̀ rọrùn láti borí.
en: The fridge, the television and the ceiling fan had gone ahead of him. Next it was probably going to be the turn of the chairs, the gas cooker and all those rugs and carpets... Then one day, she would just discover that Alamu himself had gone never to come back home again! What was her offence really that Alamu now wanted to dash their association on the rocks?

The termination of any legal union should be backed up with very strong reasons in a court of law otherwise the court would throw out the suit and award heavy costs against the plaintiff. She was, in fact, the one who ought to drag Alamu to court for desertion and double-dealing. And surely such a case would be easy to win.

passages.title: MENYO passage 351
paragraphs: Ọkùnrin ni Àlàmú, ó lè dájú, bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé kò sí ìdí fún un láti ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n nǹkan ò ṣe é gbẹ́kẹ̀lé ní ilé ayé abàmì tí ò gún régé yìí. Làbákẹ́ sì ń ṣe jẹ́jẹ́. Tinú kékeré rá lọ sí ọ̀dọ̀ rẹ̀, ó sì dìde di orúnkún ìyá rẹ̀ múfún ìrànlọ́wọ́.
Làbáké fa ọmo náà mọ́ra tìfẹ́-tìfẹ́, ó sì wo inú ojúrẹ̀ ó sì ń fọwọ́ pa á nímú. Tinú rẹ́rìn-ín músẹ́, ó ń ṣe àfihàn eyín iwáju rẹ̀ túntún. """Bàbá-ba-ba-ba,"" ó ń sọ̀rọ̀ wẹ́rẹ́wẹ́rẹ́."
en: Alamu was a man. He could be desperate, although there was no reason on earth why be should be but things could be so unpredictable in this strange, odd world. Labake kept her cool. Little Tinu crawled to her and stood up holding her knees for support.

Labake propped the little girl affectionately to herself and gazed into her small twinkling eyes, stroking her nose. Tinu smiled, proudly showing her newly-formed front teeth. """Papa-pa-pa-pa', she babbled."

passages.title: MENYO passage 352
paragraphs: "ṣé o lè rákòrò lọbá a kí o sìrẹ́rìn-ín músẹ́bí o ṣe rẹ́rìn-ín músẹ́ sí mi kí o sọ pé ""bàbá-bàbá."" Wò ẹ́!" "Àṣé o lè ní fẹ̀ẹ́ bàbá rẹ? O ò sì ní pé""màmá-mà-mà-mamàmá""! Ódáa Tinú, bàbá rẹ dà bayìí?" Bàbá tó o fẹ́ràn púpọ̀? Sọfún mi? O ò mọ̀? Ibè lo wà! Ó dáa Tinú, màá sọfún ẹ. Bàbá rẹti jáde bí ó ti ń ṣe.
Tí ó ń fi wá sílẹ̀. Ìyẹn ńkọ́? O fẹ́ẹbẹ́ẹ̀? Làbákẹ́ rí nǹkan tó jọ àyípadà nínú ìwòojú ọmọ rè tí ò mọ̀kan yìí. Tinú ti pa ẹnu rẹ̀ dé bayìí. Kò rẹ́rìn-ín músẹ́ mọ́, tí kò sì sọ̀rọ̀ wẹ́rẹ́wẹ́rẹ́ mọ́.
en: "Can you crawl to him and smile as you now smile at me and say, ""Papa-Papa."" Look at you!" "So you like your Papa? And you won't say ""Mama-Ma-ma-ma-Mama! O.K. Tinu, where is your Papa now?" The Papa you seem to like so much? Tell me. You don't know? There you are! Alright Tinu,listen. I'll tell you. Your Papa has gone out - as usual.

Leaving us alone. What about that? You like it? Labake saw what seemed to be a change of expression on the innocent face of her daughter. Tinu had closed her mouth now. She was no longer smiling. No longer babbling

passages.title: MENYO passage 353
paragraphs: Tinú, sọfún bàbá rẹ nígbà náà pé kó máa dúró nílé kí ó sì máa ṣètọ́jú gbogbo wa láti ìsinsìnyí lọ. Nísinsìnyìí tí inú rẹ kò dùn sí ibí i tèmi yìí. Ní kí bàbá rẹ sọ orúkọ obìnrin tó wà níta yẹn tí ó ń jí bàbá rẹ mọ́ wa lọ́wọ́.
A fẹ́ mọ orúko rẹ̀, kí a sì pariwo rẹ̀ fáráyé gbọ́. Sọfún bàbá rẹ kí ó má jẹ́ kí obìnrin yẹn tàn-án. Owó rẹ̀ nìkan ló ń tẹ̀lé.
en: Tinu, tell your Papa then to stay more at home and take care of all of us from now on. Now that you are unhappy about it just like me. Ask Papa to tell you the name of that woman outside who is stealing him from us.
We want to know her name and shout it for the whole world to hear. Tell your Papa not to be deceived by that woman outside. She's only after his money.

passages.title: MENYO passage 354
paragraphs: """Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni.......bẹ́ẹ̀ ni. Mo mọ̀ pé ìwọ ni Àlàmú ........ṣùgbọ́n.......ṣùgbọ́n.""" """Dákun Làbákẹ́. Bá mi ti ọkọ̀ yìí. Tí díẹ̀ ni." Ó nílò títì, bíbẹ́ẹ̀ kò ní dáhùn.
Ó ṣè è dákú nísinsìnyìí ni. Bóyá nǹkankan ti ń ṣe kọ́ńtáàti rẹ̀. Ó sì lè jẹ́ bátììrì. Àlàmú fẹyín, ló bá bú sí ẹ̀rín.
en: """Yes yes. I know it's you Alamu... But...But.""" Come on Labake. Help give the car a push. A little push. It needs some pushing else it won't start.
Just now it stopped. Maybe something wrong with its contact set. Or it may be the battery. Alamu's teeth flashed and he filled with laughter.

passages.title: MENYO passage 355
paragraphs: Óyá gbìyànjú ẹ̀. "Títì díẹ̀.""" Làbákẹ́ kò mira

"""Ọkọ̀ ta lèyí Àlàmú?,"" óbéèrè pẹ̀lú ìrújú pátápátá." """Ọkọ̀ wa. Ọkọ̀ tuntun wa Làbákẹ́,"" Àlàmú dáhùn. ""Mi ò báti jẹ́ kí o mọ̀ tẹ́lẹ̀. Ṣùgbọ́n kọ́kọ́ bá mi t.............""" """Ọkọ̀ tuntun!"" Làbákẹ́ jágbe mọ́ ọn, ""Ìwọ pe èyí ní ọkọtuntun? Kí ló ṣe ọkọ̀ pijó 504 rẹ tí o wà jáde láàárọ̀ yìí Àlàmú?."""
en: Now try it. "A little push.""" Labake did not move.

Whose car is this Alamu?' she asked, utterly perplexed. """Our car. Our new car Labake"" replied Alamu, ""I should have let you know earlier. But first, do give ...""" """New car!"" Labake shouted back, ""Do you call this a new car? What happened to your Peugeot 504 which you drove out in the morning Alamu?"""

passages.title: MENYO passage 356
paragraphs: Kí ló ti yára ṣe ọkọ̀ láàárín ásìkò tí Àlàmú kúrò nílé láàárọ̀ àti ọ̀sán yìí? """Nísinsìnyí Àlàmú,"" Làbákẹ́ tẹ̀síwájú, ""Níbo ni ọkọ̀ náà wà, ṣé lọ́dọ̀ mẹkáníìkì?""" """Ẹẹnn. Rárá. Bẹ́ẹ̀ kọ́. Ẹẹn. ṣo rí i. Ibo ni a ti máa rí adúrú owó yẹn láti tún un ṣe?, lo yẹ kí o béère."

"Fún ìdí èyí, mo........mo......tà áláti ra.....ra eléyìí.""" """Dúró ná, Àlàmú ,"" Làbákẹ́ kò gba etí rẹ̀ gbọ́, ""Kí ni mo gbọ́ tó o wí yẹn?" Pé o ta ọkọ̀ pijó 504 láti ra ọkọ̀ ìjàpá bítù tó ti relé yìí?
en: What then could have gone wrong with the car between the time Alamu left the house in the morning and this afternoon? """And now Alamu, Labake pressed on, ""Where is the car? Still with the mechanic?""" """Well. No. Not exactly. Well. You see. The question is, where shall we get all that money to repair it, Labake?"

"So.. So.. I. sold it to purchase. to purchase this one.""" """Beg your pardon Alamu,"" Labake could not believe her ears, ""What is it that you have just said?" you have sold a Peugeot 504 saloon car to purchase this rickety Volkswagen Beetle?

passages.title: MENYO passage 357
paragraphs: Ní òwúrọ̀ ọjọ́ kejì, ẹjọ́ àwọn alásọbótò àdúgbò dún sí etí rẹ̀bí ó ṣe rí wọn tí wọ́n ń kọjá níwájú géètì ilé wọn. Kò sí àní-àní, wọ́n mọ̀ọ́mọ̀ sọ ọ́ ni. Ọ́n ní ìmọ̀ràn díẹ̀ tí kò bèrè fún fún un. Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ ìtanijí mìí ràn fún un nípa ọkọ rẹ̀. Àti àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ ìyánu díẹ̀, láti fi dá wọn mọ̀ pẹ̀lú ìbànújẹ́ rẹ̀yìí, àti ọ̀rọ̀ àdúrà gan an pàápàá. Wọ́n kò wò ó lójú tààrà láti sọ ọ́.

Wọ́n kàn ń kọjá lo ni - wọ́n díbọ́n bí ìgbà tí wọ́n bá ń lọ ibìkan! - Wọn kò tiẹ̀ gbìyàn jú àtikí i. Ohun tí wọ́n kàn ń ṣe ni títú kẹ̀kẹ́ ọ̀rọ̀ ohun tí wọ́n ní lọ́kàn - láì sọ pàtó, wọ́n á kọ́jú sí òfurufú láti sọ ọ́. Ṣùgbọ́n á já geere fún àwọn tó létí láti gbọ́ ọ.
en: In the morning of the following day, the careless talk of the neighbours flickered into her ears, as she caught them walking past the gate of their house no doubt intentionally. They had a few words of unsolicited advice for her. Few other hints for her about her husband. And a few exclamations, to identify themselves with her present sorrow, even words of supplication. They did not face her directly to say it.

They just walked past - pretending to be going somewhere! - They did not even venture to greet her. All they did was mumble out what they had in mind - indirectly, facing the empty air to say it. But loud enough for those who had ears to hear.

passages.title: MENYO passage 358
paragraphs: "Wọn á mú un rẹ́rìn-ín lójú mọmọ, wọn á mú un rẹ́rìn-ín lọ́gànjọ́ òru.""" """A kò lè sùn lóru. Gbogbo rẹ̀ ni à ń gbọ́. Aruwo rẹ̀ ń dún sí wa létí." "Ẹ̀rín... Ẹ̀rín... Ẹ̀rín... Ìṣọ́ra ní láti wà, bíbẹ́ẹ̀ kọ́!..."""

"""Àánú. Àwa ò ní nǹkan mìí rànbí kò ṣe àánú.. Àánú fún ìwọ obìnrin tí ò ń bá a gbé. Ro bí wàhálà ṣe ń wọnú ayé rẹ... Àánu...""" Ó ní láti se nǹkan si i. Ni kíákíá si ni pẹ̀lú. O ní láti jáde síta kí o wá ìrànlọ́wọ́. Ẹ̀ ń ti ara yín mọ́ ilé fún gbogbo ọjọ́! Kò síì ṣòro tó níyanjú lọ́ nà yẹn! """Ọlọ́run á ràn yín lọ́wọ́. Ọlọ́run á ṣí ojú yín àti etí yín. Ẹ ẹ́ lè ríran rí ara yín bí ẹ ṣe wàyìí. Àwa wí!"""
en: "They make him laugh in the day time. They make him laugh at midnight.""" """We couldn't sleep during the night. We heard it all. Its noise came ringing in our ears." Laughter... Laughter... Laughter... Care must be taken or else..

"""Pity. We have nothing but pity... Pity for you woman living with him. Imagines trouble entering your life. At the prime of your life... Pity...""" """You just must do something about it. And quickly too. You have to get out and look for help. You lock yourselves up all day! No problem is solved that way!""" """May God help you. May God open your eyes and your ears. May you see yourselves as you are in reality. We have spoken!"""

passages.title: MENYO passage 359
paragraphs: Gbogbo rẹ̀ ni àwọn aládùúgbò rẹ̀ ti fẹsẹ̀ múlẹ̀ fún un yìí. Ẹ̀rí mìí ràn wo ni ó tún nílò? Ilé ìwòsàn tí wọ́n ti ń ṣètọ́ jú àwọn alárùn ọpọlọ kán wà ní òpin ìlú - ní ìdojúkọ ìlà-oòrùn - ilé ọlọ́dà funfun lórí òkè. Ilé ìwòsàn náà jọ àwọn ilé alákọ̀ọ́kànrun ìtòsí rẹ̀.

Àwọn àlejò ìlú máa ń wo apá ibẹ̀ ní ìwò àwò-má-leèlọ. Ó rẹ wà láti wò - àwòrán àlàáfíà tí ó ṣe ojú jẹ́jẹ́ ni, bí ènìyàn bá ń wò ó láti ọ̀nà jíjìn. Apá ibẹ̀ nínú ìlú ni Làbákẹ́ ṣe àbẹ̀wò sí nígbà tó kọ́kọ́ dé láti ìlú òyìnbó.
en: All it had now been corroborated by the neighbours. What more evidence did she need? There was a Mental Hospital on the outskirts of the city - towards the eastern horizon - a solitary white-washed building on top of the hill. Just a little way off this building was the cluster of imposing skyscrapers.

Visitors to the city often found themselves gazing instinctively towards that section of the city. It was beautiful to look at - serene and romantic, a picture of peace and calm to the eyes, viewed from a distance. That area of town was one of the few places Labake visited when she first arrived in the country from England.

passages.title: MENYO passage 360
paragraphs: Àlàmú yẹra fún oníṣirò àti alábojútó ilé ìfowópamọ́sí náà. Wọ́n mọra dáadáa, ṣùgbọ́n kò sí lára Àlàmú láti kí ènìyàn lásìkò yìí. Wọ́n lè máa fìyẹn bí í ní àwọn ìbéèrè oríṣìírísìí, fún àpẹẹrẹ iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ àti ìlọsíwájú tuntun níbẹ̀. Kò sì ní fẹ́dáhùn sí irú àwọn ìbéèrè wọ̀nyí. Ó kàn wásí ilé ifowópamọ́ sí yìí fún òwò kékeré ni, á sì fẹ́ jáde ní kíákíá bí ó bá ṣe rọrùn sí.

Ojú rẹ̀ lọ sí ọ̀dọ̀ olùtọ́jú owó kìíní, tí ó ní òkìtì owótúntún ńlá níwájú rẹ̀. Pẹ̀lú orí ìka ọwọ́ ni olùtọ́jú owó náà fi ń ṣí i láwẹ́láwẹ́ tí ó sì ń kà á síra rẹ̀ tí ó sì ju orí tẹ̀lé kíkà rẹ̀ yìí láti fìdí kíkà rẹ̀ yìí múlẹ̀. Òkìtì owó tó wà níwájú rẹ̀ yìí lè tó ẹgbẹẹgbẹ̀rún náírà. Bóyá ogún ọ̀kẹ́ tàbí ogójì ọ̀kẹ́.
en: Alamu avoided the Accountant and the Manager. He was quite familiar with them, but this time around, he was in no mood to exchange pleasantries. They might in the process, start asking him questions about this, about that... questions, for instance, about his place of work and the latest development there. These are questions he would not want to answer. He was in the bank only for a slight business, and would want to get out of the place as quickly as he could make it.

His attention was directed to the cashier current, who had in front of him a huge pile of new currency notes. With the tip of his finger, this cashier flipped expertly through the bundles counting to himself, and shaking his head all along - to attest to the correctness of his arithmetic. The pile of notes in front of the cashier might be running to several thousands of naira. Perhaps four hundred thousand or even eight hundred thousand.

passages.title: MENYO passage 361
paragraphs: Fún ìgbà pípẹ́, ọ̀gá á dùbúlẹ̀ láìlérò bí oníwárápá. Sènábù ṣàlàyé fún màmá pẹ̀lú ọkàn mímó àìlẹ́bí àti omijé lójú rẹ̀. Làbákẹ́...... Làbákẹ́......orúkọ tí a fi ń ṣé pè orúkọ! Ó kan lẹ́nu, bí ewúro, ó ń lọ́ ahọ́n, ó ń kó ẹnu ènìyàn bí i ọbẹ̀ ilá tí ò níyọ̀.
Ìyá Àlàmú dá sọ̀ pẹ̀lú ìrira, ó sì tutọ́ orúkọ ìyàwó ọmọ rẹ̀ kíkorò jáde. Bí ó ṣe kórira orúko náà báyìí àti ẹni tí ó ń jẹ́ orúkọ náà. Óhàn gbangba pé màmá àti Làbákẹ́ kì í ṣe ọ̀rẹ́ gidi rárá.
en: And for a long time, master would lic down unconscious - like an epileptic victim. Zenabu gave the account to Mama innocently and with tears welling up in her eyes. Labake.... Labake.... What a terrible name for anybody to called by! It tasted sour in the mouth, like bitter leaf, twisting the tongue, soiling the mouth like the stickly mess of saltless okro soup.

Alamu's mother mused in disgust and spat out the bitter-leaf name of her son's wife. How very much she now hated that name and the person who bore it. Mama and Labake were clearly not the best of friend.

passages.title: MENYO passage 362
paragraphs: Màmá sì ni ìyáfún ọkọ Làbákẹ́ àtàtà... nítorí náà, ó le fún ìkankan nínú wọn láti dojú ìjà kọ ẹnìkejì. Bí wọn kò bá fẹ́ràn ara wọn, dájú dájú wọ́n gbọ́dọ̀ máa dẹ ara wọn! Ṣùgbọ́n gbogbo ìgbà ni Àlàmú ń ṣe ojúṣe rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí onídàájọ́.

Ó mọ bí ó ṣe máa tẹ́ màmá lọ́rùn dáadáa. Ó sì mọ bí ó ṣe máa tẹ́ olólùfẹ́ rẹ̀ lọ́rùn. Èyí kò túmò sí pé ó ti ṣa ṣeyọrí nínú títẹ́ àwọn méjèèjì lọ́rụ̀n ní pípé. "Fún àpẹẹrẹ, àwọn àsìkò kán wà tíì yá rẹ̀ ní kí ó yéé máa sọ""èmi àti ìyàwó mi....èmi àti ìyàwó mi"" ní gbogbo ìgbà ní ìṣojú wọn."
en: And Mama was the mother of Labake's loving husband... so it had been difficult for anyone of them to launch a direct attack. If they did not like each other surely they must be at each other's throat! But, all along, Alamu had been living up to expectation in his role as an umpire.

He very well knew how to satisfy Mama. He knew the way to please his darling. That was not to say, however, that he had succeeded in striking a perfect balance. For instance, there had been times when his mother would ask him to stop saying. 'my wife and I... my wife and I', all of the time in her presence.

passages.title: MENYO passage 363
paragraphs: Ṣùgbọ́n nísinsìnyí, kò jọ wí pé yóò ṣeésẹ láti dín asọ̀ màmá kù. Wọ́n ti bẹ̀rẹ̀ si í sọ̀rọ̀ pẹ̀lú ìbínú... """Nísinsìnyí, Àlàmú ọmọ òpònú yìí, á wá mọ nǹkan ti mo ti ń sọlá tii ye ọjọ́ yìí,"" Ó ń so lọ́kàn ara rẹ̀"

"""Èmi àtìyàwó mi....èmi àtìyàwó mi "" Òpònú ọmọ!" Á kọ́ bí yóò ti ṣe mọ rírì ọ̀rọ̀ mi nísinsìnyí tí ó ti ń kó sí páńpẹ́ rẹ̀. Ọlọ́run mọ̀ pé ó ti ń kó ipa rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìyá tòótọ́, tí ó ń gba ásìkò láti ṣí etí ọmọ rẹ̀ sí òótọ́ ayé.
en: But now, it did not seem there was going to be any way of curtailing Mama's outburst. She'd started fuming... ' Now this follish boy, Alamu, would know what I'd been talking about ever since's she told herself,

"""My wife and I.... My wife and I"" Foolish boy," he would learn to appreciate my stand now that he is falling into her trap'. God knew she'd been playing her part like a true mother, taking time to open her son's ears to the realities of life.

passages.title: MENYO passage 364
paragraphs: Ó mọ̀ pé obìnrin tún lè mú ìparun wábí i paramọ́lẹ̀. "Ó ti sọ ọ́ fún un rí pé, ""tọ́jú àṣírí rẹ fún ara rẹ Àlàmú. Má sọ gbogbo rẹ̀ fún ìyàwó rẹ, bí obìnrin bá ti ní òye gbogbo àṣírí rẹ, ó lè fà ọ́ lé àwọn ọ̀tá lọ́wọ́....." Bí ọwọ́ bá sì bà ọ́ Àlàmú, á yọ gèlè orí rẹ̀, á fa irun orí ara rẹ̀, á fò sókè á sì sunkún kíkan kíkan fún ìfẹ́ ńlá tí ó nífún ọ!
"Àlàmú, la etí rẹ dáadáa kí o gbọ́ mi...""" Àmọ́, ṣé Àlàmú gbọ́? Ṣé ó gbọ́ rí? Àbájáde kíkọ etí dídi sí ohùn ọgbọ́n àti ìrírí rè é.
en: She knew a woman could at the same time be as destructive as a rattlesnake... 'Keep your secrets to yourself Alamu. Don't tell it all to your wife', she'd once told him, 'a woman in the knowledge of all your secrets could eventually hand you over to your enemies.... And when you are seized, Alamu, she would remove her head-tie, pull at the hair on her head, jump up and weep aloud for the great love she had for you!
Alamu open your ears properly and listen to me...' But, did Alamu listen? Did he ever listen? Here was the result of closing ears to the voice of wisdom and experience.

passages.title: MENYO passage 365
paragraphs: Yàtọ̀ sí ti ìkíni àsìkò àti ìbániṣọ̀rọ̀ orí ahọ́n, Làbákẹ́ náà kò kọjá ààyè rẹ̀. """Onídàájọ́"" náà kò ráyè ṣọ́ wọn bí i ti tẹ́lẹ̀." Ìṣòro tó bá a lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ tó fún un.

Fún ìdí èyí, kò ní ààyè láti wo ìran náà mọ́. Ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbákúgbàá àti àṣì gbá ni wọ́n ń gbá pẹ̀lú ìkúùkù abẹ́nú tó rú òfin eré. Gbogbo bí Làbákẹ́ ṣe ń siṣẹ́ ilé, màmá ń fi ìwò ìyọnu lé e ká, wọ ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀, wọ balùwẹ̀, wọ ilé ìdáná, àti parí parí ẹ̀, lọ sínú yàrá rẹ̀, níbi tí wíwò màmá dè é mọ́!
en: With the exception of the period-of-the-day casual greetings and some occasional tip-of-the-tongue remarks to Mama. Umpire' had not been as vigilant as before. His own present problem was enough for him.

He, therefore, had no time to watch the game anymore. There were rough kicks and foul play - a lot of blows below the belt! As Labake went about the household business, Mama's menacing gaze chased her all about - into, the toilet, into the bedroom, into the kitchen and finally into her bedroom, where Mama's gaze seemed to have pinned her down!

passages.title: MENYO passage 366
paragraphs: Àlàmú ti jáde, àsìkò yìí ni ó dára láti sọ̀rọ̀ sí ohun èèlò ìparun tó wà nílé. Á dá sẹ̀ríà fún un - lọ́nà tirẹ̀. Kò ní dạ́kẹ́ máa wò kí ayé Àlàmú bàjẹ́ poo láti ọwọ́ aṣojú àwọn ọ̀tá tí ò farahàn yìí.
"""Wò mí!,"" Màmá sọ̀rọ̀ lójijì, ""wò mí dáadáa Làbákẹ́! Àṣírí ti tú!""" """Kíni yẹn, màmá?""" """Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni. Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni, Làbákẹ́....ó ti tú - àṣírí."
en: Alamu had gone out, this was the right time to talk straight to the mischievous instrument of destruction at home. She would deal with her herself - her own way. She was no longer going to keep quiet and watch Alamu's wife destroyed steadily by this agent of the invisible enemies.
'Look at me'! Mama blared out, 'Look at me properly Labake! The cat been let out of the bag!' 'What, Mama?' 'Yes. Yes, Labake. It has been let out of the bag - the cat.

passages.title: MENYO passage 367
paragraphs: """Ipárẹ ti pin láti àkókò yìí lọ""!" """Màmá tani? Èmi? Kí leléyìí?""" """O mọ gbogbo rẹ̀ Làbákẹ́! Yéé díbọ́n! Ìyẹ́ rẹ ti re báyìí!"

Àlàmú ni ọmọ mi kan ṣoṣo - bí o ò bá sì mọ̀ - kò sí ẹnikẹ́ni tó lè gbà á lọ́wọ́ mi. Agbára rẹ ti tán bá yìí. Màmá ti wá paradà, kì í ṣe ènìyàn lásán mọ́. Iṣan ńlá ńlá farahàn lójú rẹ̀, ó sì jẹ́ kí ó jọ ẹlẹ́mìí èṣù, bí i ti òkú tó fẹ́ gbẹ̀san lójijì.
en: 'You have become powerless from this moment onward'! 'Who Mama? Me? What is this?' 'You know it all Labake! Stop pretending! Your wings have been cut this moment!

Alamu is my only child - maybe you don't know - and nobody can take him from me. Your power is clipped from now on'. Mama had become transformed, she was no longer an ordinary human being. Great tissue - thorns crawled out of the face of a ghost of vengeance suddenly let loose.

passages.title: MENYO passage 368
paragraphs: Ìwo ò lè wojú mi mọ́! Wo bí ọkàn ẹlẹ́ṣẹ̀ ṣè ń hùwà! Mo ní agbára rẹ ti tán! Àgbàra àwọn tí ò ń jíṣẹ́ fún náà ti pin, ní ìṣẹ́jú yìí.
Àwọn bàbá-ńlá mi ò sùn lọ́run. Mo dúpẹ́ lọ́wọ́ wọn. Mo dúpẹ́ lọ́wọ́ wọn. Mo dúpẹ́ lọ́wọ́ àwọn bàbá-ńlá mi, wọ́n lajú sílẹ̀. Ní báyìí, wọ́n sì ti gbèjà mi. Fún ìdí èyí, ọmọ mi á rí ìgbàlà.
en: You no longer can look at my face! See how a guilty mind behaves! I say your power is clipped! The powers of those you are running errands for have also ended, this very minute.
My fore-fathers have not slept in heaven. I thank them. I thank them. I thank my fore-fathers, they are wide awake. And now they have intervened. So my son will be saved.'

passages.title: MENYO passage 369
paragraphs: "Òrun gan-an ń bínú si ọ fún nǹkan tí ò ń ṣe láti pa ayọ̀ mi. Nǹkankan ṣoṣo tó jẹ́ n máa gbáyé.""" """Èmi kọ́! Mi ò lè pa ayọ̀ yín láéláé Màmá.""" """Ṣùgbọ́n o lè pa álára - àbí bẹ́ẹ̀ kọ́?"

Màá já ara mi sí hòòhò níwájú ẹ báyìí, màá sì fi eyín mi ya ẹ́ sí wẹ́wẹ́! Dúró, jẹ́ n já ara mi sí hòòhò! """Màmá tú gèlè rẹ̀, ó bọ́ bùbá rẹ̀, ó bọ́ bàtà, ó sì ju ìró rẹ̀ sílẹ̀! Ó dúró díẹ̀ -ó ń mí lókè lókè...'"
en: Heaven itself is angry with you for what you are doing to kill my joy. The only thing i live for this world.' 'Not me! I can't ever kill your joy Mama.' 'But you can maim my joy - not so?

I'll strip myself naked before you now and tear you to pieces with my teeth! Wait, let me strip myself naked! Mama removed her head tie, removed her buba, took off her slippers, and threw down her wrapper! She held on for a while - breathing heavily....

passages.title: MENYO passage 370
paragraphs: Màmá fẹ́ fìdí ọ̀rọ̀ rẹ̀ gúnlẹ̀ dáadáa kí ó tó di wí pé á já ara rẹ̀ sí hòòhò. Bí ó máa nílò, Lẹ́yìn náà láti já ara rẹ̀ sí ìhòòhò, á ṣe é. """Wò mí dáadáa, Làbákẹ́... ojú ti ń tì ọ́ báyìí, wo ẹ̀bi ní gbogbo ara ẹ. Wòó..."

Àlàmú ò níí kú. Á borí gbogbo ìṣòro náà. "Lórúkọ àwọn bàbá mi tí ò sùn lọ́run.""" """Màmá... Màmá...ìṣòro wo? Ìṣòro Àlàmú ...ìṣòro rẹ̀ bó ti wù kí ó tó jẹ́ ìṣòro tèmi náà...hooo Màmá...... Báwo lẹ ṣe lè......."""
en: Mama wanted to drive home her point properly before she would strip herself naked. If it would be necessary, thereafter, to strip stark naked, she would do it. """Look at me properly, Labake.... now you are ashamed and see the guilt all over you. Look..."

Alamu will not die, he will get over the problem. In the name of my fathers whose eyes never close in heaven. """""Mama..... Mama.... What problem? Alamu's problem... His problem, however heavy is my problem too... Oh Mama... How can you..."
